<!-- source: docs/controllers.md -->

# MIDI controllers & embedding

open-audiovisual models MIDI controllers as data: one JSON file per device, with the
faceplate layout, every control's exact MIDI message, LED feedback, how to recognise its
port, and the document each number came from. The same file drives an on-screen controller
you can play, follows the real device when you plug it in, and can be dropped into any web
page. Every device is on the [controllers page](https://openaudiovisual.com/controllers/).

## Play one in a page

```html
<script type="module" src="https://openaudiovisual.com/packages/midi/element.js"></script>
<oav-controller profile="akai-lpd8" readout></oav-controller>
```

That is the whole integration. The element works without Web MIDI (Safari, iPad): it plays
and fires events; only hardware and MIDI out report that they are unavailable. It never asks
for MIDI permission unless you turn on `hardware`, `midi-out` or learn. Safari has none because WebKit has not implemented it ([bug 107250](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=107250), still open).

| Attribute | What it does |
|---|---|
| `profile` | which device: an id, a short name, or a URL to your own profile JSON |
| `layout` | `auto`, `face` (as it looks) or `stack` (re-gridded for a phone held upright) |
| `hardware` | `on`, or `ask` for a button: the real device moves the on-screen one |
| `midi-out` | a port name (`IAC`, `loopMIDI`), `/regex/`, or `ask`: what you play is sent there |
| `channel` | 1–16, when your unit is set to another channel |
| `picker`, `readout`, `learn`, `follow` | device picker, last-message line, learn button, show whatever known device you plug in |

## Listen to it

```js
const el = document.querySelector('oav-controller');
el.addEventListener('control', (e) => {
  const { id, value, signal, message, source } = e.detail;
  // 'k1'  0..1  'midi/lpd8/k1'  { type: 'cc', ch: 1, cc: 70, value: 53 }  'ui' | 'hardware'
});
await el.ready;
el.set('k1', 0.5);           // move a control as a hand would
el.ingest([0xb0, 70, 64]);   // MIDI from anywhere: the faceplate follows
```

Other events: `noteon`, `noteoff`, `connect`, `disconnect`, `status`, `profilechange`,
`ready`, `error`. All bubble and cross the shadow root. Every field of every payload is in
[packages/midi/README.md](../packages/midi/README.md).

## Without the element

```js
import { createController } from 'https://openaudiovisual.com/packages/midi/index.js';

const ctl = createController('akai-lpd8', { signals });   // signals: publish into a show
ctl.mount(document.querySelector('#pads'));                // optional
ctl.on('control', (e) => console.log(e.signal, e.value));
```

Inside a show, do not read `midi/lpd8/k1` in `update()`: route it to a param with
`controllerRoutes(profile, { k1: 'hue' })` (rule 1 in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md)).
Example 09 does this for six devices at once.

## In an iframe

For places that only take an iframe:

```html
<iframe src="https://openaudiovisual.com/embed/controller/?profile=akai-lpd8&readout&frame=pads"
        width="720" height="220" style="border:0" allow="midi" title="AKAI LPD8"></iframe>
```

The frame posts `{ source: 'openav', type, frame, detail }` to its parent for every event,
and accepts `{ target: 'openav', type: 'set' | 'ingest' | 'press' | 'release' | 'reset' |
'profile' | 'layout' | 'get', … }`. Add `origin=https://your.site` to talk to your page only.

## Play your DAW with it

1. macOS: Audio MIDI Setup → Window → Show MIDI Studio → IAC Driver → “Device is online”.
   Windows 11: the built-in Windows MIDI Services (released 2026-02-17, rolled out in stages to 24H2 and 25H2) share MIDI ports between apps and include a loopback, and Microsoft's announcement says web pages using Web MIDI can use it ([Windows blog](https://blogs.windows.com/windowsexperience/2026/02/17/making-music-with-midi-just-got-a-real-boost-in-windows-11/)). We have not tested it with open-audiovisual. Older Windows: install loopMIDI and add a port; that still works.
2. `<oav-controller profile="akai-lpd8" midi-out="IAC">` (on Windows, give the name of the port you made or the one Windows shows).
3. In Ableton Live, turn on Track and Remote for that input; in TouchDesigner, a MIDI In CHOP
   on it; in Resolume, Preferences → MIDI.

Hands on the screen are sent; your real hardware is not forwarded (the DAW already hears it).
The engine never listens to IAC inputs, and the element mutes an input named like its
output, so nothing loops.

## Telemetry

So the project can see where its controllers and shows end up, the packages send **one anonymous hit per page load** to Google Analytics 4 (the openaudiovisual.com property, `G-1YG2JHK2WT`):

| event | when | params |
|---|---|---|
| `oav_embed_load` | an `<oav-controller>`, `createController()` or the iframe starts | `oav_kind` (element · headless · iframe), `oav_profile`, `oav_host`, `oav_version` |
| `oav_hardware_connect` | a real controller is plugged in and matched | `oav_kind`, `oav_profile`, `oav_host`, `oav_version` |
| `oav_show_start` | `createShow()` starts | `oav_kind` (show), `oav_host`, `oav_version` |

`oav_host` is the **origin** of the page it runs on (for the iframe, the page that holds it), never the path, query or title. Nothing anyone plays is sent, no cookies are set, and the client id is random for every page load, so visitors can't be followed. No gtag.js is loaded: a page with its own Google Analytics keeps its dataLayer untouched. Nothing is sent from localhost, LAN addresses, `file://` or openaudiovisual.com itself, or when the browser sends Do Not Track / Global Privacy Control.

Turn it off: `<oav-controller telemetry="off">` · `createController(p, { telemetry: false })` · `createShow({ telemetry: false })` · the iframe's `?telemetry=0` · or `globalThis.OPENAV_TELEMETRY = false` before anything loads. Source: `packages/midi/telemetry.js`.

## Add a controller

1. Copy the closest file in `packages/midi/profiles/`, or a generic layout.
2. Write each control's type and message from the manual's MIDI implementation chart.
3. Cite every source; mark anything unconfirmed `"verified": false` with a note.
4. `validateProfile(profile)` lists every problem; `npm test` checks every shipped profile.
5. Try it with `<oav-controller profile="./my-device.json">`, then register it in
   `profiles/index.js` and open a pull request.

No manual: choose a generic layout, press Learn, move your controls in order, and keep
`controller.exportMapping()` as the start of a profile.

---

<!-- source: docs/p5.md -->

# p5.js in one line

Any p5.js sketch (OpenProcessing, the p5 editor, your own page) can be played from a MIDI controller, from a
controller drawn on screen, or from a phone, by adding one line at the top:

```js
document.head.prepend(Object.assign(document.createElement('script'), { src: 'https://openaudiovisual.com/p5/oav-p5.js' }));
```

On OpenProcessing you can instead paste the URL into Sketch → Libraries → **+** (custom library). Both work in p5 1.x
and 2.x global mode, and nothing has to be called in `setup()`.
A sketch that carries this line, playable right now: [example 15](https://openaudiovisual.com/examples/15-p5-one-line/).

## Read it like the mouse

```js
function draw() {
  background(knob1 * 255);                 // knob 1, 0..1, like mouseX
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 50 + knob2 * 300);
}

function notePressed(note, velocity) {     // like keyPressed(): any key, or a pad
  circle(random(width), random(height), velocity * 100);
}
```

| read | value |
|---|---|
| `knob1` … `knob8`, `knob(n)` | 0..1, numbered as printed on the controller |
| `fader1` … `fader8`, `fader(n)` | 0..1 |
| `pad1` … `pad16`, `pad(n)` | the velocity while the pad is held, 0 when released |
| `note`, `velocity` | the last key (MIDI number) and how hard (0..1) |
| `noteIsPressed`, `noteIsDown(60)` | like `keyIsPressed` and `keyIsDown()` |

| define | called when |
|---|---|
| `notePressed(note, velocity)`, `noteReleased(note)` | a key goes down / up (a pad too, unless you define `padPressed`) |
| `knobMoved(n, value)`, `faderMoved(n, value)` | a knob or fader moves |
| `padPressed(n, velocity)`, `padReleased(n)` | a pad is hit / let go |

Knob 1 is knob 1 on whichever controller played it: the [controller profiles](controllers.md) say which MIDI message
each knob sends (MiniLab 3's knob 1 is CC 74, LPD8's is CC 70). On a controller OAV has no profile for, the first
knob you turn becomes `knob1`, the next `knob2`. A sketch that already has its own `note`, `velocity` or `knob1`
keeps it.

## Note names

Wherever a note number goes, a note name goes too (0.8):

```js
function draw() {
  if (noteIsDown('C4')) circle(width / 2, height / 2, 100);   // the same as noteIsDown(60)
}

function mousePressed() {
  midi.play('C#4', 0.8);                    // sends note 61, as a key would
}
```

| write | you get |
|---|---|
| `noteNumber('C4')` | `60`; a number comes back as it is, held to 0..127 |
| `noteName(61)` | `'C#4'`; `noteName(61, { flats: true })` is `'Db4'`, `noteName(61, { octave: false })` is `'C#'` |
| `noteFreq('A4')`, `noteFreq(69)` | `440` (Hz), for a sketch that makes its own sound; `noteFreq(69.5)` is a quarter tone up |
| `noteIsDown('C4')`, `midi.isDown('C4')`, `midi.play('C#4', 0.8)` | the same as with `60`, `61` |

A name is a letter A to G (either case), an optional `#` or `b` (`♯` and `♭` too), and the octave number: `C4`, `c#4`,
`Db3`, `F♯2`, `C-1` (0) up to `G9` (127). **C4 is 60**, the scientific pitch notation the course modules use; some software
(Ableton, Yamaha) calls 60 "C3", so a name copied from there is one octave off. These are also the names Strudel writes
(`c4 e4 g4`, `#` for sharp, `b` for flat). Anything else, such as `H4` or `C-2`, stops with a one-line card saying how to write it.
`notePressed(note, velocity)` still hands you the number: `noteName(note)` writes it back as a name.

## With OP Configurator

[OP Configurator 3000](https://github.com/msawired/OPC) (OPC, built into OpenProcessing) names a variable and its
range. With this line on the page the controller is wired to those variables in order, with no mapping step:

```js
OPC.slider('radius', 60, 10, 300);   // knob 1
OPC.slider('speed', 1, 0, 5, 0.1);   // knob 2
OPC.toggle('trails', true);          // pad 1 flips it
```

Knobs drive the sliders in the order they are declared, the faders continue after the knobs, and pads drive toggles
and buttons. OPC's panel moves with the knob, and `parameterChanged()` fires as usual. OpenProcessing's OPC panel can
also learn hardware by itself (its MIDI switch); once that mapping is seen working, hardware is left to it and this
line keeps wiring the on-screen controller and the phone, which OpenProcessing cannot see. Avoid OPC names that are
also p5 functions (`hue`, `fill`): p5 1.x clashes with them.

**One knob, one job.** If the sketch also reads `knob1` itself, knob 1 is the sketch's: the first OPC slider no longer
follows it (drag it on OPC's panel), the other knobs stay wired, and a hint says so once. The first line of the 🎹 panel
is the wiring, for example *knob1 → knob1 (sketch; radius by its slider) · knob2 → speed (OPC)*.

## The microphone

The same line reads the microphone, and the sketch reads it the same way: as variables.

```js
function draw() {
  background(230, 40, 10);
  fill(200 + bass * 160, 70, 100);                      // bass: the low end, 0..1
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 50 + micLevel * 300);   // micLevel: how loud, 0..1
}

function beatDetected(level) {                          // like keyPressed(): a beat just landed
  // flash, spawn, jump to the next scene
}
```

| read | value |
|---|---|
| `micLevel` | 0..1, how loud it sounds: the room's own noise is 0, talking is about 0.4–0.6, shouting is near 1 |
| `bass`, `mid`, `treble` | 0..1, the energy in 20–250 Hz, 250–2000 Hz and 2000–8000 Hz |
| `beat` | `true` for one frame per beat, like `mouseIsPressed` while a button is down |
| `micIsOn` | whether the microphone is running |
| `startMic()`, `stopMic()` | turn it on or off from code (they return a promise) |
| `micSensitivity(2)` | twice as sensitive; `micSensitivity()` returns the current value |

| write this function | when it is called |
|---|---|
| `beatDetected(level)` | a beat: a jump in loudness over what the room has been doing (level 0..1) |
| `kickDetected(level)`, `snareDetected(level)`, `hatDetected(level)` | a hit in the low, middle or high band (20–120 Hz, 150–800 Hz, 6–14 kHz) |

**It is off until the sketch asks.** Nothing is requested when the page loads. The first time the sketch reads
`micLevel`, `bass`, `mid`, `treble` or `beat`, or calls `startMic()`, the browser asks for the microphone; until the
answer arrives every value is `0`. A sketch that defines `beatDetected()` and reads nothing starts it on the first
click or key. In the 🎹 panel the **🎤** button turns it on and off by hand and shows the level, and it says so when
the browser blocked the microphone (click it again after allowing it from the address bar).

- **Click first, if the browser wants one.** Browsers keep audio quiet until the page has been clicked. This file
  asks as soon as `draw()` reads a value and starts the microphone again on the first click or key if the browser
  held it back, so no `userStartAudio()` is needed.
- **Next to p5.sound.** The analysis is [`@openav/audio`](packages.md) (an `AnalyserNode`), loaded from next to this
  file the first time it is needed, with its own `AudioContext`. `p5.sound` (`p5.AudioIn`, `p5.FFT`) can run on the same page; the two
  microphones do not share anything, and none of these names is a p5 or p5.sound name. It works in p5 1.x and 2.x global mode.
- **How loud is loud.** `micLevel` is a loudness in decibels, measured from the room: its bottom follows the room's own
  noise (it settles in a second or two, and rises at most 1.5 dB a second, so a voice never becomes the new silence), and
  −10 dBFS, shouting into a laptop, is 1. So `50 + micLevel * 300` visibly grows when someone talks. A quiet or far
  microphone: `micSensitivity(3)` (+9.5 dB on `micLevel`, ×3 on the bands, still capped at 1). The raw numbers are
  `OAVp5.mic.rms` (0..1), `OAVp5.mic.db` and `OAVp5.mic.floor` (the room, in dBFS).
  `OAVp5.mic.on('beat', fn)` is the same as defining `beatDetected`, and returns a function that stops it.
- **Your own names win.** A sketch that already has a `bass` or `mid` (a `let`, a function, a library) keeps it, and this
  file never starts the microphone for it.
- **Off switch.** `?mic=click` (or `window.OAV_P5 = { mic: 'click' }`) means only 🎤 and `startMic()` turn it on;
  `mic=off` means nothing can start it (the names stay `0`). `https` or `localhost` is required, as for any microphone page.
- A sketch with a microphone, ready to open: `p5/examples/mic/`.

## Sound: what is played is heard

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(windowWidth, windowHeight);
  startSound('piano');          // every key is heard: a keyboard, the 🎹 on screen, a phone
}
```

| call / read | value |
|---|---|
| `startSound(instrument)` | turn sound on (default `'piano'`), or switch instruments while it plays |
| `stopSound()` | turn it off |
| `soundIsOn` | whether notes are heard now |

The instruments are those of [`@openav/sound`](packages.md): `piano` (the Salamander grand; its 2 MB of samples load the
first time, and the electric piano plays meanwhile, or instead if they cannot load), `epiano`, `organ`, `strings`, `choir`,
`harp`, `marimba`, `vibraphone`, `xylophone`, `glockenspiel`, `music-box` and the `synth/…` presets. In the 🎹 panel,
**🔊** turns sound on and off and shows a picker with every instrument and the loading progress.

- **Off until asked.** Nothing loads before `startSound()` or 🔊; then `@openav/sound` from next to this file and Tone.js 15
  from jsDelivr (the option `tone=<url>` loads it from elsewhere).
- **The first click.** Browsers play audio only after the page has been clicked, and a key on a MIDI keyboard does not count.
  A sketch that calls `startSound()` in `setup()` is heard from the first click or key; until then the 🔊 on the 🎹 button is yellow.
- **Pads are drums.** Notes on MIDI channel 10 (MiniLab 3 and LPD8 pads, the General MIDI drum channel) play the drum kit,
  not the piano. The sustain pedal holds notes.
- **No code at all.** `?oav_sound=piano` on the page (any instrument id; on OpenProcessing `?sketch_oav_sound=piano`) makes any sketch heard
  from the first click; `sound=off` keeps it silent.
- A sketch that plays and draws, ready to open: `p5/examples/keys/`.

## Drum machine

```js
function setup() {
  startDrums('breakbeat', 110);   // a 16-step grid on screen; click a cell to change the beat
}

function kickDetected(level) {    // the microphone's own callback
  // swell, flash, spawn
}

function drumHit(lane, velocity) {   // every hit: 'kick', 'snare', 'hat' or 'clap'
}
```

| read | value |
|---|---|
| `drumsAreOn` | whether the machine is playing |
| `drumStep` | 0..15, the step that just played |
| `drumBar` | 1, 2, 3 …, counted from `startDrums()` |
| `drumBpm` | the tempo (the grid's slider changes it too) |
| `drumPhase` | 0..1, how far through the bar, smoothly, as heard: `rotate(drumPhase * TWO_PI)` turns once a bar |
| `beatPhase` | 0..1, how far through the beat (a quarter note): `1 - beatPhase` swells on each beat and shrinks to the next |
| `startDrums(pattern, bpm)`, `stopDrums()` | start (or change the pattern and tempo while it plays), stop |

| write this function | when it is called |
|---|---|
| `drumHit(lane, velocity)` | every hit, every drum (a line of rhythm's crash, ride or toms too) |
| `kickDetected(level)`, `snareDetected(level)`, `hatDetected(level)` | a kick; a snare, a clap or a rim; a hat (closed, open or pedal) |
| `beatDetected(level)` | a kick or a snare, once per step (and `beat` is true for a frame) |
| `rhythmChanged(src, how)` | the line changed: `startDrums()`, a click on a cell, a line typed, ↶ (0.7) |

**A microphone sketch moves over unchanged.** Each hit calls the same functions the microphone does, so a sketch written for
the microphone reacts to the machine as it is. Once a sketch has started the machine, defining `kickDetected()` no longer
opens the microphone on the first click (a sketch that reads `micLevel` still asks, and then both call it).

- **Patterns.** `'four on floor'`, `breakbeat`, `'half time'`, `latin`, `sparse`, your own
  `startDrums({ kick: 'x...x...x...x...', snare: '....x.......x...', hat: 'x.x.x.x.x.x.x.x.' })` (a lane left out is silent),
  or one line of rhythm (below).
- **The card.** The lanes are named in the page's language (大鼓 小鼓 鈸 拍手 in a Chinese browser), the bar it is in shows
  beside the tempo, and the step that sounds is a yellow column (13:1 against the dark card, readable on a projector).
- **Where the grid sits.** At the top centre: on OpenProcessing between the 🎹 and OPC's icon and clear of the console, and
  below the 🎹 panel while that is open. – folds it, × stops the machine, and **🥁** in the 🎹 panel starts and stops it with
  no code at all.
- **The kit.** [`@openav/drums`](packages.md)' synthesized kit (no samples), heard from the first click like sound; the
  callbacks run from the start either way.

**On time, however heavy the sketch.** The hits are handed to the kit ahead of time, on its audio clock: a heartbeat in a
Web Worker wakes every 25 ms and schedules what falls in the next 0.1 s at its exact time. Measured on the kit's own output
with a `draw()` that keeps the page busy 30 ms a frame, the kick-to-kick interval varies by 0.000 ms (0.5, which played each
hit in the frame it was due, varied by 15 ms). The callbacks still come in a frame: the one in which the hit is *heard* (its
time plus the output latency the browser reports), right before `draw()`, in the same order as before.

- **A tab in the background** keeps playing and counting: `drumBar` follows the clock on the wall and the cues fire, with one
  `barStarted` a bar. The hits and `stepStarted` are not told while nobody can see them, and nothing is told twice when the
  tab comes back, so a sketch that adds a particle per hit does not burst.
- **A `draw()` longer than 0.1 s** makes the machine look 0.3 s ahead from then on (🩺 says so); a click on a cell is then
  heard up to 0.3 s later.
- **A Bluetooth speaker** is late by 0.15–0.25 s; where the browser reports it the callbacks wait for it, and
  `?oav_drumlatency=200` (milliseconds) sets it by hand.
- **The safety net**: `?oav_drums=frame` (on OpenProcessing `?sketch_oav_drums=frame`) brings back 0.5's machine, moved by the
  frames.

### One line of rhythm

```js
function setup() {
  startDrums("bd*4, [~ sd]*2, hh*8", 110);   // a kick on every beat, a snare on 2 and 4, eight hats
}
```

Any text that is not a pattern name is a line of rhythm; names, grids and numbers work exactly as before. The line shows over
the grid, and the word that sounds lights up and fades.

| write | means | e.g. |
|---|---|---|
| a word | a drum: `bd` kick, `sd` snare, `hh` hat, `oh` open hat, `cp` clap, `rim`, `lt` `mt` `ht` toms, `cr` crash, `rd` ride, `cb` cowbell | `"bd sd bd sd"` |
| `~` | a rest | `"bd ~ sd ~"` |
| space | the words share the bar evenly | `"bd hh sd hh"` |
| `[ ]` | a group shares one place | `"bd [sd sd]"` |
| `*n` | n times in that place | `"hh*8"` |
| `,` | another line on top | `"bd*4, hh*8"` |
| `< >` | one per bar, in turn | `"<bd*4 [bd ~ bd ~]>"` |
| `(k,n)` | k hits spread over n steps | `"bd(3,8)"` |

The whole list is in [`@openav/pattern`](packages.md), loaded from next to `oav-p5.js` with the drums. Drums the grid has no
lane for (crash, ride, toms, open hat) get a row of their own; a hit off the sixteen steps (a triplet) is drawn where it falls
inside its step. **A mistake** in `startDrums("…")` shows a card in the page's language with the character it is at, why, and
how to fix it, and the machine plays `'four on floor'` meanwhile; `'x...x...'` on its own (one lane of the grid) says to put it
inside `{ kick: … }`.

**A line copied from strudel.cc** works too: `startDrums('s("bd*4, [~ sd]*2").fast(2)')` plays `[bd*4, [~ sd]*2]*2`.
`s("…")`, `sound("…")`, with `"`, `'` or `` ` `` quotes, several of them (`$: s(…)`) as layers, `.fast(n)` and `.slow(n)`;
`setcpm(110/4)` or `setcps(…)` sets the tempo when `startDrums()` is given none. `.bank("…")` is left out (OAV plays its own
synthesized kit) and anything else in the chain (`.jux(rev)`, `.every(…)`, `.gain(…)`) gets a card that says OAV does not do it
yet and points at **Open in Strudel**; the rest plays.

The way of writing one line of rhythm comes from TidalCycles / Strudel ([strudel.cc](https://strudel.cc)); OAV implements it
independently from their public documentation.

### The cells and the line edit each other

Since 0.7 the line over the grid is always there (a preset shows the line its grid is: `'four on floor'` is
`bd*4, [~ sd]*2, hh*8`) and both ways work:

- **Click a cell**: the line is rewritten the way a person would write it, and the machine plays the new line at once.
  Steady hits become `bd*4` / `hh*8`, one hit per group `[~ sd]*2`, a Euclidean rhythm `bd(3,8)` (with its rotation:
  `bd(3,8,2)` starts two steps later), anything else beat by beat: `bd [~ ~ ~ bd] bd*2 ~`. Lines are joined with `, `.
  When the line holds more than sixteen steps can (triplets, `< >`, `/2`, `?`, `bd:2`), the first click shows a card saying
  what would go, and the next click rewrites it.
- **Type in the line**: click it, change it; Enter, or a pause of 400 ms, plays it and the cells follow. A mistake marks the
  word in red, a card says what is wrong, and **the last line that worked keeps playing** (not `'four on floor'`). Escape
  drops what is not played yet. Typed keys never reach the sketch's `keyPressed()`.
- **↶** on the card (or ⌘Z / Ctrl+Z after touching the card) goes back one line; `OAVp5.drums.history` lists them.
- **Copy** puts `startDrums("…", 110)` on the clipboard, ready to paste into `setup()`.
- **Open in Strudel** opens the same line at strudel.cc in a new tab, as `s("…")` with `setcpm(bpm/4)` (one OAV bar is one
  Strudel cycle of four beats; strudel.cc's docs: `setcpm(bpm/bpc)`). `OAVp5.drums.strudelUrl` is the link.

```js
function rhythmChanged(src, how) {   // how: 'code' · 'cell' · 'type' · 'undo' · 'menu'
  line = src;                        // e.g. draw the line on the canvas, so a recording shows it
}
```

`OAVp5.drums.src` is the line that plays, `OAVp5.drums.edit("…")` plays a line as if typed, `OAVp5.drums.undo()` goes back. Keys that swap the rhythm, step back and open Strudel: `p5/examples/rhythm-lab/`.

### The rhythm on the canvas

The card is part of the page, not the canvas, so a recording never shows it. `drawRhythm()` draws the rhythm on the canvas:

```js
function draw() {
  background(0);
  drawRhythm(20, 20, 360, 90, 'grid');          // the sixteen steps, a playhead
  drawRhythm(20, 130, 300, 300, 'circle');      // a ring of 16 per drum, a hand turned by drumPhase
  drawRhythm(340, 130, 300, 300, 'spiral', { bars: 4, colors: { kick: '#ff7b54' } });   // the last 4 bars, wound outwards
}
```

`drawRhythm(x, y, w, h, style, options)`: `style` is `'grid'`, `'circle'` or `'spiral'`; a hit lights up the moment it is
heard (the clock `drumPhase` reads) and a triplet sits where it falls. Options: `colors` (`{ kick: '#f66', … }`, any p5 color),
`color` (one for all), `off` (the empty steps), `playhead` (a color, or `false`), `bg`, `bars` (spiral). Drawn inside
`push()` / `pop()` with p5's own shapes, in 2D and WEBGL, p5 1.x and 2.x; **in WEBGL (0, 0) is the middle of the canvas**:
`drawRhythm(-width / 2, -height / 2, width, height, 'circle')`. With no box it draws a strip along the bottom (`'grid'`) or a
square in the middle. A sketch with all three: `p5/examples/rhythm-visual/`.

## Timeline: bars and cues

The drum machine is also the clock: sixteen steps a bar, counted from `startDrums()`. Declare what happens at which bar:

```js
function setup() {
  startDrums('breakbeat', 110);
  cue(1, 'calm', 12);             // bar 1, and again every 12 bars
  cue(5, 'bloom', 12);
  cue(9, 'storm', 12);
}

function cueFired(name, bar) {    // or read cueName in draw()
  look = SCENES[name];
}
```

| call / read / define | |
|---|---|
| `cue(bar, name, every)` | at bar `bar` (1 is the first, `4.5` is halfway through bar 4); `every` bars again if given |
| `cueName` | the last cue that fired (`''` before the first) |
| `cueFired(name, bar)` | a cue's bar has come |
| `barStarted(bar)`, `stepStarted(step, bar)` | the first step of every bar; every step |

The same `cue()` twice adds nothing, so it may also sit in `draw()`. On one step the cues fire in the order they were
declared, then `barStarted`, `stepStarted` and that step's hits. A silent clock: `startDrums({})`. The whole of it, ready to
open: `p5/examples/drums/`; a line of rhythm with `drumPhase` and `beatPhase`: `p5/examples/rhythm/`; the rhythm drawn on the canvas: `p5/examples/rhythm-visual/`.

## Values over time: lag, env, speed, spring, trail

A knob or `micLevel` jumps; what looks good is how it moves between the jumps. TouchDesigner does this with CHOPs; the
same operators are here, one call each in `draw()`, nothing to declare, and seconds are seconds (the same curve at 30 and
at 144 fps):

```js
circle(width / 2, height / 2, 50 + lag(micLevel, 0.03, 0.4) * 300);   // a VU meter: opens at once, closes slowly
scale(1 + env('kick', 0.01, 0.3));                                     // the drum machine: every kick swells it, gone in 0.3 s
rotate(spring(knob1, 100, 6) * TWO_PI);                                // flick a knob: it overshoots and settles
```

| TouchDesigner | oav-p5 | |
|---|---|---|
| Lag CHOP (Lag 1 / Lag 2) | `lag(value, up, down)` | follows `value`: `up` seconds while it rises, `down` while it falls (`down` = `up` if left out; 0.1) |
| Trigger CHOP (attack, decay) | `env('kick', attack, decay)`, `trigger('boom')` | 0..1: up to 1 in `attack` seconds after each event, back to 0 in `decay` (0.01, 0.3). Events: `'kick'` `'snare'` `'hat'` `'beat'` (the microphone or the drum machine, the hits `kickDetected` hears), `'note'` (any key), `'bar'` `'step'` (the drums), a cue's name, `trigger('boom')`; or a switch: `env(mouseIsPressed, …)` |
| Speed CHOP | `speed(rate)` | adds `rate` every second: `rotate(speed(TWO_PI))` turns once a second |
| Spring CHOP | `spring(value, stiffness, damping)` | follows like a mass on a spring (100, 6: two or three bounces; damping 20: none) |
| Trail CHOP | `trail(value, seconds)` | the last `seconds` (2) as an array, 60 values a second, oldest first, the newest last |
| Slope CHOP | `slope(value)` | how fast it changes, per second |
| Count CHOP | `count(beat)`, `count(beat, 4)`, `count('kick')` | how many times it turned on; with 4: 0 1 2 3 0 …; a name: how many of those events so far |
| a CHOP's viewer | `scope(value, 'label')` | a small plot in the corner of the page (below) |
| | `drawTrail(values, x, y, w, h)` | the same plot on the canvas, in the work and in a recording |

**Seconds, the same as in TouchDesigner.** A lag's seconds mean what a Lag CHOP's do: about the time the value takes to
follow 90% of a jump, so `lag(x, 0.1)` here moves like a Lag CHOP set to 0.1 ([Lag CHOP](https://docs.derivative.ca/Lag_CHOP)).
Underneath it is a one-pole lag with a time constant of seconds ÷ 2.3 (ln 10); `@openav/mapping`'s `smooth` keeps its
own 63% time constant. Attack and decay are lengths in both.

**Nothing to declare.** The first `lag()` in `draw()` keeps the first lag's memory, the second the second, every frame;
`spring()`, `speed()`, `trail()` … are counted each on their own. Put one inside an `if`, or in a loop whose length
changes, and the order slips: a card says so, and from then on oav-p5 matches each call by the line it is written on. The
sure way is a name, a string at the end: `lag(p.size, 0.1, 0.5, 'p' + p.id)`. A named one is the same wherever it is called,
`draw()`, `setup()` or `mousePressed()`; an unnamed one outside `draw()` has nothing to remember by and returns its input
(`speed` 0, `trail` `[]`), and a card says that too. `env()`, `trigger()` and `count('kick')` are about events and work
anywhere. A sketch with its own `speed` or `count` keeps it; `OAVp5.chop.speed(…)` is the same function under another name.

**Seeing the values.** `scope(value, 'label')` returns `value`, so it can wrap an expression:
`circle(x, y, scope(lag(micLevel, 0.03, 0.4), 'lag') * 300)`. Each label is one line in a small oscilloscope across the
page from the 🎹: the last 4 seconds and the value now; `scope(micLevel, 'mic')` beside it shows what the lag did. It lives
on the page, not on the canvas: never in a recording or a 📷, never in the way of a click; `hints=off` or `scope=off` hides
it. To draw it in the work: `stroke(255); drawTrail(trail(micLevel, 3), 0, height - 100, width, 100)` (or
`drawTrail(micLevel, …)`, which keeps its own 2 seconds): 0 at the bottom of the box, 1 at the top (`lo`, `hi` after `h`),
the sketch's `stroke()` (white under `noStroke()`).

The math is [@openav/chop](packages.md#openav-chop), loaded from next to this file the first time one of these is called;
until it arrives (a few frames) each returns its input as it is. What each parameter means follows Derivative's
TouchDesigner documentation; the code is OAV's own. Raw against lagged, side by side, with the scope: `p5/examples/lag/`. `env`, `spring`, `speed`, `count` and `slope` driving a disc that a bass drum opens, with `startDrums()` as the only input: `p5/examples/chop/`.

## Recording: a video with its sound

```js
function keyPressed() {
  if (key === 'r') recordingIsOn ? stopRecording() : startRecording();   // startRecording(10): ten seconds, then it stops
}

function recordingSaved(info) {   // info.name, info.seconds, info.bytes, info.format ('mp4' or 'webm')
}
```

| call / read / define | |
|---|---|
| `startRecording()`, `startRecording(seconds)`, `startRecording({ seconds, fps, mic, name, canvas, bitrate })` | record the canvas and the sketch's sound; with seconds it stops by itself; a take is 5 minutes at most. `canvas` is the canvas to record (a p5 canvas or `createGraphics()`; the default is the biggest p5 canvas on the page), `bitrate` is bits a second (the default follows the canvas size and frame rate: 4 to 16 Mb/s, up to 24 Mb/s above 30 frames a second) |
| `stopRecording()` | stop; the file downloads |
| `recordingIsOn` | whether a take is running |
| `recordingSaved(info)` | the file is saved: `name`, `seconds`, `bytes`, `format`, `width`, `height`, `audio`, `sources`, `warnings`, `blob`, `url` |

In the 🎹 panel, **⏺** starts and stops a take with no code; while it runs, the 🎹 button shows a red dot and the time (a
click on the dot stops it). **📷** saves the canvas as a PNG.

- **What is in the video.** The p5 canvas at its own pixel size (a retina screen doubles it), 30 frames a second, and every
  sound this file makes: `startSound()`, the drum machine and the pads, the microphone while it is on, and p5.sound 1.x, mixed
  into one track while the speakers play as before. The 🎹, the drum grid, the cards and OPC's panel are not on the canvas,
  so they are not in the video.
- **The file.** MP4 (H.264 + AAC), which Instagram, YouTube and every editor take, wherever the browser can write it: Chrome
  126 and later, Edge, Safari. Elsewhere (Firefox, an older Chrome) WebM, and a card says Instagram will not take it. It is
  named `oav-20261015-183005.mp4`; on a computer it lands in Downloads, on a phone a **Share** button on the card saves it to
  the photo library or sends it to Instagram.
- **Checked after every take.** A card says what was recorded (format, length, size, with or without sound) and, when something
  is wrong, what and why: nothing reached the recording although a sound was on (no click on the page yet, nothing played), WebM,
  an almost empty file, a black video of a canvas that was not black (Safari recording a WebGL canvas, WebKit 229611), an image
  from another site on the canvas (no CORS), no recorder in this browser.
- **The microphone** is in the take while it is on: wear headphones, or the speakers are recorded twice. `record=nomic` leaves
  it out.
- **p5.sound.** p5.sound 1.x (the one for p5 1.x) is recorded. The p5.sound made for p5 2.x connects each sound straight to
  the speakers, with no output a recording can tap: it is not in the take, and a card says so. Switch the sketch to p5 1.11, or
  use `startSound()` and `startDrums()`. Sound the sketch makes with its own Tone.js or Web Audio code is not recorded either.
- **Stills.** 📷 (or `OAVp5.record.shot()`) saves the canvas alone as `oav-<date>-<time>.png`, without the 🎹 or the cards;
  from code, p5's own `saveCanvas('name', 'png')` does the same.
- **Options.** `record=nomic` (no microphone) or `record=off` (no ⏺ or 📷; `startRecording()` does nothing), `recfps=60`,
  `reclimit=600` (seconds), `title=my-piece` (in the file name); for one take, `startRecording({ seconds, fps, mic: false, name, canvas, bitrate })`.
- The whole of it, ready to open: `p5/examples/record/`.

## Three inputs

| input | how |
|---|---|
| a real controller | Web MIDI in Chrome, Edge and Firefox; the browser asks once |
| the on-screen controller | 🎹 opens `<oav-controller>`, which follows the controller you plug in |
| a phone | 📱 in that panel shows a QR code; the phone's [remote page](remote.md) MIDI tab plays the sketch |

All three arrive as the same MIDI bytes, so the sketch cannot tell them apart (`midi.last.source` can). Safari and
iPad have no Web MIDI; the on-screen controller and the phone still work there. A sketch that uses Web MIDI itself
(`navigator.requestMIDIAccess`, WebMidi.js) also hears the screen and the phone, as one more input called
**OAV Virtual MIDI**.

Other programs are a fourth input (0.7). What a program plays into OAV Virtual MIDI's **output** — Strudel's
`.midi('OAV Virtual MIDI')` — reaches the sketch at the moment it was stamped with (`midi.last.source` is `virtual-out`);
an external MIDI clock moves `drumPhase`, `drumBar` and a drum machine; and `link=<room>` brings another tab's or another
computer's programs into this sketch. All of it: [With Strudel](strudel.md).

## When something goes wrong

Nobody watches OpenProcessing's console while playing, so problems are said on the page: a small card beside the 🎹, never
over the middle of the canvas, in the browser's language, once per page, with a × to close it. Each card says **what
happened, why, and what to press**, and the console gets the same sentence.

- **The microphone**: refused (the lock left of the address → allow → click the canvas), refused by the computer's settings,
  by an embed without `allow="microphone"`, missing, held by another app (Zoom, OBS), an `http:` page, or the browser still asking.
- **MIDI**: no Web MIDI (Safari, iPad: use the 🎹 or a phone), or the permission refused. Only for a sketch that plays from
  MIDI; a sketch that uses none of this never sees a card.
- **Your own code**: an error inside `notePressed()`, `kickDetected()`, `drumHit()` and the other callbacks shows the
  message with the file and line, and the sketch keeps running. A sketch that declares its own `note` or `knob1` (`let`,
  `var`, `function`) keeps it, and the card says what to read instead (`midi.last.note`, `knob(1)`).
- **Sound and drums**: waiting for the first click, the piano still loading (the electric piano meanwhile), an instrument
  that failed (the fallback plays), Tone.js unreachable, the drum machine playing silently until a click.
- **Recording**: started (what it hears, how to stop), saved (format, length, size, sound), a take with no sound in it, WebM
  (not for Instagram), a black take, an almost empty file, a canvas with another site's image, no recorder in this browser.

`?oav_hints=off` (or `window.OAV_P5 = { hints: 'off' }`) keeps them in the console only; `OAVp5.hints` lists what was said.

**🩺 Check-up.** 🩺 in the 🎹 panel (or `OAVp5.check()`) shows the version, the page, the browser, the microphone, MIDI,
sound, drums, recording (MP4 or WebM here, the last take), the wiring, the sketch's own names and the hints so far, as one card to screenshot, with a *copy* button and a
link to the full [device check](https://openaudiovisual.com/check/).

## In Hydra

[Hydra](https://hydra.ojack.xyz) has a loader of its own; the same file works there, and Hydra's arrow functions read the
variables each frame:

```js
await loadScript('https://openaudiovisual.com/p5/oav-p5.js')
osc(10, 0.1, () => knob1 * 2).out()                     // knob 1 sets the colour offset
```

```js
osc(10, 0.1, () => 1 + micLevel * 3).out()              // the microphone, asked for when this line first runs
```

`note`, `velocity`, `knob1` … `knob8`, `fader1` …, `pad1` …, `drumStep` and the 🎹 on-screen controller are there the same way.
Hydra is not p5, so there are no `notePressed()` callbacks to define; subscribe instead:
`midi.on('notePressed', (note, velocity) => { … })` or `OAVp5.drums.on('hit', (lane, velocity) => { … })` (each returns a
function that unsubscribes). Checked against
hydra-synth 1.4.0, the library the editor runs (`p5/test/hydra-smoke.cjs`).

## Notes

- **Why `prepend`.** p5's friendly-error checker reads the last `<script>` on the page as your sketch. Put first, this
  file is never mistaken for your code.
- **Why one asynchronous line is enough.** p5 starts global mode on the window's `load` event, and a script inserted
  while the page is loading holds `load` back until it has run, so `knob1` already exists in `setup()`.
- **When the line does not load** (offline, a typo in the URL), code that reads `knob1` stops with *knob1 is not
  defined*.
- **Embedding a sketch elsewhere.** OpenProcessing's own pages allow MIDI and the microphone in the sketch frame. The
  embed code it gives you does not: add `allow="midi"` to that `<iframe>` if the embedded sketch should hear a hardware
  controller, and `allow="microphone"` if it should hear the microphone.
- **Options, MIDI-level access and tests**: [`p5/README.md`](https://github.com/frank890417/open-audiovisual/tree/main/p5).
  Examples: `p5/examples/particles/`, `p5/examples/opc/`, `p5/examples/mic/`, `p5/examples/keys/`, `p5/examples/drums/`, `p5/examples/rhythm/`, `p5/examples/rhythm-visual/`, `p5/examples/rhythm-lab/`, `p5/examples/record/`, `p5/examples/lag/`, `p5/examples/chop/`, `p5/examples/with-strudel/` and `p5/examples/note-names/`.

---

<!-- source: docs/strudel.md -->

# With Strudel

[Strudel](https://strudel.cc) is a live-coding environment for music in the browser, a JavaScript version of
[TidalCycles](https://tidalcycles.org). OAV is a separate program. The two run side by side the way two programs on a
stage do: Strudel plays, and OAV brings what Strudel does not have — knobs on screen and on a phone, a microphone that
is analysed, Web MIDI where the browser has none — and draws what Strudel plays in a p5.js sketch, on the same page or
in another tab or on another computer. They meet through MIDI (OAV's virtual port, "OAV Virtual MIDI") and through
the page's own variables (`knob1`, `micLevel`, `drumPhase`). OAV never loads or calls any of Strudel's code.

Everything on this page was run on strudel.cc as a user runs it (its editor, Ctrl+Enter, its documented functions):
`p5/test/strudel-smoke.cjs` does it again.

## Load OAV in Strudel

Strudel → **settings** → **prebake**, add one line at the end, **save**:

```js
await import('https://openaudiovisual.com/p5/oav-p5.js')
```

- **Single quotes.** Strudel reads text in double quotes (and backticks) as mini-notation: a URL in double quotes is a
  `[mini] parse error`.
- **Why the prebake.** It runs before your code, also after a reload (about 2.5 s after the editor appears), so OAV is
  on the page before anything opens MIDI. If Strudel's `midin()` ran before OAV loaded, `midin('OAV Virtual MIDI')` gets
  nothing and says nothing: reload. 🩺 then shows "no program has asked OAV Virtual MIDI for MIDI".
- The line can also be the first line of your code. Options go on the line before it:
  `window.OAV_P5 = { link: 'my-room' }`.
- Strudel's **share** button puts the prebake into the link (with "share with patterns" ticked): whoever opens it gets
  OAV too.

On strudel.cc OAV changes its manners. It does not ask for MIDI when it loads (`hardware=click`: Strudel's `midin()`
asks). The 🎹 panel is a box in the corner, a third of the window high, so the code stays in view. One card says which
names Strudel already has — `note`, `velocity`, `beat` are Strudel's functions, OAV leaves them alone — and what to
read instead: `OAVp5.last.note`, `OAVp5.last.value`, `OAVp5.mic.on('beat', fn)`. `knob1`, `micLevel`, `drumPhase`
and the rest are free names there.

## Recipe 1: knobs, a phone and the microphone as Strudel's parameters

Strudel's `signal()` turns a function into a parameter; OAV's names are plain values a function can return.

```js
s("bd*4").gain(signal(() => knob1))
s("hh*8").lpf(signal(() => 300 + micLevel * 8000))
```

- `knob1` moves with knob 1 of the 🎹 on screen, of a MIDI controller, or of a phone (🎹 → 📱, scan the code).
  `knob(2)`, `fader1`, `pad1` are there too. Measured: knob 1 at 0, the kick is silent; at 127, it is heard (RMS 0.58).
- Strudel reads the value when it schedules, 0.2–0.3 s before the sound: a knob is heard that much later.
- `micLevel`, `bass`, `mid`, `treble` are OAV's analysis of the microphone (Strudel has none); reading one asks for the
  microphone. Wear headphones: the microphone hears the speakers, and `gain(signal(() => micLevel))` feeds back.
- Strudel's own MIDI input works on OAV's port too, also in Safari (no Web MIDI there; OAV's port is virtual):

```js
const cc = await midin('OAV Virtual MIDI')
s("bd*4").gain(cc(74))
```

Knob 1 of the on-screen MiniLab 3 is CC 74. `midikeys('OAV Virtual MIDI')` makes the 🎹 keys and the phone Strudel's
keyboard.

## Recipe 2: Strudel plays, a p5 sketch draws

**On the same page.** Send to OAV's port:

```js
note("c3 [e3 g3] <a3 b3> c4").midi('OAV Virtual MIDI')
```

Strudel hands each note over 0.21–0.32 s early with the moment it should sound; OAV waits for that moment and then
calls `notePressed(note, velocity)` (in Strudel, with no sketch: `OAVp5.on('notePressed', fn)`), moves `knob1` for a CC,
plays a pad. Measured on strudel.cc: each note is heard within 5 ms of its timestamp (10 notes, at most 4.5 ms late; `p5/test/strudel-smoke.cjs`), and `drumPhase` follows Strudel's clock to 0.1 ms. What arrives on the port is never handed
back to OAV's input, so `midikeys('OAV Virtual MIDI')` played into `.midi('OAV Virtual MIDI')` is one echo, not a loop.

**Strudel's clock.** MIDI counts 24 clocks a beat, so a cycle of one 4-beat bar sends 96:

```js
setcps(128 / 60 / 4)
$: s("bd*4, [~ sd]*2, hh*8")
$: midicmd("clock*96, <start stop>/8").midi('OAV Virtual MIDI')
```

`drumPhase`, `beatPhase`, `drumBar`, `drumStep` and `drumBpm` follow it. A drum machine started with `startDrums()`
plays at Strudel's tempo, on Strudel's downbeat, and starts and stops with it (the card says "following an external
clock · 128 BPM"). Measured at 128 bpm: `drumPhase` within 1.2 ms of Strudel's bar (median 0.04 ms), every kick within
6 ms of Strudel's beat (three runs); Strudel's start, which arrives three times with one timestamp, counts once. Without a clock
nothing changes; `clock=off` ignores one.

**In another tab, or on another computer.** Give both pages the same room. In Strudel's prebake:

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { link: 'my-room' }
await import('https://openaudiovisual.com/p5/oav-p5.js')
```

and in the p5 sketch (OpenProcessing: before the one line; or `?sketch_oav_link=my-room` on the page's address):

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { link: 'my-room' };
document.head.prepend(Object.assign(document.createElement('script'), { src: 'https://openaudiovisual.com/p5/oav-p5.js' }));
```

Everything Strudel sends to OAV's port — notes, CCs, the clock — reaches every other OAV page in the room, through the
same relay the phones use. 🎹 grows a 🔗: green when another page is there; the panel says the room, the pages and the
trip. The receiving page plays each note when Strudel plays it, not when it arrives: it lines the two clocks up from the
fastest trips it has seen and the round trips both pages measure (packages/relay/link.js explains how), and Strudel's
quarter-second head start covers the trip. Measured with two tabs on one Mac over wss://remote.cheyuwu.com (one way
≈ 61 ms): notes within −3 … +7 ms of Strudel's timestamps (two runs). Across two computers add the difference between the
two halves of a round trip (usually a few ms). Keep the default relay (`wss://`): Chrome does not let strudel.cc reach a
relay on your own machine or network (`ws://127.0.0.1…` is blocked by its local-network checks). On a network whose jitter is longer than Strudel's head start, `linkdelay=` (ms)
buffers more. A page never sends on what it received, and a program that plays a linked note back out is caught as an
echo. The room is the phones' room too: one QR code plays every page in it.

The sketch side, ready to run: `p5/examples/with-strudel/` (?room=… on its address).

## Recipe 3: Strudel, Hydra and OAV on one page

With OAV in the prebake:

```js
await initHydra()
osc(10, 0.1, () => knob1 * 2).rotate(() => drumPhase * 6.28).color(1, () => micLevel, 0.6).out()
setcps(120 / 60 / 4)
$: s("bd*4, [~ sd]*2, hh*8").gain(signal(() => 0.3 + knob1))
$: midicmd("clock*96").midi('OAV Virtual MIDI')
```

Hydra turns once a bar on Strudel's clock (through `drumPhase`), knob 1 drives Hydra and Strudel at once, and the
microphone colours the picture.

## Options for Strudel

Set before the line (`window.OAV_P5 = { … }`), or `?oav_key=value` on a p5 page's address.

| key | values | default |
|---|---|---|
| `link` | a room name (letters, digits, `-`, `_`): pages in it hear each other's programs | none |
| `linkdelay` | milliseconds of extra buffer on a linked page's notes | `0` |
| `clock` | `follow` (an external MIDI clock moves `drumPhase` and the drums) · `off` | `follow` |
| `strudel` | `auto` (strudel.cc, or Strudel's functions already on the page) · `on` · `off` | `auto` |
| `compact` | `on` (the panel as a box in the corner) · `off` | `on` in Strudel |
| `hardware` | `auto` · `click` · `off` | `click` in Strudel |

## Credits and licences

Strudel is © its contributors (begun by Felix Roos and Alex McLean), free software under the GNU Affero General
Public License v3: [strudel.cc](https://strudel.cc), source at [codeberg.org/uzu/strudel](https://codeberg.org/uzu/strudel).
TidalCycles, whose way of writing patterns Strudel carries to the browser, is Alex McLean's. Music you make with Strudel is
yours (Strudel's FAQ).

OAV is MIT-licensed and a separate program. It contains no Strudel code, does not load `@strudel/*` at run time and calls
none of Strudel's functions: it only looks at the page's address and at which names the page already has, to choose its
manners. The two meet the way two programs on a stage meet, over MIDI. OAV's own rhythm strings (`startDrums("bd*4,
hh*8")`, @openav/pattern) are an independent implementation of the TidalCycles / Strudel way of writing rhythm, from their
public documentation. Please do not ask Strudel's community for help with OAV: OAV's issues are on
[GitHub](https://github.com/frank890417/open-audiovisual/issues).
