- [x] oav-p5: one line for any p5.js sketch, with controllers, a phone, the microphone, sound, a drum machine you can
  write as one line of rhythm, bars and cues, and video recording; versioned on its own ([changelog](https://openaudiovisual.com/changelog/))
- [x] one line of rhythm, TidalCycles/Strudel-style mini-notation (`@openav/pattern`)
- [x] values over time as TouchDesigner's CHOPs shape them: lag, envelope, speed, spring, trail (`@openav/chop`)
- [x] next to Strudel: what a program plays into OAV Virtual MIDI, an external MIDI clock, and `link=<room>` across
  tabs and computers ([With Strudel](strudel.md))

## v1.x — the show grows

- **Audience-device input** — *classic controller shipped* (`@openav/relay`, `@openav/surface`,
  `@openav/remote`): a zero-dep room server, `phone/{id}/*` sensors, a TouchOSC-style widget set,
  layout JSON, `autoSurface(params)`, feedback to the phone. Next:
  - [x] QR code on the join card (`@openav/remote/qr`, a ~150-line zero-dep encoder) — and on static hosts the show uses the public relay with a random room, so the examples on openaudiovisual.com take phones too
  - [ ] *experimental* surfaces: gesture/physics widgets, shared multi-user surfaces, audience-mode (many phones → aggregate signals like `crowd/tilt/mean`)
  - [ ] mic as a phone sensor; per-device profiles; layout editor / import-export UI
- **Score & Director** — *shipped* (`@openav/score`): cuts as segment lengths, derived versions, cues, `hold`, segment modules that fail alone, the prompter's acts, score → MIDI markers. Next:
  - [x] MIDI clock in: `MidiClock` (`@openav/midi`) follows start, stop and song position, and oav-p5's drum machine and `drumPhase` follow it (0.7)
  - [ ] the score on an external clock, and clock and transport out, so a DAW can be the master clock of the score, or follow it
  - [ ] a `clocks` table in the cut, only if a show needs engines on two different time lines (see [Score & Director](score.md#clocks-why-there-are-none))
  - [ ] a score editor on the desk: drag a segment's length, see every cue move
- **Signal recording & replay** — *MIDI takes shipped* (`@openav/record`: `TakeRecorder`,
  `TakePlayer`, `.mid` in and out; `EventLog` already records any signal beside a video). Next:
  replay the full signal stream (hands, body, audio analysis) into any world. Rehearse without
  the performer; archive the gesture, not just the video.
- **npm publish** of `@openav/*`, and docs pages that are themselves performable with the framework.
- **WebGPU world adapter** as WebGPU compute matures for particle/agent worlds.

## v2.x — the stage widens

- **NDI gateway**: headless-browser → NDI bridge so browser output enters
  professional video pipelines (research: WebRTC→NDI converters already exist).
- **Distributed performance**: multi-browser signal sync over WebRTC data
  channels — several machines, one signal space, geographically split ensembles.
- **Agent performers**: LLM-driven agents subscribing to signals and writing
  params — improvising alongside humans (lineage: The Last Input's autonomous
  city agents).

## Non-goals

- a node-based visual editor (cables.gl does this well; we are a library)
- a synthesis toolkit of our own (Tone.js is the neighbor: `@openav/sound` wraps it
  behind a small engine contract, and `audio.input()` accepts its nodes)
- being a platform: your show is your repo, not an account on our server


---

<!-- source: docs/reference/reference.json -->

# API reference (generated)

> 487 public names of oav-p5 0.8.2 and every package, read from the code and checked against it in CI. Page: https://openaudiovisual.com/docs/reference/ (search it, every name has an anchor: #micLevel). Data: https://openaudiovisual.com/docs/reference/reference.json. An oav-p5 example starts, in a sketch, with this line: `document.head.prepend(Object.assign(document.createElement('script'), { src: 'https://openaudiovisual.com/p5/oav-p5.js' }));`

## midi

- `controlChange` (event, oav-p5): `function controlChange(cc, value, channel) {}` — You define this function; oav-p5 calls it for every MIDI control change (a knob, a fader, the mod wheel, the sustain pedal), whether or not the controller is known. (before it has a value: Defining the function is enough. oav-p5 asks the browser for Web MIDI when it loads (the default, [`?oav_hardware=auto`](#option-hardware)), and a sketch that defines it also gets a card if Web MIDI is missing or blocked. Keys from 🎹, a phone, [`OAVp5.input()`](#OAVp5.input) and other programs reach it too. `OAVp5.on('controlChange', fn)` does the same without defining a global function, and returns a function that stops it.)

```js
let shown = 'move a knob, the mod wheel or a pedal';

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(24);
}

function controlChange(cc, value, channel) {
  shown = 'CC ' + cc + ' = ' + nf(value, 1, 2) + '  (channel ' + channel + ')';
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(shown, width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `fader` (function, oav-p5): `fader(n)` — Returns the position of fader number `n`, from 0 to 1: the same as `fader1` to `fader8`, for any `n`.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  for (let i = 1; i <= 4; i++) circle(i * 80, height - 40 - fader(i) * 200, 30);
}
```

- `fader1`, `fader2`, `fader3`, `fader4`, `fader5`, `fader6`, `fader7`, `fader8` (variable, oav-p5): `fader1` — The position of a controller fader (slider), from 0 to 1: `fader1` is the first fader, up to `fader8`. (range 0..1; before it has a value: Nothing to call. Web MIDI is asked for at load, exactly as for a knob ([`knob1`](#knob1)); reading a fader also makes a missing or refused Web MIDI show as a card.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  rect(40, height - 40, fader1 * (width - 80), 24);   // fader 1 is a level bar
}
```

- `faderMoved` (event, oav-p5): `function faderMoved(n, value) {}` — You define this function; oav-p5 calls it whenever a fader moves.

```js
let level = 0;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function faderMoved(n, value) {
  if (n === 1) level = value;   // fader 1 only
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  rect(40, height - 40, level * (width - 80), 24);
}
```

- `knob` (function, oav-p5): `knob(n)` — Returns the position of knob number `n`, from 0 to 1: the same as `knob1` to `knob8`, for any `n`.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  noStroke();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  for (let i = 1; i <= 8; i++) {
    rect(i * 44 - 20, height - 20, 30, -10 - knob(i) * 250);   // one bar per knob
  }
}
```

- `knob1`, `knob2`, `knob3`, `knob4`, `knob5`, `knob6`, `knob7`, `knob8` (variable, oav-p5): `knob1` — The position of a controller knob, from 0 to 1: `knob1` is the first knob, `knob2` the second, up to `knob8`. (range 0..1; before it has a value: Nothing to call. With the default `hardware=auto`, oav-p5 asks the browser for Web MIDI as soon as it loads, whatever the sketch reads (Chrome, Edge and Firefox have it; Safari and iPad do not: use 🎹 or a phone there). Reading a knob also tells oav-p5 the sketch plays from MIDI, so when Web MIDI is missing or refused a card beside the 🎹 says so; a sketch that uses none of this never sees that card. [`?oav_hardware=click`](#option-hardware) waits for the 🎹 panel instead.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(knob1 * 255);   // knob 1 sets the brightness
}
```

- `knobMoved` (event, oav-p5): `function knobMoved(n, value) {}` — You define this function; oav-p5 calls it whenever a knob moves.

```js
let last = 'turn a knob';

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(32);
}

function knobMoved(n, value) {
  last = 'knob ' + n + ': ' + nf(value, 1, 2);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(last, width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `lastNoteTs` (variable, oav-p5): `lastNoteTs` — When the last key went down, on the `millis()` clock: `millis() - lastNoteTs` is how many ms ago.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  noStroke();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  const ago = millis() - lastNoteTs;    // ms since a key went down
  fill(255, 200 * exp(-ago / 400) + 30);
  circle(200, 150, 60 + 160 * exp(-ago / 400));
}
```

- `midiMessage` (event, oav-p5): `function midiMessage(bytes, source) {}` — You define this function; oav-p5 calls it for every MIDI message it receives, with the raw bytes and where they came from. (before it has a value: Defining the function is enough. oav-p5 asks the browser for Web MIDI when it loads (the default, [`?oav_hardware=auto`](#option-hardware)), and a sketch that defines it also gets a card if Web MIDI is missing or blocked. Keys from 🎹, a phone, [`OAVp5.input()`](#OAVp5.input) and other programs reach it too. `OAVp5.on('midiMessage', fn)` does the same without defining a global function, and returns a function that stops it.)

```js
let shown = 'play something';

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(20);
}

function midiMessage(bytes, source) {
  shown = bytes.map((b) => '0x' + b.toString(16).toUpperCase()).join(' ') + '  from ' + source;
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(shown, width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `note` (variable, oav-p5): `note` — The MIDI number (0 to 127) of the last key pressed. (range 0..127; before it has a value: Nothing to call. Web MIDI is asked for at load (see [`knob1`](#knob1)). Unlike a knob, merely reading `note` does not tell oav-p5 the sketch plays from MIDI: defining [`notePressed()`](#notePressed) or reading a knob or pad does, which is what makes a missing or refused Web MIDI show as a card. 🎹 and a phone always work.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(64);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(noteName(note), width / 2, height / 2);   // the last key, as a name
}
```

- `noteIsDown` (function, oav-p5): `noteIsDown(n)` — True while the key `n` (a MIDI number or a name like `'C4'`) is held down.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(noteIsDown('C4') ? color(255, 211, 107) : 80);
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 140);   // lights up while middle C is held
}
```

- `noteIsPressed` (variable, oav-p5): `noteIsPressed` — True while at least one key is held down.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(noteIsPressed ? 90 : 20);   // lighter while any key is down
}
```

- `noteOff` (event, oav-p5): `function noteOff(note, channel) {}` — You define this function; oav-p5 calls it for every MIDI note-off, with the key and the channel. (before it has a value: Defining the function is enough. oav-p5 asks the browser for Web MIDI when it loads (the default, [`?oav_hardware=auto`](#option-hardware)), and a sketch that defines it also gets a card if Web MIDI is missing or blocked. Keys from 🎹, a phone, [`OAVp5.input()`](#OAVp5.input) and other programs reach it too. `OAVp5.on('noteOff', fn)` does the same without defining a global function, and returns a function that stops it.)

```js
const down = {};
let held = 'play a key and let it go';

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(24);
}

function noteOn(note) { down[note] = millis(); }

function noteOff(note) {
  if (down[note] !== undefined) {
    held = noteName(note) + ' was held ' + round(millis() - down[note]) + ' ms';
    delete down[note];
  }
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(held, width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `noteOn` (event, oav-p5): `function noteOn(note, velocity, channel) {}` — You define this function; oav-p5 calls it for every MIDI note-on, with the key, how hard and the channel. (before it has a value: Defining the function is enough. oav-p5 asks the browser for Web MIDI when it loads (the default, [`?oav_hardware=auto`](#option-hardware)), and a sketch that defines it also gets a card if Web MIDI is missing or blocked. Keys from 🎹, a phone, [`OAVp5.input()`](#OAVp5.input) and other programs reach it too. `OAVp5.on('noteOn', fn)` does the same without defining a global function, and returns a function that stops it.)

```js
let shown = 'play a key';

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(24);
}

function noteOn(note, velocity, channel) {
  shown = noteName(note) + '  velocity ' + nf(velocity, 1, 2) + '  channel ' + channel;
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(shown, width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `notePressed` (event, oav-p5): `function notePressed(note, velocity) {}` — You define this function; oav-p5 calls it each time a key (or a pad) goes down. (before it has a value: Defining it is enough: oav-p5 calls it from every source, and if Web MIDI is missing or refused it says so in a card beside the 🎹 (Web MIDI itself is asked for at load, see [`knob1`](#knob1)). Keys from 🎹 and from a phone call it too.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  background(20);
  noStroke();
}

function notePressed(note, velocity) {
  fill(random(255), random(255), random(255), 200);
  circle(map(note, 36, 96, 20, width - 20), height / 2, 10 + velocity * 120);
}
```

- `noteReleased` (event, oav-p5): `function noteReleased(note) {}` — You define this function; oav-p5 calls it each time a key (or a pad) is let go.

```js
let held = {};

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function notePressed(note) { held[note] = millis(); }
function noteReleased(note) { delete held[note]; }

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(Object.keys(held).map((n) => noteName(+n)).join('  '), 20, 40);   // the keys down now
}
```

- `pad` (function, oav-p5): `pad(n)` — Returns how hard pad number `n` is pressed, 0 to 1: the same as `pad1` to `pad16`, for any `n`.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  noStroke();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  for (let i = 1; i <= 8; i++) {
    fill(255, 90, 31, 60 + pad(i) * 195);
    square(20 + ((i - 1) % 4) * 92, 40 + floor((i - 1) / 4) * 110, 80);
  }
}
```

- `pad1`, `pad2`, `pad3`, `pad4`, `pad5`, `pad6`, `pad7`, `pad8`, `pad9`, `pad10`, `pad11`, `pad12`, `pad13`, `pad14`, `pad15`, `pad16` (variable, oav-p5): `pad1` — How hard a drum pad is pressed, from 0 to 1: `pad1` is the first pad, up to `pad16`; 0 when it is let go. (range 0..1; before it has a value: Nothing to call. Web MIDI is asked for at load, exactly as for a knob ([`knob1`](#knob1)); reading a pad also makes a missing or refused Web MIDI show as a card.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255, 90, 31);
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 40 + pad1 * 260);   // swells while pad 1 is held
}
```

- `padPressed` (event, oav-p5): `function padPressed(n, velocity) {}` — You define this function; oav-p5 calls it each time a drum pad is hit.

```js
let hits = [];

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  noStroke();
}

function padPressed(n, velocity) {
  hits.push({ x: 40 + ((n - 1) % 4) * 105, y: 70 + floor((n - 1) / 4) * 130, r: 20 + velocity * 60 });
}

function draw() {
  background(20, 40);
  fill(255, 90, 31);
  for (const h of hits) { circle(h.x, h.y, h.r); h.r *= 0.95; }
  hits = hits.filter((h) => h.r > 2);
}
```

- `padReleased` (event, oav-p5): `function padReleased(n) {}` — You define this function; oav-p5 calls it each time a drum pad is let go.

```js
let down = {};

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function padPressed(n) { down[n] = true; }
function padReleased(n) { down[n] = false; }

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255, 90, 31);
  for (let i = 1; i <= 8; i++) if (down[i]) square(10 + (i - 1) * 48, 130, 40);   // lit while held
}
```

- `pitchBend` (event, oav-p5): `function pitchBend(value, channel) {}` — You define this function; oav-p5 calls it whenever the pitch wheel moves, with its position from −1 to 1. (before it has a value: Defining the function is enough. oav-p5 asks the browser for Web MIDI when it loads (the default, [`?oav_hardware=auto`](#option-hardware)), and a sketch that defines it also gets a card if Web MIDI is missing or blocked. Keys from 🎹, a phone, [`OAVp5.input()`](#OAVp5.input) and other programs reach it too. `OAVp5.on('pitchBend', fn)` does the same without defining a global function, and returns a function that stops it.)

```js
let bend = 0;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function pitchBend(value) {
  bend = value;
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  circle(width / 2 + bend * 150, height / 2, 50);   // wheel up: right, wheel down: left
}
```

- `velocity` (variable, oav-p5): `velocity` — How hard the last key was pressed, from 0 to 1. (range 0..1)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255, 90, 31);
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 20 + velocity * 300);   // a harder key makes a bigger circle
}
```

- `OAVp5.bend` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.bend` — Where the pitch wheel is, from −1 (all the way down) through 0 (middle) to 1 (all the way up). (range -1..1)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function mouseDragged() {
  OAVp5.input([0xE0, 0, constrain(round(mouseX / width * 127), 0, 127)]);   // no wheel? drag the mouse
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  circle(width / 2 + OAVp5.bend * 150, height / 2, 50);   // wheel up: right, wheel down: left
  text('bend ' + nf(OAVp5.bend, 1, 2), 20, 30);
}
```

- `OAVp5.cc` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.cc` — An array of 128 numbers, one per MIDI controller number: where each control last was, 0 to 1. `OAVp5.cc[1]` is the mod wheel, `OAVp5.cc[64]` the sustain pedal. (range 128 numbers, 0..1 each)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function mouseDragged() {
  OAVp5.input([0xB0, 1, constrain(round(mouseX / width * 127), 0, 127)]);   // no wheel? drag the mouse
}

function draw() {
  background(OAVp5.cc[64] >= 0.5 ? 90 : 20);   // sustain pedal down: lighter
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 40 + OAVp5.cc[1] * 300);   // mod wheel: size
}
```

- `OAVp5.connectHardware` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.connectHardware()` — Asks the browser for Web MIDI now, and returns a promise that says whether a real controller can be heard. (before it has a value: A browser with Web MIDI (Chrome, Edge, Firefox), on `https` or `localhost`. Some browsers want a click first: call it from `mousePressed()` or a button handler if `setup()` is too early. Safari and iPad have none: the promise resolves `false` and [`OAVp5.hardware`](#OAVp5.hardware) is `'unavailable'`.)

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { hardware: 'click' };   // do not ask at load

let answer = 'click the canvas to ask for Web MIDI';

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function mousePressed() {
  OAVp5.connectHardware().then((ok) => { answer = ok ? 'Web MIDI allowed' : 'no Web MIDI for this page'; });
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(answer, 20, 30);
  text('state: ' + OAVp5.hardware, 20, 60);
}
```

- `OAVp5.devices` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.devices` — The names of the MIDI controllers plugged in, as the browser reports them: an array of text, empty when there is none.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(OAVp5.devices.length ? 'playing: ' + OAVp5.devices.join(', ') : 'no MIDI controller plugged in', 20, 30);
}
```

- `OAVp5.hardware` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.hardware` — Where Web MIDI stands: `'off'`, `'asking'`, `'connected'`, `'waiting'`, `'denied'` or `'unavailable'`. (range 'off' | 'asking' | 'connected' | 'waiting' | 'denied' | 'unavailable')

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(OAVp5.hardware === 'connected' ? color(20, 60, 30) : 20);
  fill(255);
  text('Web MIDI: ' + OAVp5.hardware, 20, 30);
  text('devices: ' + (OAVp5.devices.join(', ') || 'none'), 20, 60);
}
```

- `OAVp5.held` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.held` — A list of the MIDI numbers of the keys that are down right now, lowest first.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(40);
}

function mousePressed() { OAVp5.play(60 + floor(random(12)), 0.8); }   // no keys? click

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(OAVp5.held.map((n) => noteName(n)).join('  ') || 'play a chord', width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `OAVp5.input` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.input(bytes, [source], [device])` — Sends one MIDI message into oav-p5 by hand, as bytes: the whole sketch reacts as if a controller had sent it.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(24);
}

function mousePressed() {
  OAVp5.input([0x90, 60 + floor(random(12)), 100]);   // a note-on, as a key would send it
}

function notePressed(note, velocity) {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(noteName(note) + ' (sent by hand)', width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `OAVp5.isDown` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.isDown(n)` — True while the key `n` (a MIDI number or a name like `'C4'`) is held down: the same as `noteIsDown(n)`.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(32);
}

function mousePressed() { for (const n of ['C4', 'E4', 'G4']) OAVp5.play(n, 0.8); }   // no keys? click for a chord
function mouseReleased() { for (const n of ['C4', 'E4', 'G4']) OAVp5.play(n, 0); }

function draw() {
  const chord = OAVp5.isDown('C4') && OAVp5.isDown('E4') && OAVp5.isDown('G4');
  background(chord ? color(60, 100, 40) : 20);
  fill(255);
  text(chord ? 'C major' : 'hold C4 + E4 + G4', width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `OAVp5.last` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.last` — The latest note, control change or pitch bend that arrived: its type, number, value, channel, where it came from and which control it is. `null` before any.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textSize(16);
}

function mousePressed() { OAVp5.input([0x90, 60 + floor(random(12)), 100], 'mouse'); }   // no controller? click

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(OAVp5.last ? JSON.stringify(OAVp5.last, null, 1) : 'play something', 20, 30);
}
```

- `OAVp5.note` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.note` — An array of 128 numbers, one per MIDI key: how hard that key is held, 0 to 1, and 0 when it is up. `OAVp5.note[60]` is middle C. (range 128 numbers, 0..1 each)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  noStroke();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  for (let n = 36; n < 96; n++) {   // five octaves, C2 to B6
    const v = OAVp5.note[n];
    fill(v > 0 ? color(255, 211, 107) : 60);
    rect(20 + (n - 36) * 6, height - 40 - v * 200, 5, 40 + v * 200);
  }
}
```

- `OAVp5.on` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.on(name, fn)` — Listens to a MIDI event by name without defining a global function, and returns a function that stops listening.

```js
let heard = 0;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  OAVp5.on('noteOn', (note, velocity) => { heard++; });
}

function mousePressed() { OAVp5.play(60 + floor(random(12)), 0.8); }   // no keys? click

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('notes heard: ' + heard, 20, 30);
}
```

- `OAVp5.panel` (object, oav-p5): `OAVp5.panel` — The 🎹 panel as an object: `open()`, `close()` and `toggle()` show and hide it from code.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key === 'p') OAVp5.panel.toggle();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('press p to show or hide the 🎹 panel', 20, 30);
}
```

- `OAVp5.panel.open`, `OAVp5.panel.close`, `OAVp5.panel.toggle` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.panel.open()` — Opens the 🎹 panel (`open()`), closes it (`close()`) or flips it (`toggle()`).

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key === 'o') OAVp5.panel.open();
  if (key === 'c') OAVp5.panel.close();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('o: open the 🎹 panel,  c: close it', 20, 30);
}
```

- `OAVp5.phone` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.phone()` — Shows the 📱 card: a QR code that sends a phone to the remote page, whose MIDI tab then plays this sketch. Returns the room name. (before it has a value: A network connection, to the relay (`wss://remote.cheyuwu.com/relay` unless you set another) and, for the picture of the QR code, to jsDelivr. Without the library the card shows the link as text.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function mousePressed() {
  const room = OAVp5.phone();   // the QR code card opens
  console.log('phones join room', room);
}

function notePressed(note) {
  background(random(255), random(255), random(255));   // a phone key changes the colour
}

function draw() {
  fill(255);
  text('click the canvas, scan the QR code, open the MIDI tab', 20, 30);
}
```

- `OAVp5.play` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.play(note, [velocity])` — Plays a key as if a controller did: `midi.play(60, 0.8)` presses middle C, `midi.play(60, 0)` lets it go.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(32);
}

function mousePressed() { midi.play('C4', 0.8); }
function mouseReleased() { midi.play('C4', 0); }

function draw() {
  background(noteIsDown('C4') ? 90 : 20);
  fill(255);
  text('hold the mouse: C4 is ' + (noteIsDown('C4') ? 'down' : 'up'), width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `OAVp5.wiring` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.wiring([dev])` — Lists which controller knob, fader or pad drives which OpenProcessing OPC variable right now: `[{ control: 'knob1', name: 'radius' }, …]`.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  const wired = OAVp5.wiring();
  text(wired.length ? wired.map((w) => w.control + ' -> ' + w.name).join('\n') : 'nothing wired (no OPC here)', 20, 30);
}
```

## notes

- `noteFreq` (function, oav-p5): `noteFreq(v)` — Returns the frequency in Hz of a note: `noteFreq('A4')` is 440.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(36);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('A4 = ' + noteFreq('A4') + ' Hz\nC4 = ' + noteFreq('C4').toFixed(2) + ' Hz', width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `noteName` (function, oav-p5): `noteName(v, [o])` — Turns a MIDI number into a note name: `noteName(61)` is `'C#4'`.

```js
let shown = 'play a key';

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(64);
}

function notePressed(note) {
  shown = noteName(note) + '  ' + noteName(note, { flats: true });
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(shown, width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `noteNumber` (function, oav-p5): `noteNumber(v)` — Turns a note name like `'C4'` into its MIDI number, 0 to 127.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(40);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('C4 = ' + noteNumber('C4') + '\nA4 = ' + noteNumber('A4') + '\nF#2 = ' + noteNumber('F#2'), width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

## mic

- `bass`, `mid`, `treble` (variable, oav-p5): `bass` — How much of the microphone's sound is low (`bass`), middle (`mid`) or high (`treble`), each from 0 to 1. (range 0..1; before it has a value: Reading any of them asks for the microphone the first time, exactly like [`micLevel`](#micLevel); until you allow it they are `0`.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  colorMode(HSB, 360, 100, 100);
}

function draw() {
  background(230, 40, 10);
  fill(200 + bass * 160, 70, 100);   // low sounds push the colour toward magenta
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 80 + bass * 220);
}
```

- `beat` (variable, oav-p5): `beat` — True for one frame each time the microphone (or the drum machine) hears a beat. (before it has a value: Reading `beat` asks for the microphone the first time, like [`micLevel`](#micLevel). If you would rather be called, define [`beatDetected()`](#beatDetected).)

```js
let flash = 0;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  if (beat) flash = 1;        // true for exactly one frame per beat
  background(20 + flash * 200);
  flash *= 0.9;               // fade back down
}
```

- `beatDetected` (event, oav-p5): `function beatDetected(level) {}` — You define this function; oav-p5 calls it each time the microphone (or the drum machine) hears a beat. (before it has a value: A sketch that defines `beatDetected()` and reads no microphone value starts the microphone on the first click or key. When the drum machine is on, the same function is called for its kicks and snares and the microphone is not opened for it. `OAVp5.mic.on('beat', fn)` hears the same beats without defining a global and returns a function that stops listening, but a listener alone never starts the microphone: read [`micLevel`](#micLevel) or call [`startMic()`](#startMic) as well.)

```js
let flash = 0;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function beatDetected(level) {
  flash = 0.4 + level * 0.6;   // louder beat, brighter flash
}

function draw() {
  background(20 + flash * 200);
  flash *= 0.9;
}
```

- `kickDetected`, `snareDetected`, `hatDetected` (event, oav-p5): `function kickDetected(level) {}` — You define these; oav-p5 calls them when the microphone (or the drum machine) hears a kick, a snare or a hat. (before it has a value: Defining one of them is not enough to open the microphone once the drum machine has started; reading [`micLevel`](#micLevel) (or calling [`startMic()`](#startMic)) is. Without the drum machine, a sketch that defines any of them and reads nothing starts the microphone on the first click or key.)

```js
let kick = 0, snare = 0;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  noStroke();
}

function kickDetected(level) { kick = level; }
function snareDetected(level) { snare = level; }

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255, 90, 31);
  circle(120, 150, 40 + kick * 160);
  fill(120, 190, 255);
  circle(280, 150, 40 + snare * 160);
  kick *= 0.9;
  snare *= 0.9;
}
```

- `kickIsDetected`, `snareIsDetected`, `hatIsDetected` (variable, oav-p5): `kickIsDetected` — True in the one frame after a kick (snare, hat) is heard, from the drum machine or the microphone, like `mouseIsPressed` for a hit.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('bd*4, ~ sd ~ sd', 110);
  noStroke();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255, 90, 31, 255 * lag(kickIsDetected, 0, 0.3));    // a kick lights it, then it fades
  circle(130, 200, 140);
  fill(120, 190, 255, 255 * lag(snareIsDetected, 0, 0.3));
  circle(270, 200, 140);
}
```

- `lastKickTs`, `lastSnareTs`, `lastHatTs`, `lastBeatTs` (variable, oav-p5): `lastKickTs` — When the last kick (snare, hat, beat) came, on the `millis()` clock: `millis() - lastKickTs` is how many ms ago.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('bd*4, hh*8', 100);
  noStroke();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  const ago = millis() - lastKickTs;    // ms since the last kick
  fill(255, 90, 31);
  circle(200, 200, 40 + 160 * exp(-ago / 200));
  fill(255);
  text(isFinite(ago) ? round(ago) + ' ms since the kick' : 'no kick yet', 20, 290);
}
```

- `micIsOn` (variable, oav-p5): `micIsOn` — Whether the microphone is running right now.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(micIsOn ? 20 : 90);
  fill(255);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  text(micIsOn ? 'listening' : 'allow the microphone', width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `micLevel` (variable, oav-p5): `micLevel` — How loud the microphone hears things, from 0 (a quiet room) to 1 (shouting). (range 0..1; before it has a value: Nothing to call. The first time a sketch reads `micLevel` (or [`bass`](#bass), `mid`, `treble`, [`beat`](#beat)), oav-p5 asks the browser for the microphone, and every value stays `0` until you allow it. The page needs `https` or `localhost`. If the browser kept audio quiet until a click, the first click or key starts it. [`?oav_mic=click`](#option-mic) makes only the 🎤 button and [`startMic()`](#startMic) turn it on; `?oav_mic=off` means nothing can.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 50 + micLevel * 300);
}
```

- `micSensitivity` (function, oav-p5): `micSensitivity([v])` — Makes the microphone more or less sensitive: `micSensitivity(2)` is twice as sensitive, `micSensitivity()` says what it is now.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  micSensitivity(3);   // three times as sensitive
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 50 + micLevel * 300);
  text('sensitivity ' + micSensitivity(), 20, 30);   // no argument: just reads it
}
```

- `startMic` (function, oav-p5): `startMic()` — Turns the microphone on and returns a promise that says whether it worked. (before it has a value: Browsers want a click before audio plays: call it from `mousePressed()` or a button handler if `setup()` is too early. It works whatever the `mic` option is, except `?oav_mic=off`, where nothing can start the microphone.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
}

function mousePressed() {
  startMic().then((ok) => console.log(ok ? 'microphone on' : 'no microphone'));
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(micIsOn ? 'level ' + nf(micLevel, 1, 2) : 'click to start the microphone', width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `stopMic` (function, oav-p5): `stopMic()` — Turns the microphone off and sets every microphone value back to 0.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key === 'm') { if (micIsOn) stopMic(); else startMic(); }
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 50 + micLevel * 300);
  text('press m to turn the microphone ' + (micIsOn ? 'off' : 'on'), width / 2, height - 24);
}
```

- `OAVp5.mic` (object, oav-p5): `OAVp5.mic` — The microphone under the plain names: its state, the numbers of `micLevel` and `bass` that never turn it on when read, the raw loudness, start, stop and events.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function mousePressed() {
  if (OAVp5.mic.state === 'on') OAVp5.mic.stop(); else OAVp5.mic.start();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('microphone: ' + OAVp5.mic.state + ' (click the canvas to switch it)', 20, 30);   // reading this asks for nothing
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 50 + OAVp5.mic.level * 300);
}
```

- `OAVp5.mic.analyzer` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.mic.analyzer` — The `AudioAnalyzer` from @openav/audio that listens to the microphone, while the microphone is on; `null` otherwise.

```js
let bins;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  noStroke();
  startMic();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  const a = OAVp5.mic.analyzer;
  if (!a) return;   // the microphone is not on yet
  bins = bins || new Uint8Array(a.analyser.frequencyBinCount);
  a.analyser.getByteFrequencyData(bins);   // the spectrum, 0..255 per frequency bin
  fill(255, 211, 107);
  for (let i = 0; i < 64; i++) {
    const h = bins[i] / 255 * (height - 20);
    rect(20 + i * 5.8, height - 10 - h, 4, h);
  }
}
```

- `OAVp5.mic.bass`, `OAVp5.mic.mid`, `OAVp5.mic.treble` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.mic.bass` — The same 0 to 1 low, middle and high energy as `bass`, `mid` and `treble`, read without ever turning the microphone on. (range 0..1)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  noStroke();
  startMic();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  const bands = [OAVp5.mic.bass, OAVp5.mic.mid, OAVp5.mic.treble];
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    fill(255, 80 + i * 70, 120);
    rect(60 + i * 110, height - 20, 80, -20 - bands[i] * 240);
  }
}
```

- `OAVp5.mic.db` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.mic.db` — The loudness of the microphone in decibels relative to full scale (dBFS): 0 is as loud as it gets, −100 is silence or the microphone being off. (range -100..0)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startMic();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(nf(OAVp5.mic.db, 1, 1) + ' dBFS', 20, 30);
  const own = constrain(map(OAVp5.mic.db, -60, -10, 0, 1), 0, 1);   // an own scale: -60 dB to -10 dB
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 50 + own * 300);
}
```

- `OAVp5.mic.error` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.mic.error` — Why the microphone did not start, as the browser's error name such as `'NotAllowedError'`; `null` while there is no error.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startMic();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('state: ' + OAVp5.mic.state, 20, 30);
  text('error: ' + OAVp5.mic.error, 20, 60);   // null while all is well
}
```

- `OAVp5.mic.floor` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.mic.floor` — The room's own noise as oav-p5 has measured it, in dBFS: the level that `micLevel` treats as silence (plus 6 dB). (range -70..-45)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startMic();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('level ' + nf(OAVp5.mic.db, 1, 1) + ' dBFS', 20, 30);
  text('room noise ' + nf(OAVp5.mic.floor, 1, 1) + ' dBFS', 20, 60);
  text('micLevel ' + nf(OAVp5.mic.level, 1, 2), 20, 90);
}
```

- `OAVp5.mic.level` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.mic.level` — The same 0 to 1 loudness as `micLevel`, read without ever turning the microphone on. (range 0..1)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startMic();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 50 + OAVp5.mic.level * 300);
}
```

- `OAVp5.mic.on` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.mic.on(name, fn)` — Listens to a microphone event (`'beat'`, `'kick'`, `'snare'` or `'hat'`) without defining a global function, and returns a function that stops listening. (before it has a value: Listening does not turn the microphone on: call [`startMic()`](#startMic), press 🎤, or read [`micLevel`](#micLevel) too, or nothing will ever fire. (Defining the global `beatDetected()` is different: oav-p5 sees that function and starts the microphone at the first click.) These events come from the microphone only, not from the drum machine.)

```js
let flash = 0;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startMic();
  OAVp5.mic.on('beat', (level) => { flash = 0.4 + level * 0.6; });   // louder beat, brighter flash
}

function draw() {
  background(20 + flash * 200);
  flash *= 0.9;
}
```

- `OAVp5.mic.rms` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.mic.rms` — The raw loudness of the microphone: a smoothed RMS, 0 to 1, before oav-p5 turns it into the decibel scale of `micLevel`. (range 0..1)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startMic();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('rms ' + nf(OAVp5.mic.rms, 1, 4), 20, 30);
  rect(20, 60, min(OAVp5.mic.rms * 10, 1) * (width - 40), 20);   // magnified 10 times: a voice is small
}
```

- `OAVp5.mic.sensitivity`, `OAVp5.mic.gain` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.mic.sensitivity` — The microphone's sensitivity: 1 normally, 2 for twice as sensitive. [`micSensitivity()`](#micSensitivity) sets it; `OAVp5.mic.gain` is the old name. (range 0.05..20)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  micSensitivity(3);   // a quiet or far-away microphone
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('sensitivity ' + OAVp5.mic.sensitivity, 20, 30);   // 3
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 50 + micLevel * 300);
}
```

- `OAVp5.mic.start` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.mic.start()` — Turns the microphone on and returns a promise that says whether it worked: the same as `startMic()`.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function mousePressed() {
  OAVp5.mic.start().then((ok) => console.log(ok ? 'microphone on' : 'no microphone'));
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(OAVp5.mic.state === 'on' ? 'listening' : 'click the canvas to start the microphone', 20, 30);
}
```

- `OAVp5.mic.state` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.mic.state` — Where the microphone is: `'off'`, `'asking'`, `'on'`, `'denied'` or `'unavailable'`. (range 'off' | 'asking' | 'on' | 'denied' | 'unavailable')

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startMic();
}

function draw() {
  background(OAVp5.mic.state === 'on' ? 20 : color(90, 30, 30));
  fill(255);
  text('microphone: ' + OAVp5.mic.state, 20, 30);
  if (OAVp5.mic.state === 'denied') text('click the lock left of the address and allow it', 20, 60);
}
```

- `OAVp5.mic.stop` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.mic.stop()` — Turns the microphone off and sets every microphone value back to 0: the same as `stopMic()`.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startMic();
}

function mousePressed() {
  OAVp5.mic.stop();   // the browser's recording indicator goes away
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('microphone: ' + OAVp5.mic.state + ' (click the canvas to stop it)', 20, 30);
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 50 + OAVp5.mic.level * 300);
}
```

- `AudioAnalyzer` (class, @openav/audio): `new AudioAnalyzer({ signals = null, fftSize = 2048, smooth = 0.7 } = {})` — Listens to the microphone, an audio element or any Web Audio node, and turns it into loudness, three bands, onsets and kick, snare and hat hits. (before it has a value: Browsers start audio only after a user gesture. `enableMic()` asks for the microphone, and the analyser's `AudioContext` stays suspended until the page has had a click or a key: `update()` calls `resume()` on every frame, so the numbers start by themselves after the first click. Until then they are all 0. The page needs `https` or `localhost` for the microphone.)

## sound

- `soundIsOn` (variable, oav-p5): `soundIsOn` — Whether notes are being heard right now: true once `startSound()` has finished, false before and after. (before it has a value: It becomes true only after [`startSound()`](#startSound) (or 🔊 in the 🎹 panel, or `?oav_sound=piano`), and after the click the browser wants.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startSound('organ');
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(soundIsOn ? color(120, 220, 140) : color(220, 160, 60));
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 80);
  fill(255);
  textAlign(CENTER);
  text(soundIsOn ? 'sound is on' : 'click the canvas to turn sound on', width / 2, height - 40);
}
```

- `startSound`, `OAVp5.sound.start` (function, oav-p5): `startSound([id])` — Makes the keys you play heard through an instrument you name, and returns a promise that says whether sound is on. (before it has a value: A browser lets a page make sound only after a click or a key press on the page, and a key on a MIDI keyboard does not count. Calling `startSound()` in `setup()` is fine: [`OAVp5.sound.state`](#OAVp5.sound.state) is `'waiting'` and a card beside the 🎹 says "Sound is ready but silent"; the first click or key press turns sound on. [`soundIsOn`](#soundIsOn) tells when it has.)

```js
let playing = 60;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startSound('synth/pluck');   // every key you play is heard
}

function mousePressed() {
  playing = 48 + floor(mouseX / 25);   // low on the left, high on the right
  midi.play(playing, 0.8);
}

function mouseReleased() {
  midi.play(playing, 0);
}

function draw() {
  background(soundIsOn ? 30 : 90);
  fill(255);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  text(soundIsOn ? 'click to play a note' : 'click once to turn sound on', width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `stopSound`, `OAVp5.sound.stop` (function, oav-p5): `stopSound()` — Turns sound off and lets every ringing note go; the instrument stays loaded, so `startSound()` brings it back at once.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startSound('synth/pluck');
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key === 's') {
    if (soundIsOn) stopSound(); else startSound();
  }
}

function draw() {
  background(soundIsOn ? 40 : 100);
  fill(255);
  text('press s: sound is ' + (soundIsOn ? 'on' : 'off'), width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `OAVp5.sound` (object, oav-p5): `OAVp5.sound` — The object behind the sound names: the state, the instrument, the error, the loading progress and the loaded parts of @openav/sound.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startSound('harp');
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  const s = OAVp5.sound;
  text('state: ' + s.state, 20, 30);
  text('instrument: ' + s.instrument, 20, 60);
  text('error: ' + s.error, 20, 90);
}
```

- `OAVp5.sound.error` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.sound.error` — The message of the last thing that went wrong while loading sound, or `null` when nothing has.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startSound('strings');
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
}

function draw() {
  background(OAVp5.sound.error ? color(120, 30, 30) : 20);
  fill(255);
  text(OAVp5.sound.error ? OAVp5.sound.error : 'no error', width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `OAVp5.sound.instrument` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.sound.instrument` — The id of the instrument you hear right now, or `null` before sound has loaded.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startSound('piano');
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(OAVp5.sound.instrument || 'nothing loaded yet', width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `OAVp5.sound.state` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.sound.state` — Where sound is: `'off'`, `'waiting'` (for a click), `'loading'`, `'on'` or `'error'`. (range off | waiting | loading | on | error)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startSound('marimba');
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(28);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  const hints = { off: 'off', loading: 'loading…', waiting: 'click to hear', on: 'listening', error: 'failed' };
  fill(255);
  text(hints[OAVp5.sound.state], width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `OAVp5.sound.status` (object, oav-p5): `OAVp5.sound.status` — How the instrument is loading: `{ id, state, progress, error }`, with `progress` from 0 to 1. (range { id, state: idle | loading | ready | error, progress: 0..1, error })

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startSound('piano');
  noStroke();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  const s = OAVp5.sound.status;
  fill(60);
  rect(40, 140, 320, 16);
  fill(120, 220, 140);
  rect(40, 140, 320 * s.progress, 16);
  fill(255);
  text(s.id + ': ' + s.state, 40, 120);
}
```

- `BUILTIN_INSTRUMENTS` (constant, @openav/sound): `BUILTIN_INSTRUMENTS = array, 22 items` — The 22 instruments that come with the package, as definitions: a grand piano, mallets, strings, harp, organ, choir and 11 synth presets.
- `CATEGORIES` (constant, @openav/sound): `CATEGORIES = array, 9 items` — The instrument categories in picker order: keys, mallets, strings, plucked, organ, voice, synth, drums and other.
- `DEFAULT_INSTRUMENT` (constant, @openav/sound): `DEFAULT_INSTRUMENT = "synth/pad"` — The instrument used when none is named: 'synth/pad', the warm three-saw pad that was the framework's first voice.
- `getInstrument` (function, @openav/sound): `getInstrument(id)` — Finds a registered instrument definition by its id, or null.
- `instrumentGroups` (function, @openav/sound): `instrumentGroups(lang = 'en', list = listInstruments())` — Groups the instruments by category in picker order: [{ id, label, items }], with empty groups left out.
- `instrumentName` (function, @openav/sound): `instrumentName(def, lang = 'en')` — Gives an instrument's display name in a language, falling back to English.
- `listInstruments` (function, @openav/sound): `listInstruments({ category = null } = {})` — Lists every registered instrument, in the order they were registered, or only the ones of one category.
- `modalInstrument` (function, @openav/sound): `modalInstrument({ id, name, category = 'mallets', credit = null, params, defaults = { cutoff: 8000 }, partials, strike = null, damp = 0, pitchDecay = 0.6, transpose = 0, gain = 0, attack = 0.0015, tremolo = null, maxVoices = 40, set = null, })` — Makes a struck-bar or tine instrument from data: a list of partials that ring and die away, and a short noise for the mallet.
- `mountSoundPicker` (function, @openav/sound): `mountSoundPicker(container, sound, { lang = (globalThis.document?.documentElement?.lang || 'en').toLowerCase().startsWith('zh') ? 'zh' : 'en', className = 'oav-sound-pick', label = null, enableOnPick = true, } = {})` — Puts an instrument menu on the page: one group per category, a loading bar for samplers and the credit line an instrument asks for.
- `onInstrumentsChange` (function, @openav/sound): `onInstrumentsChange(cb)` — Calls your function whenever an instrument is registered or removed, so a menu can refresh. Returns a function that stops listening.
- `registerInstrument` (function, @openav/sound): `registerInstrument(def, { replace = false } = {})` — Adds a sound to every picker on the page: an id, a name, a category and one create() function that builds the instrument.
- `registerSynthPreset` (function, @openav/sound): `registerSynthPreset(preset, opts)` — Adds a synth preset to every picker as synth/ plus its id: describe the voice, the envelope and the effects as data.
- `SALAMANDER_NOTES` (constant, @openav/sound): `SALAMANDER_NOTES = array, 30 items` — The 30 notes the Salamander piano has samples for: every minor third from A0 (MIDI 21) to C8 (108).
- `salamanderMap` (function, @openav/sound): `salamanderMap(notes = SALAMANDER_NOTES)` — Builds the sample map of the Salamander piano for Tone.Sampler: { 'A0': 'A0.mp3', 'D#1': 'Ds1.mp3', … }.
- `SAMPLES_URL` (constant, @openav/sound): `SAMPLES_URL = "https://openaudiovisual.com/packages/sound/samples/"` — The address of the folder with the built-in sample sets, when nobody says otherwise: openaudiovisual.com/packages/sound/samples/.
- `Sound` (class, @openav/sound): `new Sound({ signals, params = null, engine, instrument = null, remember = true, picker = true })` — Makes every midi/note/on and midi/note/off on a bus audible through a sound engine, and puts the engine's params on the bus as sound/*. (before it has a value: `sound.enable()` from a click: browsers start audio only after a user gesture. With [`toneEngine()`](#toneEngine) it also loads Tone.js from the network (jsDelivr) the first time. Before `enable()` nothing is heard, and the bus is not listened to.)
- `SOUND_PARAMS` (constant, @openav/sound): `SOUND_PARAMS = array, 3 items` — The three params every instrument shares: cutoff (the filter), space (the reverb) and volume.
- `soundOptions` (function, @openav/sound): `soundOptions(value)` — Reads the modules.sound option of createShow() (true, an instrument id, or an object) into one normalized object.
- `SYNTH_PRESETS` (constant, @openav/sound): `SYNTH_PRESETS = array, 11 items` — The 11 synth presets as plain data: pad, saw lead, square lead, pluck, supersaw, bass, acid, brass, bell, sub and chip.
- `synthInstrument` (function, @openav/sound): `synthInstrument(preset)` — Turns a synth preset into an instrument definition whose id is synth/ followed by the preset id, without registering it.
- `TONE_CDN` (constant, @openav/sound): `TONE_CDN = "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/tone@15.0.4/+esm"` — The address Tone.js is loaded from when the engine is enabled: Tone 15.0.4 on jsDelivr.
- `toneEngine` (function, @openav/sound): `toneEngine({ cdn = TONE_CDN, instrument = DEFAULT_INSTRUMENT, baseUrl = SAMPLES_URL, instruments: perInstrument = {}, drumChannel = 10, } = {})` — The sound engine that plays the registered instruments with Tone.js through a filter, a reverb and a limiter. (before it has a value: `await engine.enable()` from a click: it loads Tone.js from the network, then starts its audio. Before that, `noteOn()` does nothing and `setInstrument()` only remembers the choice.)
- `unregisterInstrument` (function, @openav/sound): `unregisterInstrument(id)` — Removes a registered sound, for tests and hot reload. Returns whether it was there.
- `validateInstrument` (function, @openav/sound): `validateInstrument(def)` — Checks an instrument definition and lists everything wrong with it as readable sentences. An empty list means it is valid.
- `validateSynthPreset` (function, @openav/sound): `validateSynthPreset(p)` — Checks a synth preset and lists what is wrong with it. An empty list means it is valid.

## drums

- `beatPhase`, `OAVp5.drums.beatPhase` (variable, oav-p5): `beatPhase` — How far through the current beat the drum machine is, smoothly from 0 up to just below 1, four times per bar. (range 0..1; before it has a value: Start the machine with [`startDrums()`](#startDrums); until it plays, `beatPhase` is 0.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('four on floor', 120);
  noStroke();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255, 120, 90);
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 60 + (1 - beatPhase) * 100);   // biggest on the beat
}
```

- `drawRhythm`, `OAVp5.drums.draw` (function, oav-p5): `drawRhythm([x], [y], [w], [h], [style], [o])` — Draws the rhythm on the canvas as a grid, a circle or a spiral, with a playhead and the hits lighting up, so a recording has it too. (before it has a value: Start the machine with [`startDrums()`](#startDrums) first. Before it plays you get an empty four-lane grid.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('breakbeat', 120);
}

function draw() {
  background(14, 16, 26);
  drawRhythm(20, 100, 360, 100);   // the 16 steps with a playhead
}
```

- `drumBpm`, `OAVp5.drums.bpm` (variable, oav-p5): `drumBpm` — The tempo of the drum machine in beats per minute. (range 30..300)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('four on floor', 100);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(32);
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (keyCode === UP_ARROW) startDrums(drumBpm + 5);
  if (keyCode === DOWN_ARROW) startDrums(drumBpm - 5);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(round(drumBpm) + ' bpm', width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `drumHit` (event, oav-p5): `function drumHit(lane, velocity) {}` — An event you define: it is called for every hit of the drum machine, with the drum that sounded and how hard.

```js
const COLORS = { kick: '#ff6b6b', snare: '#ffd166', hat: '#6fd3ff', clap: '#c792ff' };
const lit = { kick: 0, snare: 0, hat: 0, clap: 0 };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('breakbeat', 120);
  noStroke();
}

function drumHit(lane, velocity) {
  lit[lane] = velocity;
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  Object.keys(lit).forEach((lane, i) => {
    fill(COLORS[lane]);
    circle(60 + i * 93, height / 2, 30 + lit[lane] * 70);
    lit[lane] *= 0.85;
  });
}
```

- `drumPhase`, `OAVp5.drums.phase` (variable, oav-p5): `drumPhase` — How far through the current bar the drum machine is, smoothly from 0 up to just below 1, as it is heard. (range 0..1; before it has a value: Start the machine with [`startDrums()`](#startDrums); until it plays, `drumPhase` is 0.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('four on floor', 120);
  strokeWeight(4);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  stroke(255, 211, 107);
  translate(width / 2, height / 2);
  rotate(drumPhase * TWO_PI - HALF_PI);
  line(0, 0, 110, 0);   // a hand that turns once per bar
}
```

- `drumsAreOn` (variable, oav-p5): `drumsAreOn` — Whether the drum machine is playing right now. (before it has a value: It becomes true after [`startDrums()`](#startDrums) (or 🥁 in the 🎹 panel) has loaded the machine, usually within a fraction of a second.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('half time', 100);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(drumsAreOn ? color(120, 220, 140) : color(220, 160, 60));
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 80);
  fill(255);
  text(drumsAreOn ? 'drums are on' : 'drums are not running', width / 2, height - 40);
}
```

- `rhythmChanged` (event, oav-p5): `function rhythmChanged(src, how) {}` — An event you define: it is called with the new line of rhythm every time the rhythm changes.

```js
let current = '';
let how = '';

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('bd*4, [~ sd]*2, hh*8', 110);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
}

function rhythmChanged(src, mode) {
  current = src;
  how = mode;
}

function mousePressed() {
  OAVp5.drums.edit('bd(3,8), [~ sd]*2, hh*16');   // as if typed on the card
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(current, width / 2, height / 2 - 10);
  text('changed by: ' + how, width / 2, height / 2 + 20);
  text('click the canvas, or click a cell of the grid', width / 2, height - 30);
}
```

- `startDrums`, `OAVp5.drums.start` (function, oav-p5): `startDrums([pattern], [bpm])` — Starts a drum machine: a 16-step grid on the page that plays a preset, your own grid or one line of rhythm, and counts the bars for your sketch. (before it has a value: Nothing before the call. The counting, [`drumHit()`](#drumHit) and the other callbacks start at once, but a browser lets the page make sound only after a click or key press on it, so the drums are silent until the first one. A card at the top says so after a moment.)

```js
let swell = 0;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('breakbeat', 120);   // the grid appears at the top of the page
}

function kickDetected(level) {
  swell = 1;
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  swell *= 0.9;
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 60 + swell * 120);
}
```

- `stopDrums`, `OAVp5.drums.stop` (function, oav-p5): `stopDrums()` — Stops the drum machine and hides its card.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('four on floor', 120);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
}

function mousePressed() {
  stopDrums();
}

function draw() {
  background(drumsAreOn ? 40 : 100);
  fill(255);
  text(drumsAreOn ? 'click to stop the drums' : 'stopped at step ' + drumStep, width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `OAVp5.drums` (object, oav-p5): `OAVp5.drums` — The object behind the drum names: the state of the machine, its counters, the line of rhythm, its history and the loaded machine.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('latin', 110);
  textSize(14);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  const d = OAVp5.drums;
  text('state: ' + d.state, 20, 30);
  text('pattern: ' + d.pattern, 20, 60);
  text('bar ' + d.bar + ', step ' + d.step + ', count ' + d.count, 20, 90);
  text('bpm: ' + d.bpm, 20, 120);
}
```

- `OAVp5.drums.copyText` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.drums.copyText` — The text the Copy button on the card puts on the clipboard: the rhythm that plays now as a ready `startDrums("…", bpm)` call.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('breakbeat', 120);
  textSize(12);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(OAVp5.drums.copyText, 20, 20, width - 40, 200);
}
```

- `OAVp5.drums.edit` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.drums.edit(text)` — Plays a line of rhythm as if it was typed on the card, and returns whether it worked and, if not, what is wrong with it. (before it has a value: The machine and the rhythm module must have loaded: call [`startDrums()`](#startDrums) first and give it a moment.)

```js
const TRIES = ['bd*4, hh*8', 'bd(3,8), [~ sd]*2', 'bd*4, xyz*8'];
let n = 0;
let result = '';

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('bd*4, [~ sd]*2, hh*8', 110);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
}

function mousePressed() {
  const r = OAVp5.drums.edit(TRIES[n % TRIES.length]);
  result = r.ok ? 'ok: ' + r.text : 'wrong: ' + r.error.message;
  n++;
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('click to try the next line', width / 2, 40);
  text(result, width / 2, height / 2 - 10);
  text('playing: ' + OAVp5.drums.src, width / 2, height / 2 + 30);
}
```

- `OAVp5.drums.history` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.drums.history` — The earlier lines of rhythm, oldest first: every click on a cell, typed line or menu pick leaves the line before it here.

```js
const LINES = ['bd*4, hh*8', 'bd(3,8), hh*8', 'bd ~ ~ bd, [~ sd]*2, hh*16'];
let n = 0;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums(LINES[0], 110);
  textSize(14);
}

function mousePressed() {
  n = (n + 1) % LINES.length;
  OAVp5.drums.edit(LINES[n]);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('click to edit the line', 20, 30);
  text('history: ' + OAVp5.drums.history.length + ' earlier lines', 20, 60);
  text(OAVp5.drums.history.join('\n'), 20, 90);
}
```

- `OAVp5.drums.now` (object, oav-p5): `OAVp5.drums.now` — A snapshot of what the machine hears right now: the bar, the step, both phases and which words of the line are lit. (range { bar, step, phase, beatPhase, tokens, mode, text })

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('bd*4, [~ sd]*2, hh*8', 80);
  textFont('monospace');
  textSize(18);
  noStroke();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  const n = OAVp5.drums.now;
  fill(255, 211, 107);
  for (const t of n.tokens) {
    rect(20 + textWidth(n.text.slice(0, t.start)), 150, textWidth(n.text.slice(t.start, t.end)), 3);   // underline the sounding words
  }
  fill(255);
  text(n.text, 20, 140);
}
```

- `OAVp5.drums.on` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.drums.on(name, fn)` — Listens to the drum machine from anywhere: `OAVp5.drums.on('hit', fn)` calls `fn` like `drumHit` does, and returns a function that stops listening.

```js
let bars = 0;
let off = null;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('four on floor', 160);
  off = OAVp5.drums.on('bar', (bar) => { bars++; });   // returns a function that stops it
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
}

function mousePressed() {
  if (off) { off(); off = null; }   // stop counting
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('bars counted: ' + bars, width / 2, height / 2);
  text(off ? 'click to stop counting' : 'stopped', width / 2, height / 2 + 30);
}
```

- `OAVp5.drums.pattern` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.drums.pattern` — What the drum machine plays, as a name: the preset's name, `'custom'` for a grid, or the line of rhythm itself.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('breakbeat', 110);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(24);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(OAVp5.drums.pattern, width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `OAVp5.drums.src` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.drums.src` — The line of rhythm that plays now, such as `'bd*4, [~ sd]*2, hh*8'`; an empty string until the machine has loaded. (before it has a value: It is `''` until [`startDrums()`](#startDrums) has loaded the machine and the rhythm module, a fraction of a second.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('half time', 100);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(OAVp5.drums.src || 'loading…', width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `OAVp5.drums.state` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.drums.state` — Where the drum machine is: `'off'`, `'loading'`, `'on'`, `'stopped'` or `'error'`. (range off | loading | on | stopped | error)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('sparse', 90);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(28);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(OAVp5.drums.state, width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `OAVp5.drums.strudelUrl` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.drums.strudelUrl` — The rhythm that plays now as a link that opens it at strudel.cc, or an empty string when there is none.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('bd*4, [~ sd]*2, hh*8', 110);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
}

function mousePressed() {
  if (OAVp5.drums.strudelUrl) window.open(OAVp5.drums.strudelUrl, '_blank');
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('click to open this rhythm in strudel.cc', width / 2, height / 2 - 15);
  text(OAVp5.drums.strudelUrl.slice(0, 40) + '…', width / 2, height / 2 + 15);
}
```

- `OAVp5.drums.undo` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.drums.undo()` — Goes back one line of rhythm, like ↶ on the card; returns `true` if there was an earlier line.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('bd*4, hh*8', 110);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
}

function mousePressed() {
  OAVp5.drums.edit('bd(3,8), hh*16');
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key === 'z') OAVp5.drums.undo();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(OAVp5.drums.src, width / 2, height / 2 - 10);
  text('click: change the line   z: undo', width / 2, height / 2 + 20);
}
```

- `drumEngine` (function, @openav/drums): `drumEngine({ samples = null } = {})` — A drum kit made of Web Audio synthesis, with no sample files: General MIDI drum notes go in, drum sounds come out. (before it has a value: `await kit.enable()` from a click: browsers start audio only after a user gesture. [`mountDrums()`](#mountDrums) and [`DrumTransport`](#DrumTransport) with `autoEnable` do that for you on the first hit.)
- `drumName` (function, @openav/drums): `drumName(voice, lang = 'en')` — The name of a drum for the screen, in English or in Chinese: `drumName('lowtom')` is `'low tom'`.
- `DrumScheduler` (class, @openav/drums): `new DrumScheduler({ bpm = 112, swing = 0, humanize = 0.35, lookahead = 0.1, pattern = 'four on floor', seed = 0, random = Math.random } = {})` — Pure drum logic with no timers and no audio: a grid or a line of rhythm goes in, timed events come out, ahead of time, on any clock you pass.
- `DrumSequencer` (class, @openav/drums): `new DrumSequencer({ onHit, onStep = null, bpm = 112, swing = 0.12, humanize = 0.35, pattern = 'four on floor' } = {})` — A 16-step, four-lane drum pattern clock that you move forward with `update(dt)` every frame and that calls your function for each hit.
- `DrumTransport` (class, @openav/drums): `new DrumTransport({ scheduler = new DrumScheduler(), engine = null, onStep = null, onHit = null, onLate = null, autoEnable = false, now = perfNow, hidden = pageHidden, heartbeat = 'auto', tick = 0.025, latency = 'auto', stale = 0.25, startDelay = 0.05 } = {})` — The runtime around a DrumScheduler: it hands every hit to the kit ahead of time on its audio clock, and tells the page each step and hit when it is heard.
- `GM` (constant, @openav/drums): `GM = object, 13 keys` — The General MIDI drum note each drum of the kit plays: `GM.kick` is 36, `GM.snare` is 38.
- `laneSteps` (function, @openav/drums): `laneSteps(v)` — Turns a lane written as text, like 'x...x...x...x...', or as a list into 16 steps of 0 and 1.
- `mountDrums` (function, @openav/drums): `mountDrums(container, { signals, engine = null, autoEnableEngine = true, onStep = null, onHit = null, onTakeover = null, bpm = 112, pattern = 'four on floor', clock = 'frame', lang = 'en', heartbeat = 'auto', latency = 'auto', now, hidden, rhythm = null, onRhythm = null, onLossy = null, onEditError = null, copyText = null, strudelComment = '' } = {})` — Puts a drum machine on the page: a step grid, a transport and a line of rhythm you can type into. It publishes every hit as `drum/*` signals. (before it has a value: A page with a DOM, and `update(dt)` called every frame. Sound waits for the browser: the kit's `AudioContext` is made by the first hit (or by `play()` with the lookahead clock), and until the page has had a click it stays suspended. Callbacks and signals run from the start; the sound comes in on the first click, and nothing from before it is played late.)
- `PATTERNS` (constant, @openav/drums): `PATTERNS = object, 5 keys` — The five preset grids of the drum machine: 'four on floor', breakbeat, 'half time', latin and sparse.
- `voiceForNote` (function, @openav/drums): `voiceForNote(note)` — Tells which drum of the kit a General MIDI drum note plays, or `null` for a note it does not play.
- `compile` (function, @openav/pattern): `compile(src, { words = WORDS } = {})` — Reads one line of rhythm text, like 'bd*4, [~ sd]*2, hh*8', and gives back the drum hits of any bar you ask for. It never throws.
- `euclid` (function, @openav/pattern): `euclid(pulses, steps, rotate = 0)` — Spreads a number of hits as evenly as possible over a number of steps, the Euclidean rhythm. `euclid(3, 8)` is the tresillo.
- `fromGrid` (function, @openav/pattern): `fromGrid(grid, { steps = 16, words = null, order = null } = {})` — Turns a grid of steps, like the drum machine card, into the one line of rhythm a person would write for it.
- `fromStrudel` (function, @openav/pattern): `fromStrudel(code)` — Reads code copied from strudel.cc, like `s("bd*4").fast(2)`, into the line of rhythm OAV plays, plus the tempo it found.
- `parse` (function, @openav/pattern): `parse(src)` — Reads a line of rhythm into a tree of nodes, each with its character range. It does not look words up in the drum kit.
- `SHORT` (constant, @openav/pattern): `SHORT = object, 13 keys` — The short word Tidal and Strudel write for each drum: `kick` is `bd`, `snare` is `sd`. The other direction from `WORDS`.
- `strudelUrl` (function, @openav/pattern): `strudelUrl(src, opts = {})` — Makes a strudel.cc link that opens the line of rhythm in the Strudel editor.
- `toGrid` (function, @openav/pattern): `toGrid(p, { bar = 1, steps = 16, seed = 0, bars = 16, words = WORDS } = {})` — Shows one bar of a line of rhythm on a grid of steps, and tells you what the grid cannot hold.
- `toStrudel` (function, @openav/pattern): `toStrudel(src, { bpm = null, comment = '', words = WORDS } = {})` — Turns a line of rhythm into Strudel code: OAV's drum words become Strudel's, with a tempo line and a comment if you give them.
- `WORDS` (constant, @openav/pattern): `WORDS = object, 26 keys` — The drum words a line of rhythm may use and the drum each one plays: `bd` is `kick`, `sd` is `snare`, `hh` is `hat`.

## timeline

- `barStarted` (event, oav-p5): `function barStarted(bar) {}` — An event you define: it is called at the first step of every bar of the drum machine, with the bar number.

```js
let shade = 200;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  colorMode(HSB, 360, 100, 100);
  startDrums('four on floor', 150);
}

function barStarted(bar) {
  shade = (shade + 40) % 360;   // a new colour every bar
}

function draw() {
  background(shade, 60, 80);
  fill(0, 0, 100);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(48);
  text(drumBar, width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `cue` (function, oav-p5): `cue(bar, name, [every])` — Plans something for a bar: at bar `bar` the function `cueFired(name, bar)` is called and `cueName` becomes `name`; with `every`, again every that many bars.

```js
let scene = 'calm';

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('four on floor', 140);
  cue(1, 'calm', 4);    // bars 1, 5, 9 ...
  cue(3, 'storm', 4);   // bars 3, 7, 11 ...
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(32);
}

function cueFired(name, bar) {
  scene = name;
}

function draw() {
  background(scene === 'storm' ? color(130, 30, 40) : color(20, 40, 100));
  fill(255);
  text(scene + ' (bar ' + drumBar + ')', width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `cueFired` (event, oav-p5): `function cueFired(name, bar) {}` — An event you define: it is called when the bar of a cue declared with `cue()` has come, with the cue's name and the bar.

```js
let scene = '-';
let when = 0;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('four on floor', 150);
  cue(1, 'intro');
  cue(3, 'verse', 4);
  cue(5, 'chorus', 4);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(32);
}

function cueFired(name, bar) {
  scene = name + ' (bar ' + bar + ')';
  when = millis();
}

function draw() {
  background(20 + max(0, 1 - (millis() - when) / 400) * 120);   // a flash on every cue
  fill(255);
  text(scene, width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `cueName`, `OAVp5.drums.lastCue` (variable, oav-p5): `cueName` — The name of the last cue that fired, or an empty string before the first one. (range '' or a cue name)

```js
const SCENES = { calm: '#3b5bdb', bloom: '#e64980', storm: '#495057' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('breakbeat', 150);
  cue(1, 'calm', 6);
  cue(3, 'bloom', 6);
  cue(5, 'storm', 6);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(32);
}

function draw() {
  background(SCENES[cueName] || '#111');   // nothing yet: dark
  fill(255);
  text(cueName, width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `drumBar`, `OAVp5.drums.bar` (variable, oav-p5): `drumBar` — Which bar the drum machine is in, counted from 1 when it started. (range 0, 1, 2, 3 …; before it has a value: Start the machine with [`startDrums()`](#startDrums). Stopping and starting again counts from bar 1 again.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('four on floor', 150);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(64);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(drumBar, width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `drumStep`, `OAVp5.drums.step` (variable, oav-p5): `drumStep` — Which of the 16 steps of the bar the drum machine just played, from 0 to 15. (range 0..15; before it has a value: Start the machine with [`startDrums()`](#startDrums). Before that, and when the machine is stopped, the value is 0 or the last one, so check [`drumsAreOn`](#drumsAreOn) if the difference matters.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('four on floor', 120);
  noStroke();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  for (let i = 0; i < 16; i++) {
    fill(drumsAreOn && i === drumStep ? 255 : 70);
    rect(20 + i * 22, 130, 18, 40);   // sixteen cells, the current one lights up
  }
}
```

- `stepStarted` (event, oav-p5): `function stepStarted(step, bar) {}` — An event you define: it is called at every one of the 16 steps of the drum machine, with the step and the bar.

```js
let ping = 0;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('breakbeat', 120);
  noStroke();
}

function stepStarted(step, bar) {
  if (step % 4 === 0) ping = 1;   // on every beat
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  ping *= 0.9;
  fill(255, 160, 80);
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 40 + ping * 120);
}
```

- `OAVp5.drums.count` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.drums.count` — How many steps the drum machine has played since it started, from 0; -1 before the first one. (range -1, 0, 1, 2 …; before it has a value: Start the machine with [`startDrums()`](#startDrums); it is -1 until the first step has played.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('half time', 140);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(28);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  const n = OAVp5.drums.count;
  text('step ' + n + '  =  bar ' + (floor(n / 16) + 1) + ', step ' + (n % 16), width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `OAVp5.drums.cue` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.drums.cue(bar, name, [every])` — The same as `cue(bar, name, every)`, but it returns the cue it made (or the one that was already there), and `null` when `bar` is not valid.

```js
let c = null;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('four on floor', 120);
  c = OAVp5.drums.cue(3.5, 'half', 4);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(c ? 'cue "' + c.name + '" at step ' + c.at + ', every ' + c.period + ' steps' : 'no cue', width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `OAVp5.drums.cues` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.drums.cues` — The list of every cue declared so far, in the order they were declared.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('four on floor', 120);
  cue(1, 'calm', 8);
  cue(5, 'storm', 8);
  textSize(14);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  OAVp5.drums.cues.forEach((c, i) => {
    text('bar ' + c.bar + (c.every ? ' (every ' + c.every + ')' : '') + ': ' + c.name, 20, 30 + i * 24);
  });
}
```

- `Director` (class, @openav/score): `new Director({ score, modules = [], api = {}, onStatus = null, onCue = null, maxStep = 2 } = {})` — Runs a score's segment modules: enters each once, updates it every frame, exits it once, fires cues, and switches off a module that crashes without stopping the show.
- `Score` (class, @openav/score): `new Score({ cuts, cut } = {})` — A show written as segments with lengths, never as absolute seconds: it works out every start, end, cue and countdown, for every version (cut) of the show.
- `ScoreError` (class, @openav/score): `new ScoreError(problems)` — The error a Score throws when it cannot be built: its `problems` array lists every reason at once, and its message lists them too.
- `CURVES` (constant, @openav/timeline): `CURVES = object, 5 keys` — The curve names a keyframe can use to say how its segment gets there: `linear`, `ease`, `in`, `out`, `step`, each a function from 0..1 to 0..1.
- `HOLD_EPS` (constant, @openav/timeline): `HOLD_EPS = 0.000001` — How far before the boundary the playhead parks when a hold stops the show: one microsecond, so it still belongs to the scene that is waiting.
- `Timeline` (class, @openav/timeline): `new Timeline({ params, automation = {}, scenes = [], total = 600, score = null, start = null, loop = false, onCue = null })` — Answers "what is every param at time t?" from keyframes, and runs the transport around it: play, seek, scenes, holds, loops, cues and recording. (before it has a value: Time only moves when you call `play()` and then `advance(dt)` every frame (a show does this for you). `state(t)` and `valueAt(key, t)` work at any moment, playing or not. The callbacks do not fire for the starting scene until the first `advance()` or `seek()`.)

## chop

- `count`, `OAVp5.chop.count` (function, oav-p5): `count(on, [limit], [name])` — Counts how often `on` has turned on, or how many `'kick'` (or any other event) have happened; with a limit it loops 0, 1, … limit − 1. (before it has a value: The event names work like [`env()`](#env): `'kick'`, `'snare'`, `'hat'` and `'beat'` come from the microphone, or from the drum machine once [`startDrums()`](#startDrums) has been called, and the first `count('kick')` asks for the microphone if the drum machine is not on. The first call loads @openav/chop, which takes a few frames.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(96);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(count(mouseIsPressed), width / 2, height / 2);   // clicks so far
}
```

- `drawTrail`, `OAVp5.chop.drawTrail` (function, oav-p5): `drawTrail(values, [x], [y], [w], [h], [lo], [hi], [name])` — Draws a line through `values` on the canvas, so it is in the work and in a recording: the oldest at `x`, `lo` at the bottom of the box, `hi` at the top. (before it has a value: Call it in `draw()` after `createCanvas()`. With a number, the first call loads @openav/chop, which takes a few frames, and nothing is drawn until then.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  const wave = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(frameCount * 0.05);
  stroke(255, 211, 107);
  strokeWeight(2);
  drawTrail(wave, 20, 100, width - 40, 100);   // a number: keeps its own 2 seconds
}
```

- `env`, `OAVp5.chop.env` (function, oav-p5): `env([event], [attack], [decay], [name])` — A 0..1 pulse that jumps up after each event (a kick, a beat, a key, a press) and then fades out: TouchDesigner's Trigger CHOP. (before it has a value: `'kick'`, `'snare'`, `'hat'` and `'beat'` need something that makes them. If the sketch has not started the drum machine ([`startDrums()`](#startDrums)), the first `env('kick')` asks for the microphone, like reading [`micLevel`](#micLevel), and `?oav_mic=off` means nothing ever fires.
