Once the drum machine is started, the microphone is not opened for it. `'note'` needs a key: play one, press 🎹, or call [`OAVp5.play()`](#OAVp5.play). A name of your own needs [`trigger()`](#trigger): if nothing fires it within 4 seconds, a card says so.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  const k = env(mouseIsPressed, 0.02, 0.5);   // 1 right after each press, then it fades
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 60 + k * 200);
}
```

- `lag`, `OAVp5.chop.lag` (function, oav-p5): `lag(value, [up], [down], [name])` — Follows `value` smoothly instead of jumping: up in `up` seconds, down in `down` seconds (TouchDesigner's Lag CHOP). (before it has a value: Nothing to call or declare: write it in `draw()`. The first call loads @openav/chop from next to oav-p5.js, which takes a few frames.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  const x = lag(mouseX, 0.5);   // follows the mouse, half a second behind
  circle(x, height / 2, 40);
}
```

- `scope`, `OAVp5.chop.scope` (function, oav-p5): `scope(value, [label])` — Shows `value` in a small oscilloscope in the corner of the page and gives it back, so you can wrap any expression to watch it. (before it has a value: Only inside `draw()`: anywhere else it just returns `value`. `?oav_scope=off` hides it, and so does `?oav_hints=off`, which is the one thing to know if it does not appear. See [`scope`](#option-scope). The first call loads @openav/chop, which takes a few frames.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  const wave = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(frameCount * 0.05);
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 40 + scope(wave, 'wave') * 200);   // watch it in the corner
}
```

- `slope`, `OAVp5.chop.slope` (function, oav-p5): `slope(value, [name])` — How fast `value` is changing, per second: positive while it rises, negative while it falls, 0 while it holds still (TouchDesigner's Slope CHOP). (before it has a value: Nothing to call or declare: write it in `draw()`. The first call loads @openav/chop, which takes a few frames.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textSize(16);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  const v = abs(slope(mouseX));   // pixels per second
  fill(255);
  text(nf(v, 1, 0) + ' px/s', 20, 120);
  rect(20, 140, min(v / 10, width - 40), 24);
}
```

- `speed`, `OAVp5.chop.speed` (function, oav-p5): `speed(rate, [name])` — Adds `rate` to a running total every second, so `rotate(speed(TWO_PI))` turns once a second and the rate can change without the total ever jumping. (before it has a value: Nothing to call or declare: write it in `draw()`. The first call loads @openav/chop, which takes a few frames.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  rectMode(CENTER);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  translate(width / 2, height / 2);
  rotate(speed(TWO_PI));   // one turn a second
  rect(0, 0, 120, 120);
}
```

- `spring`, `OAVp5.chop.spring` (function, oav-p5): `spring(value, [stiffness], [damping], [name])` — Follows `value` like a mass on a spring: it overshoots, bounces and settles (TouchDesigner's Spring CHOP). (before it has a value: Nothing to call or declare: write it in `draw()`. The first call loads @openav/chop, which takes a few frames.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  const size = spring(mouseIsPressed ? 300 : 100, 100, 6);   // overshoots, then settles
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, size);
}
```

- `trail`, `OAVp5.chop.trail` (function, oav-p5): `trail(value, [seconds], [name])` — The last few seconds of `value` as an array, 60 values a second, oldest first and newest last (TouchDesigner's Trail CHOP). (before it has a value: Nothing to call or declare: write it in `draw()`. The first call loads @openav/chop, which takes a few frames.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  const wave = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(frameCount * 0.05);   // 0..1
  stroke(255);
  drawTrail(trail(wave, 3), 20, 100, width - 40, 100);   // the last 3 seconds
}
```

- `trigger`, `OAVp5.chop.trigger` (function, oav-p5): `trigger([name])` — Fires an event of your own, by name, for [`env()`](#env) and [`count()`](#count) to react to.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function mousePressed() {
  trigger('boom');   // an event of our own
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  const k = env('boom', 0.01, 0.6);
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 60 + k * 220);
}
```

- `OAVp5.chop` (object, oav-p5): `OAVp5.chop` — The CHOP functions under one roof, plus the state of the module behind them: `OAVp5.chop.lag(…)`, `.state`, `.slots()`, `.reset()`.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  const x = OAVp5.chop.lag(mouseX, 0.4);   // the same as lag(mouseX, 0.4)
  fill(255);
  text('chop ' + OAVp5.chop.state + ', ' + OAVp5.chop.slots().length + ' memory in use', 20, 30);
  circle(x, height / 2, 40);
}
```

- `OAVp5.chop.module` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.chop.module` — The @openav/chop module itself once it has loaded, otherwise `null`: the classes and functions the CHOP functions are built on.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  lag(mouseX, 0.3, 0.3, 'warm-up');   // the first call loads the module
  const m = OAVp5.chop.module;
  fill(255);
  text(m ? 'spring defaults: ' + JSON.stringify(m.DEFAULTS.spring) : 'not loaded yet', 20, 30);
}
```

- `OAVp5.chop.reset` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.chop.reset([name])` — Forgets the memory named `name` (a lag, a speed total, a count …), or every memory when you give no name: the next call starts fresh.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function mousePressed() {
  OAVp5.chop.reset('spin');   // forget the named speed
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  translate(width / 2, height / 2);
  rotate(speed(1, 'spin'));
  rect(-40, -40, 80, 80);
}
```

- `OAVp5.chop.slots` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.chop.slots()` — Lists every memory the CHOP functions are using right now: its kind, how it is found, and its latest value.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textSize(14);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  lag(mouseX, 0.3);
  lag(mouseY, 0.3);
  spring(mouseX, 100, 6, 'ball');
  fill(255);
  const lines = OAVp5.chop.slots().map((s) => s.kind + ' ' + s.key + ' (' + s.mode + ')');
  text(lines.join('\n'), 20, 30);
}
```

- `OAVp5.chop.state` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.chop.state` — Where the @openav/chop module is: `'off'`, `'loading'`, `'on'` or `'error'`. (range 'off' | 'loading' | 'on' | 'error')

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('chop: ' + OAVp5.chop.state, 20, 30);   // off, then loading, then on
  if (frameCount > 30) circle(lag(mouseX, 0.3), height / 2, 30);   // the first lag() loads the module
}
```

- `approach` (function, @openav/chop): `approach(current, target, seconds, dt)` — One step of a one-pole lag: moves `current` toward `target`, closing 63% of the gap after `seconds`. (before it has a value: Nothing. It is pure arithmetic with no memory: you keep `current` yourself and pass in the seconds since the last call. For a value with its own memory use [`Lag`](#Lag).)
- `Count` (class, @openav/chop): `new Count({ threshold = 0.5 } = {})` — Counts how many times its input turned on (true, or a number above `threshold`); with a limit it loops 0 … limit − 1. The Count CHOP. (before it has a value: Nothing to load. Call `step` every frame, even while the input is off: it has to see the "off" to notice the next "on". It has no `dt`, because a count does not depend on time.)
- `DEFAULTS` (constant, @openav/chop): `DEFAULTS = object, 5 keys` — The default settings of every CHOP in the package, as one frozen object: lag, envelope, spring, trail and count.
- `envelope` (function, @openav/chop): `envelope(times, t, attack = 0.01, decay = 0.3, peak = 1)` — The level, 0 to `peak`, of an attack-and-decay envelope at time `t`, for events that happened at the given `times`; the Trigger CHOP. (before it has a value: Nothing to load. You record the event times yourself (for example `kicks.push(performance.now() / 1000)` when a kick arrives) and pass the same clock as `t`.)
- `envelopeStage` (function, @openav/chop): `envelopeStage(elapsed, attack, decay, from = 0, peak = 1)` — The level of one envelope `elapsed` seconds after its trigger: a straight rise to `peak`, then a fall to 0 in `decay` seconds.
- `Lag` (class, @openav/chop): `new Lag({ up = 0.1, down = up, value = null } = {})` — Follows its input with one speed while the input is above the output and another while it is below; the TouchDesigner Lag CHOP. (before it has a value: Nothing to load or start. Pass the seconds since the previous frame as `dt` (in a browser: the difference of two `performance.now() / 1000`). The first `step` only stores the input, so the output equals the input on frame one.)
- `Slope` (class, @openav/chop): `new Slope()` — How fast the input is changing, in units per second; 0 on the first step. The Slope CHOP. (before it has a value: Nothing to load. The first `step` only stores the value and returns 0, because there is no earlier value to compare with.)
- `Speed` (class, @openav/chop): `new Speed({ value = 0 } = {})` — Adds `rate` every second to a running total: a rate in units per second becomes a position; the Speed CHOP. (before it has a value: Nothing to load. Pass the seconds since the previous frame as `dt`.)
- `Spring` (class, @openav/chop): `new Spring({ stiffness = 100, damping = 6, value = null } = {})` — Follows its input like a mass on a spring: it overshoots, swings back and settles; the Spring CHOP with the input as position. (before it has a value: Nothing to load. Pass the seconds since the previous frame as `dt`. The first `step` only stores the input (the spring starts at rest on it).)
- `springStep` (function, @openav/chop): `springStep(x, v, target, stiffness, damping, dt)` — One exact step of a damped spring of mass 1 pulled toward `target`; returns `[position, velocity]`.
- `TD_LAG_RATIO` (constant, @openav/chop): `TD_LAG_RATIO = 2.302585092994046` — `Math.LN10`, about 2.303: how many time constants a lag needs to cover 90% of a jump, which is what TouchDesigner's Lag seconds mean.
- `Trail` (class, @openav/chop): `new Trail({ seconds = 2, rate = 60 } = {})` — Remembers the input over the last few seconds as a list of values, oldest first, at a fixed 60 values a second; the Trail CHOP. (before it has a value: Nothing to load. Pass the seconds since the previous frame as `dt`. A value that is not a number leaves the history as it is and returns the current list.)
- `wrapCount` (function, @openav/chop): `wrapCount(total, limit)` — Loops a count to 0 … limit − 1: `wrapCount(5, 4)` is 1. A limit of 0 or less leaves the count as it is.

## record

- `recordingIsOn` (variable, oav-p5): `recordingIsOn` — Whether a recording is running right now.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textSize(16);
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key === 'r') recordingIsOn ? stopRecording() : startRecording();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255, 120, 90);
  circle(200 + sin(frameCount * 0.05) * 120, 150, 50);
  if (!recordingIsOn) {   // the guide never reaches the video
    fill(255);
    text('r: start / stop recording', 20, 30);
  }
}
```

- `recordingSaved` (event, oav-p5): `function recordingSaved(info) {}` — An event you define: it is called when a recording has been saved and checked, with an `info` object about the file.

```js
let saved = '';

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key === 'r') startRecording(3);
}

function recordingSaved(info) {
  saved = info.name + '  ' + info.format + '  ' + info.seconds + ' s  ' + round(info.bytes / 1024) + ' KB';
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  circle(200 + sin(frameCount * 0.05) * 120, 150, 50);
  if (!recordingIsOn) {
    fill(255);
    text(saved || 'press r to record 3 seconds', 20, 30);
  }
}
```

- `startRecording`, `OAVp5.record.start` (function, oav-p5): `startRecording([o])` — Records the canvas and the sound your sketch makes into one video file, and returns a promise that says whether the recording began. (before it has a value: A browser that has `MediaRecorder`: where it is missing, a card says so and the promise resolves to `false`. The picture is recorded at once, but the page can only make sound after a click or key press on it, so a take that begins before the first one has nothing to hear at first. A canvas that shows an image from another site (no CORS) cannot be recorded, and a card says so.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key === 'r') startRecording(5);   // five seconds, then it stops and downloads
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  circle(200 + sin(frameCount * 0.05) * 120, 150, 50);
  if (!recordingIsOn) {
    fill(255);
    text('press r to record 5 seconds', 20, 30);   // not drawn while recording
  }
}
```

- `stopRecording`, `OAVp5.record.stop` (function, oav-p5): `stopRecording()` — Stops the recording; the video is finished, downloaded, and handed to `recordingSaved(info)` and to the returned promise.

```js
let message = 'press r to record, r again to stop';

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key !== 'r') return;
  if (recordingIsOn) {
    stopRecording().then((info) => {
      if (info) message = 'saved ' + info.name;   // the file is ready
    });
  } else {
    startRecording();
  }
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  circle(200 + sin(frameCount * 0.05) * 120, 150, 50);
  if (!recordingIsOn) {
    fill(255);
    text(message, 20, 30);
  }
}
```

- `OAVp5.record` (object, oav-p5): `OAVp5.record` — The object behind the recording names: the state, the time, the last file, the formats this browser can write and the screenshot function.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textSize(14);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  const r = OAVp5.record;
  text('state: ' + r.state, 20, 30);
  text('seconds: ' + nf(r.seconds, 1, 1), 20, 60);
  text('limit: ' + r.limit + ' s at ' + r.fps + ' fps', 20, 90);
}
```

- `OAVp5.record.formats` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.record.formats()` — Says what this browser can record: `{ recorder, mp4, webm, mime }`.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textSize(14);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  const f = OAVp5.record.formats();
  text('recorder: ' + f.recorder, 20, 30);
  text('mp4: ' + f.mp4 + '   webm: ' + f.webm, 20, 60);
  text('asks for: ' + (f.mime || 'nothing'), 20, 90);
}
```

- `OAVp5.record.fps`, `OAVp5.record.limit` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.record.fps` — The frame rate (`fps`) and the longest take in seconds (`limit`) that the loading options `recfps` and `reclimit` set. (range fps 1..60, limit 1 …)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textSize(14);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('a take is ' + OAVp5.record.fps + ' frames a second', 20, 30);
  text('and at most ' + OAVp5.record.limit + ' seconds (' + OAVp5.record.limit / 60 + ' minutes)', 20, 60);
}
```

- `OAVp5.record.last` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.record.last` — The `info` of the last recording that was saved (the same object `recordingSaved` got), or `null` before the first one.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textSize(14);
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key === 'r') startRecording(2);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  const last = OAVp5.record.last;
  text(last ? 'last file: ' + last.name + ' (' + last.seconds + ' s)' : 'nothing recorded yet, press r', 20, 30);
}
```

- `OAVp5.record.on` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.record.on(name, fn)` — Listens to the recording from anywhere: `OAVp5.record.on('saved', fn)` or `on('start', fn)`, and it returns a function that stops listening.

```js
let status = 'press r to record 2 seconds';

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  OAVp5.record.on('start', (i) => { status = 'recording ' + i.width + 'x' + i.height + ' at ' + i.fps + ' fps'; });
  OAVp5.record.on('saved', (i) => { status = 'saved ' + i.name; });
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key === 'r') startRecording(2);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  circle(200 + sin(frameCount * 0.05) * 120, 150, 50);
  if (!recordingIsOn) {
    fill(255);
    text(status, 20, 30);
  }
}
```

- `OAVp5.record.seconds` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.record.seconds` — How long the running take has been going, in seconds, and the length of the last take after it. (range 0 …)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key === 'r') startRecording(4);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  const t = recordingIsOn ? OAVp5.record.seconds : 0;   // 0 at the first frame of the video
  fill(255, 160, 80);
  circle(40 + t * 80, 150, 40);                         // slides right, 80 px a second
  if (!recordingIsOn) {
    fill(255);
    text('press r: the video starts with the circle at the left', 20, 30);
  }
}
```

- `OAVp5.record.shot` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.record.shot([o])` — Saves the canvas alone as a PNG picture (not the 🎹, not the cards) and downloads it.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key === 'p') OAVp5.record.shot({ name: 'still' });
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  circle(mouseX, mouseY, 60);
  fill(255);
  text('press p to save a PNG of the canvas', 20, 30);
}
```

- `OAVp5.record.sources` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.record.sources` — Which sounds the running take is hearing right now: a list of `'sound'`, `'drums'`, `'mic'` and `'p5sound'`; empty when no take runs.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('breakbeat', 120);
  startSound('synth/pluck');
  textSize(14);
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key === 'r') recordingIsOn ? stopRecording() : startRecording();
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(recordingIsOn ? 'in the take: ' + OAVp5.record.sources.join(', ') : 'press r to start a take', 20, 30);
}
```

- `OAVp5.record.state` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.record.state` — Where the recording is: `'off'`, `'starting'`, `'on'` or `'saving'`. (range off | starting | on | saving)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(28);
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key === 'r' && OAVp5.record.state === 'off') startRecording(3);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  circle(200 + sin(frameCount * 0.05) * 120, 220, 40);
  fill(255);
  text(OAVp5.record.state === 'off' ? 'press r' : OAVp5.record.state, width / 2, 70);
}
```

- `AUDIO_MIMES` (constant, @openav/record): `AUDIO_MIMES = array, 5 items` — The audio MIME types the recorder tries for a sound-only file, best first: AAC in .m4a, then Opus.
- `AudioTap` (class, @openav/record): `new AudioTap({ context = null, sources = [], captureDestination = false } = {})` — Collects the sound of your work (and, if you add it, a microphone) into one recordable track, without sending anything to the speakers. (before it has a value: An `AudioContext` that is running. Browsers start audio only after a click, so call `tap.resume()` from a click handler. Without the click the tracks exist but carry silence.)
- `cameraConstraints` (function, @openav/record): `cameraConstraints({ deviceId = '', width = 1920, height = 1080, fps = 30, facingMode = '' } = {})` — Builds the getUserMedia options for a camera: it asks for 1920 by 1080 at 30 fps, but only as an ideal, never as a demand.
- `cleanValue` (function, @openav/record): `cleanValue(v, depth = 0)` — Makes a copy of a signal value that is safe to write as JSON: rounded numbers, plain arrays, no functions, nothing too deep.
- `Compositor` (class, @openav/record): `new Compositor({ size = 'vertical-1080p', layout = 'stack', layoutOptions = {}, getWorkCanvas = null, background = '#000', mirrorCam = true, maxFps = 60, onDraw = null, canvas = null } = {})` — Draws your work and the performer's camera into one canvas of an exact size, every frame: the canvas that a Recorder records.
- `EventLog` (class, @openav/record): `new EventLog({ now = defaultNow, filter = null, throttleMs = 0 } = {})` — Keeps a timestamped list of what happened during a take, such as notes and parameter changes, on the same clock as the recording.
- `extFor` (function, @openav/record): `extFor(mime)` — Gives the file extension for a recorded MIME type: video/mp4 is 'mp4', audio/mp4 is 'm4a', anything unknown is 'bin'.
- `framePoint` (function, @openav/record): `framePoint(camRect, u, v)` — Turns a point in the camera's own 0..1 coordinates, like a hand landmark, into a pixel in the output frame.
- `fromMidiFile` (function, @openav/record): `fromMidiFile(bytes, { name, families = 'both' } = {})` — Reads a Standard MIDI File into a take whose events are the signals a keyboard playing that file would publish.
- `layoutRects` (function, @openav/record): `layoutRects(layout, out, src = {}, opts = {})` — Works out where the work and the camera go in an output frame, in whole pixels, for one of the four layouts.
- `LAYOUTS` (constant, @openav/record): `LAYOUTS = array, 4 items` — The four layout names, in picker order: `'stack'`, `'pip'`, `'side'`, `'work'`.
- `listCameras` (function, @openav/record): `listCameras()` — Lists the video inputs of this computer as { deviceId, groupId, label }.
- `listMicrophones` (function, @openav/record): `listMicrophones()` — Lists the audio inputs of this computer as { deviceId, groupId, label }.
- `midiEventsOf` (function, @openav/record): `midiEventsOf(take)` — Reads a take as plain MIDI events (note on and off, controllers, pitch bend), picking one naming family so nothing is counted twice.
- `mixTracks` (function, @openav/record): `mixTracks(tracks)` — Mixes several audio tracks into one, because Chrome records only the first audio track of a stream.
- `normalizeTake` (function, @openav/record): `normalizeTake(input)` — Turns anything take-shaped, or its JSON text, into a valid take: events sorted by time, bad events dropped, nothing negative.
- `noteOf` (function, @openav/record): `noteOf(ev)` — Tells whether a recorded event is a key going down or up, whatever its spelling, and which note on which channel.
- `noteOffFor` (function, @openav/record): `noteOffFor(n)` — Gives the events that release a sounding note, in the same spelling it was played in.
- `openCamera` (function, @openav/record): `openCamera(opts = {})` — Opens a camera and returns its MediaStream: ideally 1920 by 1080 at 30 fps, or whatever the camera can do.
- `pickMime` (function, @openav/record): `pickMime(isTypeSupported, { audioOnly = false, prefer = null, candidates = null } = {})` — Picks the first MIME type from a list that the browser can record, using the browser's own check.
- `presetById` (function, @openav/record): `presetById(id)` — Finds one size preset by its id: `presetById('vertical-4k')`.
- `PRESETS` (constant, @openav/record): `PRESETS = array, 11 items` — The output sizes the compositor knows by name, from `vertical-1080p` (1080 by 1920) to `landscape-4k`, each with its suggested layout and frame rate.
- `quantizeTake` (function, @openav/record): `quantizeTake(take, { bpm, grid = 4, strength = 1, offsetMs = 0 } = {})` — Snaps the key presses of a take to a rhythmic grid, so a loose performance lands on the beat.
- `recommendedBitrate` (function, @openav/record): `recommendedBitrate(w, h, fps = recommendedFps(w, h))` — A video bitrate that keeps fast generative detail clean: 0.12 bits per pixel per frame, held between 4 and 80 Mb/s.
- `recommendedFps` (function, @openav/record): `recommendedFps(w, h)` — The frame rate to record a frame size at: 60 up to about 2.6 megapixels, 30 above that.
- `Recorder` (class, @openav/record): `new Recorder({ canvas = null, stream = null, fps = 60, audioTracks = [], audioOnly = false, videoBitsPerSecond, audioBitsPerSecond = 192000, mimeType, prefer = null } = {})` — Records a canvas, together with the sound you give it, into one video file with one MediaRecorder, so picture and sound stay in sync. (before it has a value: A browser with `MediaRecorder` (`Recorder.supported` tells), and a canvas or a stream, or `audioOnly: true`: otherwise the constructor throws a `TypeError`. Mixing several audio tracks makes an `AudioContext`, which needs the page to have had a click. A camera or microphone in the stream needs the user's permission, as always.)
- `resolveSize` (function, @openav/record): `resolveSize(size)` — Turns any way of naming a size, like 'vertical-4k', '1080x1920' or [w, h], into { w, h }, rounded up to even numbers.
- `signalsOfMidi` (function, @openav/record): `signalsOfMidi(ev, { families = 'both', device = null } = {})` — Turns one MIDI event into the signal events a keyboard playing it would publish, so a file can drive a work like live playing.
- `TAKE_VERSION` (constant, @openav/record): `TAKE_VERSION = 1` — The version number of the take format, which is 1. Every take has `v: 1`.
- `TakePlayer` (class, @openav/record): `new TakePlayer({ signals = null, take = null, loop = true, speed = 1, yieldToLive = false, resumeAfter = 0, isLive = defaultIsLive, chase = true, clock, maxStepMs = 250, onEvent = null, onState = null, now = defaultNow } = {})` — Plays a take back into a bus at the right times, so the work, its sound and its chord detector cannot tell it from you playing.
- `TakeRecorder` (class, @openav/record): `new TakeRecorder({ signals, filter = /^midi\//, name = 'take', meta = {}, overdub = false, throttleMs = 0, now = defaultNow } = {})` — Records what you play: it listens to every midi/* signal on a bus from start() to stop() and gives you a take.
- `takeStats` (function, @openav/record): `takeStats(take)` — Counts what is in a take: notes, events, length, the channels used, and the lowest and highest note.
- `toMidiFile` (function, @openav/record): `toMidiFile(take, { ppq = 960, bpm } = {})` — Writes a take as a Standard MIDI File (type 0) that opens in any DAW.
- `trimSilence` (function, @openav/record): `trimSilence(take, { keep = 0 } = {})` — Cuts the silence before the first key press of a take, so the first note comes at the moment you choose.
- `validateTake` (function, @openav/record): `validateTake(take)` — Checks a take and lists everything wrong with it as readable sentences. An empty list means it is valid.
- `VIDEO_MIMES` (constant, @openav/record): `VIDEO_MIMES = array, 6 items` — The video MIME types the recorder tries, best first: MP4 with H.264 and AAC, then WebM.

## options

- `clock` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_clock=follow | off` — Whether an external MIDI clock (from a DAW, Strudel or a drum machine) moves `drumPhase`, `drumBpm` and the drum machine: `follow` or `off`.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { clock: 'off' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  OAVp5.input([0xFA]);                          // MIDI start
  setInterval(() => OAVp5.input([0xF8]), 20);   // clock ticks: 24 a beat, here 50 a second
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('clock option: ' + OAVp5.options.clock, 20, 30);
  text('external clock: ' + OAVp5.clock.info.state, 20, 60);   // none: the clock is ignored
}
```

- `compact` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_compact=on | off` — Shows the 🎹 panel as a small box in the corner, a third of the window high, instead of a full-width bar: `on` or `off`.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { compact: 'on', panel: 'open' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('compact: ' + OAVp5.options.compact, 20, 30);   // true
}
```

- `corner` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_corner=right | left` — Which side of the window the 🎹 button, its cards and the compact panel sit on: `right` or `left`.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { corner: 'left' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('corner: ' + OAVp5.options.corner + ' (look for the 🎹)', 20, 30);
}
```

- `debug` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_debug=1 | 0` — Prints `[oav-p5 debug]` lines in the console about clicks, the 🎹 button and loading, for finding out why the 🎹 does not respond.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { debug: 1 };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('open the console, then click the canvas', 20, 30);   // [oav-p5 debug] lines appear
}
```

- `dock` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_dock=bottom | top` — Which edge of the window the 🎹 button and its cards sit on, `bottom` or `top`; set it and the panel starts on that edge too.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { dock: 'top' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('dock: ' + OAVp5.options.dock + ' (look for the 🎹)', 20, 30);
}
```

- `drumlatency` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_drumlatency=auto | 0 to 500 (milliseconds)` — How long it takes a drum hit to be heard after oav-p5 hands it to the audio clock, so pictures land with the sound: `auto` or milliseconds.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { drumlatency: 200 };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('bd*4, [~ sd]*2, hh*8', 108);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('drumlatency: ' + OAVp5.options.drumlatency + ' s', 20, 30);
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 50 + env('kick', 0.01, 0.3) * 200);   // told 0.2 s after the hit is scheduled
}
```

- `drums` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_drums=lookahead | frame` — How the drum machine is clocked: `lookahead` (hits scheduled ahead on the audio clock) or `frame` (moved by animation frames, 0.5's way).

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { drums: 'frame' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('bd*4, [~ sd]*2, hh*8', 108);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('drums: ' + OAVp5.options.drums + ' (clock: ' + OAVp5.drums.clock.clock + ')', 20, 30);
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 50 + env('kick', 0.01, 0.3) * 200);
}
```

- `hardware` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_hardware=auto | click | off` — When oav-p5 asks the browser for Web MIDI, which a real controller needs: `auto` at load, `click` when the 🎹 panel opens, or `off`.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { hardware: 'click' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('hardware option: ' + OAVp5.options.hardware, 20, 30);
  text('Web MIDI state: ' + OAVp5.hardware, 20, 60);   // stays "off" until you open the 🎹 panel
}
```

- `hints` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_hints=on | off` — Whether oav-p5 shows its explaining cards beside the 🎹 (blocked microphone, no Web MIDI, an error in your callback): `on` or `off`.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { hints: 'off' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  lag(1);   // an unnamed lag() outside draw(): oav-p5 has something to say about that
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('cards said: ' + OAVp5.hints.length + ' (none on the page)', 20, 30);
  text(OAVp5.hints.map((h) => h.what).join('\n'), 20, 60);
}
```

- `link` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_link=a room name` — Joins a room: oav-p5 pages with the same room hear what each other's programs play, over the relay. A room name, or empty for none. (before it has a value: A network connection to the relay ([`relay`](#option-relay), `wss://remote.cheyuwu.com/relay` unless you set another). Without it the 🔗 is red and nothing is shared.)

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { link: 'my-room' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  const info = OAVp5.link.info;
  text('room: ' + OAVp5.options.link, 20, 30);
  text('state: ' + (info ? info.state + ', ' + info.peers + ' other page(s)' : 'not linked'), 20, 60);
}
```

- `linkdelay` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_linkdelay=0 to 2000 (milliseconds)` — Extra milliseconds of buffer on the notes a linked page receives, to smooth out an uneven network: 0 to 2000.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { linkdelay: 80 };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('linkdelay: ' + OAVp5.options.linkdelay + ' ms', 20, 30);
  text('link: ' + (OAVp5.link.info ? 'room ' + OAVp5.link.info.room : 'no room, so nothing to delay'), 20, 60);   // add link: 'my-room' to use it
}
```

- `mic` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_mic=auto | click | off` — Who may turn the microphone on: `auto` (the first read of `micLevel` and friends), `click` (only 🎤 or `startMic()`) or `off` (nobody).

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { mic: 'click' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function mousePressed() {
  startMic();   // now the browser asks
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 50 + micLevel * 300);   // reading micLevel no longer asks
  fill(255);
  text('microphone: ' + OAVp5.mic.state + ' (click the canvas to start it)', 20, 30);
}
```

- `opc` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_opc=on | off` — Whether oav-p5 wires the controller to the variables of OP Configurator (OpenProcessing's sliders and buttons): `on` or `off`.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { opc: 'off' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('opc option: ' + OAVp5.options.opc, 20, 30);
  text('controls wired to OPC variables: ' + OAVp5.wiring().length, 20, 60);   // 0
}
```

- `panel` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_panel=closed | open | off` — Whether the 🎹 panel starts shut, open, or does not exist: `closed`, `open` or `off`.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { panel: 'open' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('panel: ' + OAVp5.options.panel, 20, 30);
}
```

- `profile` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_profile=a profile id` — Which controller the on-screen 🎹 shows, by profile id such as `akai-lpd8`; by default it follows the one that is plugged in.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { profile: 'akai-lpd8', panel: 'open' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('profile: ' + OAVp5.options.profile, 20, 30);
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 40 + knob1 * 240);   // knob 1 of the LPD8
}
```

- `recfps` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_recfps=1 to 60` — The frame rate of recorded video, 1 to 60 frames a second.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { recfps: 60 };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('recording frame rate: ' + OAVp5.record.fps, 20, 30);
}
```

- `reclimit` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_reclimit=1 or more (seconds)` — The longest one recording may last, in seconds: a take stops by itself there.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { reclimit: 60 };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('longest take: ' + OAVp5.record.limit + ' seconds', 20, 30);
}
```

- `record` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_record=on | nomic | off` — Whether recording is available and whether it includes the microphone: `on`, `nomic` or `off`.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { record: 'nomic' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key === 'r') startRecording(3);   // three seconds, without the microphone
}

function draw() {
  background(20 + 20 * sin(frameCount * 0.05));
  fill(255);
  text('press r to record 3 seconds (' + (recordingIsOn ? 'recording' : 'idle') + ')', 20, 30);
}
```

- `relay` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_relay=a ws:// or wss:// address` — The address of the relay that phones and `link` rooms talk through: a WebSocket URL.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { relay: 'ws://localhost:7458/relay' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('relay: ' + OAVp5.options.relay, 20, 30);   // used when you open 📱 or set link
}
```

- `remote` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_remote=an https:// address` — The address of the remote page that the 📱 QR code opens on a phone.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { remote: 'http://192.168.0.10:8080/packages/remote/' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('remote page: ' + OAVp5.options.remote, 20, 30);   // the 📱 QR code points here
}
```

- `room` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_room=a room name` — The name of the room phones join to play this page: by default one made up per browser.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { room: 'class-2026' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('room: ' + OAVp5.options.room, 20, 30);   // the phones' QR code uses this room
}
```

- `scope` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_scope=on | off` — Whether `scope()` draws its oscilloscope in the corner of the page: `on` or `off`. `hints=off` turns it off too.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { scope: 'off' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  const wave = 0.5 + 0.5 * sin(frameCount * 0.05);
  circle(width / 2, height / 2, 40 + scope(wave, 'wave') * 200);   // returns wave, draws nothing
}
```

- `shim` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_shim=on | off` — Whether oav-p5 replaces `navigator.requestMIDIAccess` so sketches with their own Web MIDI code also hear the 🎹 and phones: `on` or `off`.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { shim: 'off' };

let names = 'asking…';

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  navigator.requestMIDIAccess().then(
    (access) => { names = [...access.inputs.values()].map((i) => i.name).join(', ') || 'no inputs'; },
    (error) => { names = 'refused: ' + error.name; }
  );
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('shim: ' + OAVp5.options.shim, 20, 30);
  text('MIDI inputs: ' + names, 20, 60);
}
```

- `sound` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_sound=click | off | an instrument id` — Whether notes are heard: `click` (only after `startSound()` or 🔊), `off` (never), or an instrument id that starts at the first click.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { sound: 'organ' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function mousePressed() {
  OAVp5.play(60 + floor(random(12)), 0.8);   // a key, as a controller would play it
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('sound: ' + OAVp5.sound.state + ' (' + OAVp5.sound.instrument + ')', 20, 30);
  text('click the canvas to play a note', 20, 60);
}
```

- `strudel` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_strudel=auto | on | off` — Whether oav-p5 treats the page as Strudel, the live-coding editor, and behaves politely beside it: `auto`, `on` or `off`.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { strudel: 'on' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('hardware: ' + OAVp5.options.hardware, 20, 30);   // click: Strudel asks for MIDI itself
  text('compact panel: ' + OAVp5.options.compact, 20, 60);   // true
}
```

- `telemetry` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_telemetry=off | on` — Whether the on-screen controller may send one anonymous page-load count to the project: `off` or `on`.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { telemetry: 'on' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('telemetry: ' + OAVp5.options.telemetry, 20, 30);   // nothing visible changes
}
```

- `title` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_title=a name` — A name that goes into the file name of recordings and images, as in `oav-my-piece-20261015-183012.mp4`.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { title: 'my-piece' };

let saved = 'press r to record 2 seconds';

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function keyPressed() {
  if (key === 'r') startRecording(2);
}

function recordingSaved(info) {
  saved = 'saved as ' + info.name;
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(saved, 20, 30);
}
```

- `tone` (option, oav-p5): `?oav_tone=an ES module URL` — Where Tone.js, the sound engine behind `startSound()`, is loaded from: an ES module address. Empty means jsDelivr.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { tone: 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/tone@15.0.4/+esm' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('Tone.js from: ' + OAVp5.options.tone, 20, 30);   // the address here is the built-in one
}
```

## oavp5

- `OAVp5`, `midi`, `oavMidi` (object, oav-p5): `OAVp5` — The object oav-p5 hangs everything on: MIDI state, the panel, the microphone, the clock, the check-up. `midi` and `oavMidi` are the same object. (before it has a value: Only the loader line. If it has not loaded, `OAVp5` is not defined, and a sketch that reads it stops with "OAVp5 is not defined".)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('same object: ' + (OAVp5 === midi && OAVp5 === oavMidi), 20, 30);
  text('version: ' + OAVp5.version, 20, 60);
  text('MIDI hardware: ' + OAVp5.hardware, 20, 90);
  text('microphone: ' + OAVp5.mic.state, 20, 120);   // reading the state does not start it
  text('external clock: ' + OAVp5.clock.info.state, 20, 150);
}
```

- `OAVp5.check` (function, oav-p5): `OAVp5.check([opts])` — Runs the 🩺 check-up: the version, page, browser, microphone, MIDI, sound, drums, recording, wiring and hints, as a card to screenshot and as an object.

```js
let report;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  report = OAVp5.check({ show: false });   // the report, without the card on the page
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  textSize(10);
  text(report.text, 10, 10, width - 20, height - 20);
}
```

- `OAVp5.clock` (object, oav-p5): `OAVp5.clock` — What oav-p5 hears of an external MIDI clock: its state, tempo and where it is in the bar. Nothing until another program or device starts sending one.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  OAVp5.input([0xFA]);                          // MIDI start
  setInterval(() => OAVp5.input([0xF8]), 20);   // clock ticks: 24 a beat, here 50 a second (125 BPM)
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('clock: ' + OAVp5.clock.info.state, 20, 30);
  text('tempo: ' + (OAVp5.clock.bpm ? nf(OAVp5.clock.bpm, 1, 1) : '-') + ' BPM', 20, 60);
  const p = OAVp5.clock.phase;
  if (p) circle(40 + p.beat * (width - 80), 150, 30);   // sweeps across once a beat
}
```

- `OAVp5.clock.bpm` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.clock.bpm` — The tempo of the external MIDI clock in beats a minute, or `null` while there is none.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  OAVp5.input([0xFA]);                          // MIDI start
  setInterval(() => OAVp5.input([0xF8]), 20);   // clock ticks: 24 a beat, here 50 a second (125 BPM)
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  textSize(48);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  const bpm = OAVp5.clock.bpm;
  text(bpm ? nf(bpm, 1, 1) + ' BPM' : 'no clock', width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `OAVp5.clock.info` (object, oav-p5): `OAVp5.clock.info` — A snapshot of the external clock: `state` (`none`, `running`, `stopped` or `lost`), `bpm`, whether the drums follow it, where it came from, and counts.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  OAVp5.input([0xFA]);                          // MIDI start
  setInterval(() => OAVp5.input([0xF8]), 20);   // clock ticks: 24 a beat, here 50 a second (125 BPM)
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  const i = OAVp5.clock.info;
  text('state: ' + i.state + (i.running ? ' (running)' : ''), 20, 30);
  text('bpm: ' + i.bpm + ',  following: ' + i.following, 20, 60);
  text('source: ' + i.source + ',  clocks heard: ' + i.clocks, 20, 90);
}
```

- `OAVp5.clock.phase` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.clock.phase` — Where the external clock is right now: `{ pos, bar, beat, bpm, running }`, or `null` while there is no tempo.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  OAVp5.input([0xFA]);                          // MIDI start
  setInterval(() => OAVp5.input([0xF8]), 20);   // clock ticks: 24 a beat, here 50 a second (125 BPM)
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  const p = OAVp5.clock.phase;
  if (!p) return;
  noStroke();
  fill(255, 211, 107);
  circle(40 + p.bar * (width - 80), 100, 30);   // once a bar (four beats)
  fill(120, 190, 255);
  circle(40 + p.beat * (width - 80), 200, 30);  // once a beat
}
```

- `OAVp5.drums.clock` (object, oav-p5): `OAVp5.drums.clock` — How the drum machine keeps time: which clock moves it, how far ahead it schedules and how long the callbacks wait for the speakers. (range { clock, heartbeat, lookahead, latency, audio, extended, preDraw, … })

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('four on floor', 120);
  textSize(14);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  const c = OAVp5.drums.clock;
  text('clock: ' + c.clock + ' (' + c.heartbeat + ')', 20, 30);
  text('lookahead: ' + c.lookahead + ' s', 20, 60);
  text('latency: ' + c.latency + ' s', 20, 90);
  text('hook before draw: ' + (c.preDraw || 'none'), 20, 120);
}
```

- `OAVp5.drums.machine` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.drums.machine` — The drum machine from @openav/drums that the grid on the page belongs to, or `null` before it has loaded. (before it has a value: It is `null` until [`startDrums()`](#startDrums) (or 🥁) has loaded the machine. Check for `null` before you use it.)

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startDrums('four on floor', 120);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
}

function mousePressed() {
  const m = OAVp5.drums.machine;
  if (m) m.play(!m.seq.playing);   // pause and resume, the grid stays
}

function draw() {
  background(OAVp5.drums.state === 'stopped' ? 80 : 20);
  fill(255);
  text('click to pause or resume (' + OAVp5.drums.state + ')', width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

- `OAVp5.hints` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.hints` — The list of cards oav-p5 has shown or would have shown so far (a blocked microphone, no Web MIDI, an error in your callback), each with what, why and what to press.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  lag(1);   // an unnamed lag() outside draw(): oav-p5 has something to say
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(OAVp5.hints.length + ' card(s) so far', 20, 30);
  text(OAVp5.hints.map((h) => h.kind + ': ' + h.what).join('\n'), 20, 60);
}
```

- `OAVp5.link` (object, oav-p5): `OAVp5.link` — What the link to other oav-p5 pages in the same room is doing: only `OAVp5.link.info`, and `null` unless a room is set.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text(OAVp5.link.info ? 'linked' : 'not linked: add link: \'my-room\' to the options', 20, 30);
}
```

- `OAVp5.link.info` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.link.info` — The state of the link: its room, `state` (`connecting`, `open`, `closed`), how many other pages are there, and the trip time. `null` when no room is set.

```js
window.OAV_P5 = { link: 'my-room' };

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  const i = OAVp5.link.info;
  text('room: ' + i.room + ',  state: ' + i.state, 20, 30);
  text('other pages: ' + i.peers + ',  one-way trip: ' + (i.trip == null ? '-' : i.trip + ' ms'), 20, 60);
}
```

- `OAVp5.sound.shell`, `OAVp5.sound.engine`, `OAVp5.sound.module` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.sound.shell` — The loaded parts of @openav/sound: the `Sound` shell, its Tone.js engine and the module itself. All three are `null` until sound has loaded. (before it has a value: Call [`startSound()`](#startSound) first and wait until [`OAVp5.sound.state`](#OAVp5.sound.state) is no longer `'loading'`, or check for `null` before you use them.)

```js
let ids = [];

function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  startSound('synth/pluck');
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  textSize(12);
  if (!ids.length && OAVp5.sound.module) ids = OAVp5.sound.module.listInstruments().map((d) => d.id);
  text(ids.length ? ids.join(', ') : 'loading…', 20, 20, width - 40, height - 40);
}
```

- `OAVp5.version` (variable, oav-p5): `OAVp5.version` — The version of oav-p5 that loaded, as text such as `'0.8.0'`.

```js
function setup() {
  createCanvas(400, 300);
  textAlign(CENTER, CENTER);
  textSize(32);
}

function draw() {
  background(20);
  fill(255);
  text('oav-p5 ' + OAVp5.version, width / 2, height / 2);
}
```

## midi-io

- `BEND_CENTER` (constant, @openav/midi): `BEND_CENTER = 8192` — The resting value of a pitch-bend wheel: 8192, the middle of the 14-bit range 0..16383. (range 8192)
- `bendToUnit` (function, @openav/midi): `bendToUnit(v)` — Turns a 14-bit pitch-bend value (0..16383) into −1..1, with the centre (8192) exactly 0.
- `CONTROL_TYPES` (constant, @openav/midi): `CONTROL_TYPES = array, 8 items` — The kinds of control a profile may contain: `knob`, `encoder`, `fader`, `pad`, `button`, `keys`, `wheel`, `strip`. (range ['knob', 'encoder', 'fader', 'pad', 'button', 'keys', 'wheel', 'strip'])
- `controllerRoutes` (function, @openav/midi): `controllerRoutes(profile, bindings, { short = profile.short, ...extra } = {})` — Builds mapper routes for "this control drives that param": `controllerRoutes(profile, { knob1: 'hue' })` routes the knob's signal to the param `hue`.
- `createVirtualMIDIAccess` (function, @openav/midi): `createVirtualMIDIAccess({ name = 'OAV Virtual MIDI', manufacturer = 'open-audiovisual', id = 'oav-virtual', sysex = false, onOutput = null, onClear = null } = {})` — Builds a Web MIDI `MIDIAccess` that always has one more input and output of its own, so a sketch written for a MIDI keyboard works with none plugged in.
- `DEFAULT_PROFILE` (constant, @openav/midi): `DEFAULT_PROFILE = "arturia-minilab3"` — The profile id used when none is given: `'arturia-minilab3'`. (range 'arturia-minilab3')
- `describe` (function, @openav/midi): `describe(ev)` — Returns a short readable line for a parsed MIDI event, for logs and learn screens: `CC ch1 #74=64`, `Bend ch1 0.50`.
- `EchoGuard` (class, @openav/midi): `new EchoGuard({ window = 40, max = 256 } = {})` — Recognises our own MIDI messages coming back: remember what was sent, and an identical message arriving within a short window is an echo, not a performer.
- `encodeMessage` (function, @openav/midi): `encodeMessage(ev)` — Turns an event object back into MIDI bytes, the inverse of `parseMessage()`: `{ type: 'cc', ch: 1, cc: 74, value: 64 }` becomes `[0xb0, 74, 64]`.
- `eventOfSignal` (function, @openav/midi): `eventOfSignal(name, value, { channel = 1 } = {})` — The inverse of `genericSignals()`: turns one generic MIDI signal (`midi/ch/10/note/36`, `midi/cc/74`) back into the MIDI event it came from.
- `findPort` (function, @openav/midi): `findPort(ports, query)` — Finds a MIDI port by name: a `/regex/flags`, then the exact name, then a case-insensitive substring; `null` when nothing matches.
- `findProfile` (function, @openav/midi): `findProfile(ref, profiles)` — Finds a profile in a list by id or short name, or returns `null`; no validation, no loading.
- `genericSignals` (function, @openav/midi): `genericSignals(ev, { device = null, legacy = true, channel = true } = {})` — Lists the device-independent signals one MIDI event becomes: `midi/cc/74`, `midi/note/on`, `midi/bend`, and their per-channel twins such as `midi/ch/2/cc/74`.
- `groupsOf` (function, @openav/midi): `groupsOf(p)` — Groups a profile's controls by their `group` (`knob`, `pad`, `fader` …), returning `{ group: [control ids] }`.
- `indexProfile` (function, @openav/midi): `indexProfile(p)` — Builds the lookup from a MIDI message to the control it moves: `"cc:1:74"` maps to the knob listening for CC 74 on channel 1.
- `isLive` (function, @openav/midi): `isLive(p)` — Says whether a MIDI port can still be sent to: it exists and its `state` is not `'disconnected'`.
- `isProfileUrl` (function, @openav/midi): `isProfileUrl(ref)` — Tells a URL to a profile file apart from a profile id: `true` for `./pads.json`, `https://…`, `/p/x`, `false` for `'akai-lpd8'`.
- `linkControllers` (function, @openav/midi): `linkControllers(relay, signals, controllers)` — Links the on-screen controllers to phones over the room relay: tells phones which device is on screen, echoes this machine's moves to them, and mirrors theirs here.
- `loadProfile` (function, @openav/midi): `loadProfile(ref, o = {})` — Loads a controller profile by id, short name or URL (a JSON file anywhere CORS allows), checking any file or object you give it; returns a promise.
- `matchProfile` (function, @openav/midi): `matchProfile(portName, profiles)` — Finds the device profile that owns a MIDI port name, such as `'Minilab3 MIDI'`, by testing each profile's `match` patterns.
- `Midi` (class, @openav/midi): `new Midi({ signals = null, filterOut = 'IAC', requestAccess = null, echoWindow = 40, prefer = [] } = {})` — The Web MIDI engine: asks the browser for access, listens to every input, publishes what arrives as signals, and sends to one output port. (before it has a value: Call `await midi.enable()` first. Browsers with Web MIDI (Chrome, Edge, Firefox) ask the visitor for permission at that moment, so call it from a click when you can. Safari and iPad have no Web MIDI: `enable()` gives `false`.)
- `MidiController` (class, @openav/midi): `new MidiController(profile, { signals = null, sink = null, short = null, onLed = null } = {})` — One MIDI controller (a profile) as a live model: MIDI bytes go in, control values and signals come out, and a hand on screen sends the bytes the device would.
- `MidiControllers` (class, @openav/midi): `new MidiControllers({ profiles, signals = null, sink = null, midi = null, initial = null, storage = safeStorage() } = {})` — Ties hardware ports to controller profiles: plug in a MiniLab 3 and the on-screen one appears and moves with your hands; unplug it and it stays playable.
- `normalizeProfile` (function, @openav/midi): `normalizeProfile(raw)` — Validates a profile and returns a filled-in copy with defaults for channel, labels, groups, encoder mode and portrait layout; the input is not changed.
- `parseMessage` (function, @openav/midi): `parseMessage(data)` — Turns the bytes of one MIDI message into an event object such as `{ type: 'noteon', ch: 1, note: 60, vel: 100 }`, or `null` for bytes it does not know.
- `pickOutput` (function, @openav/midi): `pickOutput(outputs, { preferred = '', prefer = [] } = {})` — Chooses which MIDI output to send to from a list: the port you named, else the first match of a preference list, else the first live port.
- `pickPort` (function, @openav/midi): `pickPort(ports, profile)` — Of several ports one device exposes ("Minilab3 MIDI", "Minilab3 DIN THRU", "Minilab3 MCU/HUI"), picks the one to listen to.
- `profileById` (function, @openav/midi): `profileById(id)` — Looks up a shipped controller profile by its id (`'akai-lpd8'`) or its short signal name (`'lpd8'`), or returns `null`.
- `PROFILES` (constant, @openav/midi): `PROFILES = array, 27 items` — Every controller profile that ships with the package, as an array of plain JSON objects: real devices first, then the generic layouts.
- `profileSignals` (function, @openav/midi): `profileSignals(p)` — Lists every signal name a profile can publish under its own namespace (`midi/lpd8/…` for the LPD8), for docs, tests and mapping screens.
- `publish` (function, @openav/midi): `publish(signals, list)` — Publishes a list of `{ name, value, pulse?, min?, max? }` into a `Signals` registry, declaring each signal the first time it is seen.
- `RELATIVE_MODES` (constant, @openav/midi): `RELATIVE_MODES = array, 4 items` — The four ways an endless encoder can write a turn as a CC value: `offset64`, `offset16`, `twos` and `signbit`. (range ['offset64', 'offset16', 'twos', 'signbit'])
- `relativeDelta` (function, @openav/midi): `relativeDelta(value, mode = 'offset64')` — Turns the CC value an endless encoder sends into signed steps: with `offset64`, 65 is +1, 63 is −1 and 64 is no move.
- `relativeValue` (function, @openav/midi): `relativeValue(delta, mode = 'offset64')` — The inverse of `relativeDelta()`: the CC value that says "turned by this many steps" in a given encoder encoding.
- `reselectOutput` (function, @openav/midi): `reselectOutput({ current, outputs, preferred = '', prefer = [] })` — Decides what to send to after the port list changed or the current port died, and returns the one line to print about it.
- `RESERVED_IDS` (constant, @openav/midi): `RESERVED_IDS = array, 7 items` — Control ids a profile may not use, because they are signal suffixes: `last`, `raw`, `delta`, `hit`, `on`, `off`, `pressure`. (range ['last', 'raw', 'delta', 'hit', 'on', 'off', 'pressure'])
- `resolveProfile` (function, @openav/midi): `async resolveProfile(ref, { profiles = [], fetch = globalThis.fetch, base = undefined } = {})` — Turns a profile object, an id or short name, or a URL to a profile JSON into a profile; an object or a file that is not valid is rejected with every problem listed.
- `ScoreMidi` (class, @openav/midi): `new ScoreMidi({ midi, channel = 15, segment = { note: 36 }, cue = { note: 84 }, length = 0.15, scrub = false, enabled = true, timer = (fn, ms) => setTimeout(fn, ms) } = {})` — Turns a show's segment changes and cues into MIDI notes and CCs on one channel, so a DAW or lighting desk can follow the show.
- `unitToBend` (function, @openav/midi): `unitToBend(u)` — Turns a −1..1 number into a 14-bit pitch-bend value (0..16383), the inverse of `bendToUnit()`.
- `validateProfile` (function, @openav/midi): `validateProfile(p)` — Checks a controller profile and returns every problem as a sentence; an empty array means it is valid.
- `virtualRequestMIDIAccess` (function, @openav/midi): `virtualRequestMIDIAccess({ real = null, make, waitMs = 1200 })` — Wraps `navigator.requestMIDIAccess` so every caller gets the virtual access: real ports join if they answer in time, and the virtual input stays without Web MIDI.
- `withChannel` (function, @openav/midi): `withChannel(profile, ch)` — Returns a copy of a profile with every control moved to another MIDI channel, for a unit that is set to a channel other than the profile's.

## controllers

- `CANVAS_THEME` (constant, @openav/midi): `CANVAS_THEME = object, 16 keys` — The default look of `ControllerCanvas`: background, body, text, idle colours, `accent`, `glow` and fonts. Pass any subset as the `theme` option.
- `controlDetail` (function, @openav/midi): `controlDetail(mc, id, st, info = {})` — Builds the `control` event payload for one control change: `id`, `value`, `raw`, `signal`, the parsed `message`, its `bytes` and where it came from.
- `ControllerCanvas` (class, @openav/midi): `new ControllerCanvas({ profile = 'arturia-minilab3', signals = null, controller = null, mapping = null, theme = {}, notes = 'auto', screen = true, padding = 0.05, now = defaultNow } = {})` — Draws a controller's faceplate into any 2D canvas context, every frame, at any size: the bottom of a performance video, an overlay, a thumbnail.
- `controllerGeometry` (function, @openav/midi): `controllerGeometry(profile, rect, { padding = 0.05, notes = 'auto' } = {})` — Computes where everything goes when a profile's faceplate is drawn into a pixel rectangle: the face, every section, every control cell, and the notes strip.
- `ControllerHost` (class, @openav/midi): `new ControllerHost(profile = 'arturia-minilab3', { profiles = PROFILES, signals = null, sink = null, channel = null, follow = false, midi = null, requestAccess = null, filterOut = 'IAC', storage = undefined, telemetry = true, embedKind = 'headless' } = {})` — The object `createController()` returns: one controller with its events, its playable faceplate, its hardware connection and its MIDI output. (before it has a value: `connectHardware()`, `setOutput()` and `requestMidi()` are the only calls that ask the browser for MIDI. Chrome, Edge and Firefox show a permission prompt, so call them from a click when you can. Without Web MIDI (Safari, iPad) the controller still plays and fires events, and `status` says `unavailable`.)
- `ControllerView` (class, @openav/midi): `new ControllerView(container, controller, { mode = 'auto', minTouch = 38 } = {})` — The playable on-screen faceplate of a controller: knobs, faders, pads and keys you drive with a mouse, a finger or the keyboard, repainted from the controller's state. (before it has a value: A browser DOM and a container with a height. `createController(…).mount(el)` is the usual way to get one.)
- `createController` (function, @openav/midi): `createController(profile = 'arturia-minilab3', o = {})` — Makes one MIDI controller you can play, listen to, and point at hardware or a DAW, with no element and no framework: `createController('akai-lpd8')`.
- `defineController` (function, @openav/midi): `defineController(tag = 'oav-controller')` — Registers the controller element under another tag name (importing `@openav/midi/element` already registers it as `oav-controller`).
- `describeDetail` (function, @openav/midi): `describeDetail(d)` — Writes the readout line for a `control` event payload: `midi/minilab3/knob1 = 0.42 ← CC 74 = 53 · ch 1`.
- `describeMessage` (function, @openav/midi): `describeMessage(m)` — Writes one parsed MIDI message the way a person reads it: `CC 70 = 53`, `Note 36 · vel 90`, `Bend 12288`.
- `EMBED_ATTRS` (constant, @openav/midi): `EMBED_ATTRS = array, 11 items` — The attributes the `oav-controller` element reads, which are also the query parameters of the iframe page: `profile`, `layout`, `hardware`, `midi-out` and more. (range ['profile', 'layout', 'hardware', 'midi-out', 'channel', 'learn', 'picker', 'readout', 'follow', 'theme', 'telemetry'])
- `EMBED_EVENTS` (constant, @openav/midi): `EMBED_EVENTS = array, 9 items` — The nine events the `oav-controller` element dispatches and the iframe posts to its page, from `ready` and `control` to `profilechange` and `error`. (range ['ready', 'control', 'noteon', 'noteoff', 'connect', 'disconnect', 'status', 'profilechange', 'error'])
- `EMBED_LAYOUTS` (constant, @openav/midi): `EMBED_LAYOUTS = array, 3 items` — The three layouts a controller can have: `auto`, `face` (the device as it looks) and `stack` (re-gridded for a tall box). (range ['auto', 'face', 'stack'])
- `embedChannel` (function, @openav/midi): `embedChannel(v)` — Reads the `channel` attribute: a whole number from 1 to 16, or `null` for anything else.
- `embedColor` (function, @openav/midi): `embedColor(v)` — Checks the `bg` colour of the iframe page and returns a safe value: `transparent`, a hex colour, or a plain colour name; anything else is `null`.
- `embedFlag` (function, @openav/midi): `embedFlag(v)` — Reads a boolean attribute: present means on, unless it says `false`, `0`, `off` or `no`.
- `embedMode` (function, @openav/midi): `embedMode(v, { bare = 'on' } = {})` — Reads `hardware` and `midi-out`: off, `ask` (a button, so the permission prompt waits for a click) or on, plus which port.
- `fadeLevel` (function, @openav/midi): `fadeLevel(now, at, ms)` — The brightness of a fading touch: 1 at the moment it happened, 0 after `ms`, eased so it still reads on a 30 fps frame.
- `followMidiSignals` (function, @openav/midi): `followMidiSignals(signals, onEvent, { channel = 1, defer = (fn) => queueMicrotask(fn) } = {})` — Listens to a `Signals` bus and hands you each MIDI message back exactly once, as an event, although hardware publishes it under two names.
- `FRAME_COMMANDS` (constant, @openav/midi): `FRAME_COMMANDS = array, 8 items` — The commands a page may send into an embed iframe: `set`, `ingest`, `reset`, `profile`, `layout`, `get`, `press`, `release`. (range ['set', 'ingest', 'reset', 'profile', 'layout', 'get', 'press', 'release'])
- `fromFrame` (function, @openav/midi): `fromFrame(data)` — Page side: reads a message that came from an embed iframe, returns `{ type, frame, detail, v }`, or `null` when it is not one of ours.
- `fromParent` (function, @openav/midi): `fromParent(data)` — Frame side: validates a command from the page and returns a clean command, or `null` (the message is ignored).
- `keyboardGeometry` (function, @openav/midi): `keyboardGeometry(from, to, rect)` — Computes the rectangles of piano keys from one note to another inside a rect: white keys side by side, black keys over the seams at 60% of the height.
- `keyWindow` (function, @openav/midi): `keyWindow(from, to, base, note)` — Tells which note a drawn keyboard should start at after a note outside its printed range arrives, so it follows the device's octave buttons.
- `midiNoteName` (function, @openav/midi): `midiNoteName(n)` — Turns a MIDI note number into its name with the octave, middle C being C4: `midiNoteName(60)` is `'C4'`, `midiNoteName(61)` is `'C#4'`.
- `mountMidiPanel` (function, @openav/midi): `mountMidiPanel(parent, mcs, { mode = 'full', open = true, id = null, onToggle = null, closeButton = mode === 'dock', profiles = null, contained = false } = {})` — Mounts a controller panel: a toolbar (device picker, hardware status, port picker, Learn, last message) above a playable faceplate, docked at the bottom or full size.
- `OavController` (class, @openav/midi): `new OavController()` — The `oav-controller` custom element: a playable MIDI controller you paste into any page with one line, with no import map and no build. (before it has a value: Wait for the controller to exist: `await el.ready` (a promise that resolves with the element), or listen for the `ready` event. Before that, `set()`, `press()`, `release()` and `ingest()` return `null` and print one console warning, and `get()` also returns `null`. It never asks for MIDI permission unless `hardware`, `midi-out` or Learn is used.)
- `PANEL_CSS` (constant, @openav/midi): `PANEL_CSS = "\n.mcp { position: absolute; inset: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; …"` — The stylesheet text of the controller panel (`mountMidiPanel`), as a string.
- `parseEmbedOptions` (function, @openav/midi): `parseEmbedOptions(src)` — Reads the options of one embed from an element, a query string, an object or a getter function, and returns them cleaned up with defaults.
- `POST_SOURCE` (constant, @openav/midi): `POST_SOURCE = "openav"` — The word that marks a message as an open-audiovisual embed message: `'openav'`, sent as `source` by the iframe and as `target` by the page. (range 'openav')
- `POST_VERSION` (constant, @openav/midi): `POST_VERSION = 1` — The version of the iframe message format, `1`, written as `v` in every message. (range 1)
- `preferredAspect` (function, @openav/midi): `preferredAspect(profile, width, { layout = 'auto', minTouch = 38 } = {})` — Works out the width ÷ height a controller wants in a box of a given width: its faceplate when every control stays finger-sized, a taller stack otherwise.
- `restValue` (function, @openav/midi): `restValue(c)` — Says where a control rests: knobs and faders at their default (0), bipolar wheels at the centre, pads, buttons and keys at 0.
- `setControl` (function, @openav/midi): `setControl(mc, id, value, { note = null, source = 'ui' } = {})` — Moves one control the way a hand would, whatever its type, and returns the MIDI bytes it sent: `setControl(mc, 'k1', 0.5)`.
- `toFrame` (function, @openav/midi): `toFrame(type, args = {})` — Page side: builds a command to post into an embed iframe: `{ target: 'openav', v: 1, type, ...args }`.
- `toParent` (function, @openav/midi): `toParent(type, detail = null, { frame = null } = {})` — Frame side: builds the message the iframe posts to its page for an event: `{ source: 'openav', v: 1, type, frame, detail }`.
- `touchText` (function, @openav/midi): `touchText(c, st, note = null)` — Writes what a device's screen says about a touch: `Knob 1 · 87`, `C4 · 100`, `Pad 3 · 96`, `Pitch +0.42`.
- `valuesOf` (function, @openav/midi): `valuesOf(mc)` — Reads every control's current value from a controller as `{ id: number }`; for keys it is 1 while any key is held.
- `VIEW_CSS` (constant, @openav/midi): `VIEW_CSS = "\n.mcv { position: relative; width: 100%; height: 100%; overflow: hidden; touc…"` — The stylesheet text of the on-screen controller (`ControllerView`), as a string.

## keys

- `KeysPiano` (class, @openav/keys): `new KeysPiano(container, opts = {})` — An on-screen piano you can play with the mouse, a finger or the computer keyboard, that calls a function for every note.
- `mountKeys` (function, @openav/keys): `mountKeys(container, { signals, chord = null, base = 48, octaves = 2, sim = true, capture = true } = {})` — Puts a playable piano on the page in one call, with a keyboard switch and a self-playing performer, and publishes every note as `midi/note/on` and `midi/note/off`. (before it has a value: A page with a DOM. The keyboard checkbox must be ticked before the computer keyboard plays, on purpose: while it is on, every letter key is taken by the piano, so hotkeys on letters stop working. A key listener goes on `window` until `dispose()`.)
- `PIANO_KEYMAP` (constant, @openav/keys): `PIANO_KEYMAP = object, 17 keys` — Which computer-keyboard letter plays which note: `a` is the base note, `w` a semitone higher, `s` two.
- `SimPlayer` (class, @openav/keys): `new SimPlayer({ press, release, base = 60, scale = [0, 2, 4, 7, 9], density = 1 } = {})` — A hands-free performer: it presses and releases notes on its own, in a scale, so a demo can play itself.

## leap

- `boneBasis` (function, @openav/leap): `boneBasis(prev, next, palmNormal, left)` — An advanced helper: the orthonormal basis `[x, y, z]` of a bone, rebuilt from two joints and the palm normal the way LeapJS expects.
- `DEFAULT_PORT` (constant, @openav/leap): `DEFAULT_PORT = 6437` — The Leap bridge's default port: 6437, the port the original Leap service used, so old `leap.js` sketches find it unchanged.
- `DEFAULT_URL` (constant, @openav/leap): `DEFAULT_URL = "ws://127.0.0.1:6437/v6.json"` — The default address `LeapInput` connects to: `ws://127.0.0.1:6437/v6.json`, the bridge on this machine speaking the LeapJS protocol.
- `deviceEvent` (function, @openav/leap): `deviceEvent({ device = null, service = true } = {})` — A LeapJS device event telling the client whether a device is attached and streaming, plus our own `service` flag.
- `FINGERS` (constant, @openav/leap): `FINGERS = array, 5 items` — The five finger names in order, `thumb index middle ring pinky`: the order of `hand.fingers` and the names in the fingertip signals.
- `handAngles` (function, @openav/leap): `handAngles(direction, normal)` — Turns a hand's direction and palm normal into `{ pitch, yaw, roll }` in radians, with the LeapJS conventions.
- `handBones` (function, @openav/leap): `handBones(hand)` — The bones to draw for a hand, as pairs of points: each finger's joints in turn, the line across the knuckles, and the forearm.
- `HandGestures` (class, @openav/leap): `new HandGestures(thresholds = THRESHOLDS)` — Turns pinch and grab strengths into clean start and end events, per hand plus a both-hands pinch, using hysteresis so a wobbling value fires once.
- `handsOf` (function, @openav/leap): `handsOf(msg)` — Reads either wire format (raw line or LeapJS v6 frame) into the one hand shape the rest of the package uses; anything else gives `[]`.
- `Hysteresis` (class, @openav/leap): `new Hysteresis(on, off)` — One Schmitt trigger: `update(v)` says `'start'` when the value rises above `on`, and `'end'` only when it falls below `off`.
- `INTERACTION_BOX` (constant, @openav/leap): `INTERACTION_BOX = object, 2 keys` — The classic Leap interaction box, `{ center: [0, 200, 0], size: [235.247, 235.247, 147.751] }` in millimetres, that positions are normalised against.
- `LeapInput` (class, @openav/leap): `new LeapInput({ signals = null, url = DEFAULT_URL, reconnect = true, fingers = true, box = INTERACTION_BOX, thresholds = THRESHOLDS, WebSocket: WS = null } = {})` — Reads Leap Motion hands from the local bridge and publishes them as `leap/*` signals, plus the joints (`leap.hands`) for drawing the hand itself. (before it has a value: For real hands: the bridge must be running (`node packages/leap/bridge/leap-bridge.mjs`, or `--mock` for animated made-up hands) and you must call `connect()`. Nothing is published until the first frame arrives. No sensor and no bridge: feed it hands with `ingest()`, or call `simulate()` to turn the mouse into hands.)
- `leapSignals` (function, @openav/leap): `leapSignals({ fingers = true } = {})` — The list of every signal `LeapInput` publishes, with its range, as `[[name, meta], …]`, ready to hand to `signals.define()`.
- `mockFrame` (function, @openav/leap): `mockFrame(t, id = Math.round(t * 60), { hands = 2 } = {})` — One frame of made-up, animated hands at time `t`: a right hand circling and pinching every 3 seconds, a left hand rising, falling and slowly making a fist.
- `mockHand` (function, @openav/leap): `mockHand({ id = 1, side = 'R', palm = [0, 200, 0], pinch = 0, grab = 0, roll = 0, yaw = 0, pitch = 0, vel = [0, 0, 0], conf = 1, width = 85 } = {})` — Builds one made-up hand, with all five fingers and the arm, from a palm position plus pinch, grab, roll, yaw and pitch.
- `mountLeapPanel` (function, @openav/leap): `mountLeapPanel(el, leap, { width = 300, simulate = true, simTarget } = {})` — Mounts a small panel that shows whether the Leap is alive (bridge, service, device, hands) and draws what it sees, with a button to simulate hands.
- `normalizePoint` (function, @openav/leap): `normalizePoint(p, box = INTERACTION_BOX, clamp = true)` — Maps a point in millimetres to 0..1 inside the interaction box, clamped by default: the same normalisation the `leap/*` signals use.
- `palmBasis` (function, @openav/leap): `palmBasis(direction, normal, left)` — An advanced helper: the orthonormal basis `[x, y, z]` of the palm, from its direction and normal, in the rows LeapJS reads as `hand.r`.
- `PROTOCOL_VERSION` (constant, @openav/leap): `PROTOCOL_VERSION = 6` — The highest LeapJS protocol version we speak: 6. LeapJS 1.1.1 and earlier throw "unrecognized version" above that.
- `protocolOfPath` (function, @openav/leap): `protocolOfPath(pathname)` — Which protocol version a `/vN.json` path asks for, as a number, or `null` when the path is not one.
- `rawToV6` (function, @openav/leap): `rawToV6(raw, tUs, opts)` — One-off conversion of a raw frame to a LeapJS v6 frame, with a fresh converter each time (no history, so no velocities).
- `RESERVED_PORTS` (constant, @openav/leap): `RESERVED_PORTS = array, 1 items` — The ports the Leap bridge refuses to use: `[7457]`, which belongs to The Last Input and the backstage monitor.
- `startBridge` (function, @openav/leap): `startBridge({ port = DEFAULT_PORT, host = '127.0.0.1', mock = false, hz = 60, bin = null, log = () => {} } = {})` — Starts the Leap bridge on this machine: a loopback WebSocket and HTTP server that serves the sensor's hands to every page (Node only). (before it has a value: Node 22 or later, and for real hands the Ultraleap Hand Tracking service plus Xcode's `clang` to build the reader on first start. With `mock: true` neither is needed.)
- `STATUS` (constant, @openav/leap): `STATUS = object, 4 keys` — The four levels of the `leap/status` signal by name: `off` 0, `bridge` 1, `service` 2, `tracking` 3.
- `THRESHOLDS` (constant, @openav/leap): `THRESHOLDS = object, 3 keys` — The default hysteresis levels for the gestures: pinch 0.86 / 0.5, both-hands pinch 0.8 / 0.5, grab 0.8 / 0.5 (start above `on`, end below `off`).
- `V6Converter` (class, @openav/leap): `new V6Converter({ box = INTERACTION_BOX, smoothing = 0.5 } = {})` — Converts raw hand lines into LeapJS v6 frames, keeping the little state the protocol needs: time visible, smoothed positions and fingertip velocities.
- `v6Header` (function, @openav/leap): `v6Header(serviceVersion = 'unknown', version = PROTOCOL_VERSION)` — The first message of a LeapJS v6 connection: `{ serviceVersion, version }`, with `version` held to 1..6 because LeapJS throws above 6.

## pose

- `HandTracker` (class, @openav/pose): `new HandTracker({ signals = null, mirror = true } = {})` — Tracks up to two hands from the camera with 21 landmarks each and publishes palm position and thumb-to-finger pinch distances as `hand/*` signals. (before it has a value: Call `await hands.enable()`: it loads the MediaPipe library from jsDelivr and the hand model from Google's model storage (so it needs the network), asks for the camera (`https` or `localhost`, and the user must allow it) and starts the loop. Until then the signals sit at their starting values.)
- `PoseTracker` (class, @openav/pose): `new PoseTracker({ signals = null, mirror = true } = {})` — Tracks one body from the camera and publishes wrist positions, wrist speed, hand spread, height and lean as `pose/*` signals. (before it has a value: Call `await pose.enable()`: it loads the MediaPipe library from jsDelivr and the model from Google's model storage (so it needs the network), asks the browser for the camera (the page needs `https` or `localhost`, and the user must allow it), and starts the loop. Until then every signal sits at its starting value.)

## chord

- `ChordDetector` (class, @openav/chord): `new ChordDetector({ window = 80, onChord = null, signals = null } = {})` — Groups notes struck close together into one gesture and analyses it: chord type, consonance, triad and cluster flags, published as `chord/*` signals. (before it has a value: Feed it with `noteOn(note, vel)` (and `noteOff(note)`), or let `createShow` do it from `midi/note/on|off`. Nothing is published until `window` milliseconds after the last `noteOn`, so the result is asynchronous. `analyze()` is the exception: it is instant and needs no setup.)

## osc

- `OscOut` (class, @openav/osc): `new OscOut(url = 'http://127.0.0.1:7456')` — Sends OSC messages from the browser to TouchDesigner, Max, Reaper or a spatialiser, batched once per frame, through a small local bridge. (before it has a value: The bridge must be running, and you must `await osc.enable()` first: it probes `GET /health` and answers `false` if nobody is there. Until it succeeds `flush()` just throws the queue away. On a public https page, Chrome asks permission before the page may reach `127.0.0.1`.)
- `DEFAULT_PORT` (constant, @openav/out): `DEFAULT_PORT = 6450` — The out-bridge's default port: 6450.
- `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` (constant, @openav/out): `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 500` — The watchdog time when the config does not say: 500 milliseconds without a value, and a channel is put on its safe value.
- `globToRegExp` (function, @openav/out): `globToRegExp(glob)` — Turns a channel glob like `light/*` into the regular expression the bridge matches channel names with: only `*` is special, and it crosses slashes.
- `loadConfig` (function, @openav/out): `loadConfig(file)` — Reads the out-bridge config from a JSON file and returns it as an object (Node only); throws when the file cannot be read.
- `OUT_DEFAULT_URL` (constant, @openav/out): `OUT_DEFAULT_URL = "ws://127.0.0.1:6450/out"` — The address `OutClient` connects to by default: `ws://127.0.0.1:6450/out`, the out-bridge on this machine.
- `OutClient` (class, @openav/out): `new OutClient({ url = OUT_DEFAULT_URL, id = null, WebSocket: WS, schedule, maxBackoffMs = 5000, minBackoffMs = 250 } = {})` — The page side of the out-bridge: `set(channel, value)` sends a number to a named hardware channel, at most once per frame, and keeps the connection alive. (before it has a value: Call `connect()` (the bridge must be running: `node packages/out/bridge/out-bridge.mjs --config out.json`), or `simulate()` for no hardware at all. `set()` before the socket is open is not lost: it waits in `last` and goes out on open.)
- `RESERVED_PORTS` (constant, @openav/out): `RESERVED_PORTS = array, 1 items` — The ports the out-bridge refuses to use: `[7457]`, which belongs to The Last Input and the backstage monitor.
