- `startBridge` (function, @openav/out): `startBridge({ port = DEFAULT_PORT, host = '127.0.0.1', config = null, watchdog = true, log = () => {}, print = (s) => console.log(s) } = {})` — Starts the out-bridge: a loopback WebSocket server that routes channel values from the page to hardware sinks, with a watchdog that falls back to safe values (Node only). (before it has a value: Node 22 or later. The sinks need what they talk to: a WLED device for `ddp`, the device file for `serial`, a listener for `osc`.)

## mapping

- `LearnWizard` (class, @openav/mapping): `new LearnWizard({ mapper, keys, onChange = null })` — Binds a list of params one after another: it arms learn for the first, you turn a knob, it binds it and arms the next. Skip, back and stop steer it.
- `loadMapUrl` (function, @openav/mapping): `async loadMapUrl(mapper, value, { base = (typeof location !== 'undefined' ? location.href : undefined), fetchImpl = (typeof fetch !== 'undefined' ? fetch : null), timeoutMs = 8000 } = {})` — Fetches a map file from an address (what `?map=` calls) and puts it on the mapper; it never throws and never blocks the show.
- `MAP_FORMAT` (constant, @openav/mapping): `MAP_FORMAT = "openav.map"` — The text `"openav.map"`: the value of `format` in every map file. A file with another format is refused.
- `MAP_MAX_BYTES` (constant, @openav/mapping): `MAP_MAX_BYTES = 262144` — The longest map text `parseMap()` will read: 262144, which is 256 KB. Longer text is refused without being parsed.
- `MAP_VERSION` (constant, @openav/mapping): `MAP_VERSION = 1` — The newest map file version this build reads and writes: 1. A file with a higher version is refused with a message.
- `Mapper` (class, @openav/mapping): `new Mapper({ signals, params, profile = 'default', onChange = null, onLearn = null })` — Connects signals to params: it holds a list of routes (a window, a curve, smoothing) and writes the matching param whenever a signal arrives. (before it has a value: Create the signals and the params first, then the mapper. A smoothed route (`smooth > 0`) writes its param only inside `update(dt)`, so call `mapper.update(dt)` every frame (`createShow()` does).)
- `parseMap` (function, @openav/mapping): `parseMap(input)` — Reads and cleans a map file (JSON text or a parsed value) without touching any mapper; it never throws.
- `parseMapUrl` (function, @openav/mapping): `parseMapUrl(value, base)` — Decides whether a `?map=` address may be fetched: same origin, or an absolute https URL, and nothing else.
- `serializeMap` (function, @openav/mapping): `serializeMap(routes, { world = 'default', now = new Date() } = {})` — Builds the portable map file object from a list of routes: `{ format, version, world, exported, routes }`.

## core

- `Bus` (class, @openav/core): `new Bus()` — A minimal event emitter: `on(event, cb)`, `emit(event, payload)`, `off(event, cb)`. No wildcards, no async.
- `Loop` (class, @openav/core): `new Loop(onFrame, { maxDt = 0.1 } = {})` — The frame clock: calls your function every animation frame with the seconds since the last one, and keeps ticking when the tab is hidden. (before it has a value: Call `start()`: nothing ticks until you do. It needs a browser (`requestAnimationFrame`, `performance`); in Node there is no clock to run it.)
- `Params` (class, @openav/core): `new Params(schema = [])` — The values a world listens to: a list of declared params, each resolved every frame from the timeline, unless a hand, a knob or a route has overridden it.
- `Signals` (class, @openav/core): `new Signals()` — The registry every input writes into and everything else reads from: named values that are either a level (continuous) or an event (pulse).
- `createShow` (function, @openav/show): `async createShow({ world = null, worlds = [], timeline: timelineCfg = { total: 120 }, routes = [], modules = {}, artwork = null, hint = '', profile = null, map = null, onFrame = null, mount = null, telemetry = true, score: scoreCfg = null, } = {})` — Builds a whole show around a world in one call: signals, params, stage, timeline, mapper, the modules you switch on, the console, the backstage feed and the frame loop. (before it has a value: `await` it: it is async because it waits for the world's `init()` (and for lazily loaded modules). It needs a page (`document`, `location`, `localStorage`), and an import map or bundler that resolves every `@openav/*` package it imports (copy the one from `examples/01-hello-particles/index.html`). Browsers start audio only after a click, so sound and the microphone start from the console's buttons.)
- `isStacked` (function, @openav/show): `isStacked(width, height)` — Whether a window of this size gets the stacked layout (stage on top, panel below): upright and no wider than 820 pixels.
- `SHELL_CSS` (constant, @openav/show): `SHELL_CSS = "\n body { margin: 0; background: #000; height: 100vh; display: grid;\n grid…"` — The CSS text `createShow()` puts in the page: the two-column grid, the 340 px side panel, the hint and credit styles, and the stacked layout.
- `STACK_MAX_WIDTH` (constant, @openav/show): `STACK_MAX_WIDTH = 820` — The widest window that can get the stacked layout: 820 pixels (a small tablet held upright).
- `STACK_QUERY` (constant, @openav/show): `STACK_QUERY = "(max-width: 820px) and (orientation: portrait)"` — The media query behind the stacked layout: `(max-width: 820px) and (orientation: portrait)`.
- `STAGE_SHARE` (constant, @openav/show): `STAGE_SHARE = 58` — How much of the window height the stage keeps when the layout is stacked: 58 (percent).
- `stageHeight` (function, @openav/show): `stageHeight(height)` — The stage height in pixels for a window of this height when the layout is stacked: 58% of it, rounded.
- `createCanvas` (function, @openav/stage): `createCanvas(container, { alpha = false } = {})` — Makes a 2D canvas that fills its container and keeps its size in step with it, at up to 2 times the device pixel ratio.
- `Stage` (class, @openav/stage): `new Stage({ container, params, signals, io = {} })` — Runs one world at a time: registers worlds and their params, switches between them, and each frame resolves the params and calls the world's `update` and `render`. (before it has a value: Register your worlds, then `await stage.activate(name)` once; until a world is active, `frame()` returns `null` and does nothing. Then call `stage.frame(dt, baseState)` every frame (a show's loop does).)
- `webtoeWorld` (function, @openav/world-webtoe): `webtoeWorld({ name = 'webtoe', app = 'https://webtoe.openaudiovisual.com/', project = null, params = [], extra = null, } = {})` — Turns a WebToe node patch into a world: the patch runs in an iframe and every changed param is posted into it. (before it has a value: The page must be able to load the WebToe app in an iframe (the network, by default `https://webtoe.openaudiovisual.com/`), and the patch file must be reachable by the app. The world does its work when it is activated, so use it with `createShow({ world })`, or `stage.register()` and `stage.activate()`.)

## remote

- `aliasOf` (function, @openav/relay): `aliasOf(name, alias = 'any')` — The "latest phone" name of a phone signal: `aliasOf('phone/ab12/tilt/x')` is `'phone/any/tilt/x'`. `null` for anything else.
- `attachRelay` (function, @openav/relay): `attachRelay(server, { path = '/relay', log = () => {}, heartbeatMs = 20000 } = {})` — Attaches the room relay to a Node `http.Server`: WebSocket clients that connect to `path` are put in rooms and routed by role. Returns `{ hub, close() }`. (before it has a value: A Node program, imported from `@openav/relay/server` (a different entry point from `@openav/relay`, which is the browser side). Standalone: `node packages/relay/server.js [port]` (default 7458; `/health` answers with the room names; `RELAY_HOST=127.0.0.1` binds to localhost behind a reverse proxy).)
- `bindSignals` (function, @openav/relay): `bindSignals(client, signals, { alias = 'any', meta = signalMeta } = {})` — Connects a runner's `RelayClient` to a `Signals` registry: every signal a phone sends is filed there, plus a `phone/any/…` copy. Returns an undo function.
- `deviceId` (function, @openav/relay): `deviceId(key = 'lab.deviceId')` — The short random id of this browser, kept in `localStorage`, that names this phone in its signals, as in `phone/ab12/tilt/x`.
- `fileSignal` (function, @openav/relay): `fileSignal(signals, name, value, { pulse = false, meta = signalMeta, source = '' } = {})` — Files one incoming signal into a `Signals` registry: declares the name the first time, fills in the velocity, then sets it or pulses it.
- `normalizeValue` (function, @openav/relay): `normalizeValue(name, value)` — Fills in the missing velocity spelling of a note message: `vel` (0..1) or `velocity` (1..127). Every other message passes through unchanged.
- `RelayClient` (class, @openav/relay): `new RelayClient({ role = 'controller', room = 'default', id = deviceId(), url = null, batchHz = 30, resendMs = 1000, onStatus, onSignal, onFeedback, onConfig } = {})` — The browser end of the room relay: sends signals to the other pages in a room and receives theirs, as a phone (controller), the show (runner) or a backstage monitor. (before it has a value: A relay server for it to reach, such as `node serve.js` (it hosts one at `/relay`) or `node packages/relay/server.js`. Until the socket is open, `set()` keeps the latest values and sends them when it opens, but `send()`, `feedback()` and `config()` messages are dropped, not queued.)
- `signalMeta` (function, @openav/relay): `signalMeta(name, { pulse = false } = {})` — What the relay knows about a signal name: its range and unit, or that it is a pulse. Returns `null` for names it does not know.
- `attachTouchPad` (function, @openav/remote): `attachTouchPad(pad, io, { onMove, onEnd } = {})` — Makes an element a multi-touch pad: each finger publishes `touch/x`, `touch/y` and `touch/down` (0..1 inside the element), and `touch/count` says how many are down.
- `localSensors` (function, @openav/remote): `localSensors(signals, { prefix = 'phone/local/', alias = 'any', source = 'local', hooks = {} } = {})` — For a show page that runs on the phone itself: the phone's own sensors go straight into a `Signals` as `phone/local/…`, with a `phone/any/…` copy. (before it has a value: Call `.start()` on the result from a tap (iOS asks for permission only inside a gesture, and only on https pages). Until then nothing is published. See [`PhoneSensors`](#PhoneSensors).)
- `mountJoinCard` (function, @openav/remote): `mountJoinCard(parent, host)` — Puts a small card on the show page with a QR code and the URL a phone should open, and a line that says whether the relay is reachable and how many phones are in.
- `mountRemote` (function, @openav/remote): `mountRemote(root, opts = {})` — The whole phone app in one call: a status bar and the tabs sense, keys, control and MIDI, talking to the relay as a controller. `/packages/remote/` is exactly this. (before it has a value: A page of its own (it takes over the whole screen) and a relay to reach: the same origin's `/relay` unless `relayUrl` or `?relay=` says otherwise. Without a show in the room the header says it is waiting for the work to open.)
- `mountRemoteHost` (function, @openav/remote): `mountRemoteHost({ signals, params, mapper, world = null, room = 'default', auto = {}, surface = null, feedbackHz = 10, url = null, mode = null, controllers = null } = {})` — The show side of the phone remote: joins the relay as the runner, files phone signals, builds the control panel from the params and echoes values back. (before it has a value: A relay for `connect()` to reach: `node serve.js` hosts one at `/relay`, a static site uses the public relay (see `pickRelay()`), or pass `url`. Building the host needs none of that.)
- `PhoneSensors` (class, @openav/remote): `new PhoneSensors(io, hooks = {})` — Turns a phone's tilt, acceleration, rotation, knocks and front-camera light into named signals, in screen axes, and hands them to the `io` you give it. (before it has a value: Call `start()` from a tap or click, not on page load. iOS asks for motion permission only inside a user gesture, and it only gives motion sensors to pages on `https://`; touch and keys work over plain `http://`. `start()` always resolves `true`: look at `denied` for a refusal. If no sensor data arrives within 2.5 s, `hooks.notify` says so (a desktop, or an iPhone page on http). `setCamera(true)` also needs a gesture and HTTPS on iOS.)
- `autoArrange` (function, @openav/surface): `autoArrange(items, cols, fixed = [])` — Packs widgets into a grid first-fit, row by row, and never overlaps; `fixed` placements are kept and block their cells. Returns the placements and the rows used.
- `autoSurface` (function, @openav/surface): `autoSurface(params = [], { perPage = 8, style = 'auto', pairs = [], meters = [], smooth = 0.04, title = '' } = {})` — Turns a world's params into a control panel: a layout, the routes that drive the params, and the bindings for echoing values back.
- `canFullscreen` (function, @openav/surface): `canFullscreen()` — True when the page can ask for fullscreen: the browser has `requestFullscreen` (or the WebKit one). The code treats iPhone Safari as not having it.
- `COLOR_NAMES` (constant, @openav/surface): `COLOR_NAMES = array, 7 items` — The seven colour names a widget's `color` may be: cyan, amber, magenta, lime, violet, coral, white.
- `DEFAULT_SIZE` (constant, @openav/surface): `DEFAULT_SIZE = object, 14 keys` — The natural size of each widget type, in grid cells, as `{ w, h }`: a layout only has to give `x`, `y`, `w`, `h` when it cares.
- `feedbackFor` (function, @openav/surface): `feedbackFor(state, bindings)` — Turns the resolved param state into the normalized values the phone's widgets should show right now: `[{ name, value }]`.
- `gridOrientation` (function, @openav/surface): `gridOrientation(g)` — Says whether a grid `{ cols, rows }` is `'landscape'` (at least as many columns as rows) or `'portrait'`.
- `haptic` (function, @openav/surface): `haptic(ms, enabled = true)` — Vibrates the phone for `ms` milliseconds where the browser can (Android Chrome); silent everywhere else, and `enabled` false turns it off.
- `injectTheme` (function, @openav/surface): `injectTheme()` — Writes the surface's stylesheet into the page, once: the 15 theme variables on `:root` and the rules for every widget. Safe to call again.
- `keepAwake` (function, @openav/surface): `keepAwake()` — Asks the browser to keep the screen on (a screen wake lock) and asks again when the tab comes back. Returns `{ release() }`. (before it has a value: A page that is visible, on `https` or `localhost` (the wake lock only exists on secure pages). `mountRemote()` calls it for you.)
- `lockViewport` (function, @openav/surface): `lockViewport()` — Makes a page behave like an instrument panel instead of a web page: no scrolling, no pinch zoom, no rubber-banding. Returns a function that undoes most of it.
- `normalizeLayout` (function, @openav/surface): `normalizeLayout(raw)` — Returns a copy of a layout with the defaults filled in: ids, titles, grids and the version. The input is not changed.
- `orientationOf` (function, @openav/surface): `orientationOf(w, h)` — Says whether a box is `'landscape'` or `'portrait'` from its width and height; a square counts as landscape.
- `planKeyboard` (function, @openav/surface): `planKeyboard({ width, height, base = 48, minKeyPx = 38, maxWhites = 22, stackBelow = 2.2, forceRows = 0 })` — Decides how many piano keys, in how many rows, fit a box: one wide row, or two stacked rows when the box is tall, so keys stay a playable size.
- `resolvePage` (function, @openav/surface): `resolvePage(page, orientation)` — Works out where every widget of one page goes for one orientation: the grid and a cell for each widget, and which rule produced it.
- `routesFromLayout` (function, @openav/surface): `routesFromLayout(layout, params = [], { smooth = 0.04 } = {})` — Writes the mapper routes for a hand-written layout: every widget that names a param in `target` gets a route from its signal to that param.
- `signalNames` (function, @openav/surface): `signalNames(layout)` — Lists every signal name a layout can publish, so a mapping screen, a doc or a test can show them without touching the panel.
- `signalSink` (function, @openav/surface): `signalSink(signals)` — Makes a `sink` for a `Surface` that writes straight into a `Signals` registry: for a panel on the same page as the show, with no phone and no relay.
- `stretchRows` (function, @openav/surface): `stretchRows(placements, cols)` — Stretches a last row that stops short to the edge of the grid: five faders in four columns leave one lonely fader, and this makes it four columns wide.
- `Surface` (class, @openav/surface): `new Surface(container, { layout, sink, haptics = true, tabs = true, orientation = null, onPage = null } = {})` — A TouchOSC-style control panel: draws the pages and widgets of a layout in a container, and sends each touch out as a named signal. (before it has a value: A browser page (it builds DOM) and a container with a size. The panel injects its look once with [`injectTheme()`](#injectTheme). Nothing else to start: it works on the first touch. On a phone page, [`lockViewport()`](#lockViewport) stops the page from scrolling and zooming under the fingers.)
- `THEME_VARS` (constant, @openav/surface): `THEME_VARS = object, 15 keys` — The look of every control as 15 CSS custom properties on `:root` (`--oav-bg`, `--oav-accent` …): override them to re-skin the whole surface.
- `toggleFullscreen` (function, @openav/surface): `toggleFullscreen()` — Enters fullscreen if the page is not in it, and leaves it if it is. Call it from a tap, because browsers refuse otherwise. (before it has a value: A user gesture: call it from a `click` or `pointerdown` handler. Called on page load it is refused by the browser.)
- `validateLayout` (function, @openav/surface): `validateLayout(layout)` — Checks a layout and returns a list of readable problems; an empty list means it is fine.
- `WIDGET_CLASSES` (constant, @openav/surface): `WIDGET_CLASSES = object, 14 keys` — The widget classes, one per type, that `Surface` builds from a layout: `WIDGET_CLASSES.fader`, `.knob`, `.xy` and so on (advanced).
- `WIDGET_TYPES` (constant, @openav/surface): `WIDGET_TYPES = array, 14 items` — The names of the 14 widget types a layout may use: fader, knob, encoder, button, toggle, xy, bank, radio, pads, keyboard, number, text, label, meter.
- `widgetTypeFor` (function, @openav/surface): `widgetTypeFor(p, { continuousCount = 0, style = 'auto' } = {})` — Picks the widget type for one param declaration: a button for a pulse, a toggle, a radio, a fader or a knob.

## backstage

- `mountConsole` (function, @openav/console): `mountConsole(root, app, opts = {})` — Mounts the director's desk into an element: transport and scrubber, layers overview, inputs, mapping, param sliders, signal meters and a fullscreen performance mode. (before it has a value: Call `desk.render(state)` every frame after `stage.frame()` (a show's loop does): the desk only redraws when you tell it to. `state` is the resolved params, `params.resolve(timeline.state())`.)
- `defaultMonitorUrl` (function, @openav/monitor): `defaultMonitorUrl(loc = globalThis.location)` — Where the backstage relay is unless told otherwise: the page's own host on port 7457 as a `ws://` address, and `null` on an https page or where there is no page.
- `MonitorFeed` (class, @openav/monitor): `new MonitorFeed({ url = defaultMonitorUrl(), hz = 15 } = {})` — Streams snapshots of the running show to the backstage relay over a WebSocket, at most `hz` times a second, and quietly keeps trying when there is no relay. (before it has a value: Call `connect()` once (a show does), then `frame(snapshot)` every frame. `frame()` does nothing while `connected` is false. The relay must be reachable from the page: on an https page the browser blocks `ws://` (mixed content), so give a `wss://` address explicitly.)
- `snapshotOf` (function, @openav/monitor): `snapshotOf({ timeline, params, signals, stage, loop }, state)` — Builds the usual snapshot of a show from its parts: clock, scene, world, frame rate, resolved params, overrides and every signal.

## fab

- `candidateUrls` (function, @openav/fab): `candidateUrls(kind, opts = {})` — The list of URLs [`loadKernel()`](#loadKernel) tries for a kernel, in order: your `urls`, then `window.__LAB__.vendor`, then the unpkg default.
- `checkMesh` (function, @openav/fab): `checkMesh(input, opts = {})` — Measures a triangle mesh for 3D printing: closed or not, volume, mass, overhang, thinnest wall, fit on the bed, with a plain warning for each problem.
- `DEFAULT_URLS` (constant, @openav/fab): `DEFAULT_URLS = object, 2 keys` — Where the CAD kernels are loaded from when nothing else says so: smlibwasm 0.3.0 and manifold-3d 3.5.4, both from unpkg.
- `exportAs` (function, @openav/fab): `async exportAs(x, fmt, opts = {}, kernel = null)` — Exports a shape as STL, OBJ, GLB, STEP or DXF and resolves to `{ bytes, mime, ext, report }`: the same as `fab.export()`, without the `Fab` class.
- `Fab` (class, @openav/fab): `new Fab(opts = {})` — Checks a shape for 3D printing and exports it as STL, OBJ, GLB, STEP or DXF; takes a mesh, a three.js object or a smlibwasm solid. (before it has a value: Nothing for meshes and three.js objects. A smlibwasm `Part` has to be tessellated by the kernel: call `await fab.smlib()` once before the synchronous `check()`, or use `checkAsync()`, `meshOfAsync()` and `export()`, which load it for you. Loading needs a network, or `urls` / `window.__LAB__.vendor` pointing somewhere that has the kernel.)
- `fromMeshLike` (function, @openav/fab): `fromMeshLike(m, scale = 1)` — Turns a mesh-like object (positions and indices under any of the usual names) into a triangle mesh, multiplying the positions by `scale`.
- `fromStlBytes` (function, @openav/fab): `fromStlBytes(bytes)` — Reads a binary STL file back into a triangle mesh: every face has its own three vertices, in 32-bit floats.
- `loadKernel` (function, @openav/fab): `async loadKernel(kind, opts = {})` — Imports a CAD kernel (smlibwasm or manifold-3d) from the first URL that works, and resolves to the ready module. (before it has a value: A network, or `urls` pointing at a place that serves the kernel (the lab uses `window.__LAB__.vendor`), or an `importer` that returns one.)
- `meshOf` (function, @openav/fab): `meshOf(x, opts = {})` — Turns whatever you made into a triangle mesh `{ vertices, triangles, units }`: a mesh, a three.js object, a mesh-like object or a smlibwasm shape.
- `meshOfAsync` (function, @openav/fab): `async meshOfAsync(x, opts = {})` — Like `meshOf()`, but it waits for a `tessellate()` that returns a promise, and can load the smlibwasm kernel to tessellate a solid.
- `MIME` (constant, @openav/fab): `MIME = object, 5 keys` — The media type of each export format: `MIME.stl` is `'model/stl'`, and `obj`, `step`, `dxf` and `glb` the same way.
- `toGlbBytes` (function, @openav/fab): `toGlbBytes(mesh)` — Writes a triangle mesh as a minimal binary glTF (`.glb`): one mesh with welded positions and indices, in millimetres.
- `toObjText` (function, @openav/fab): `toObjText(mesh, name = 'fab')` — Writes a triangle mesh as OBJ text: welded vertices (`v x y z`), then faces (`f a b c`), one object, in millimetres.
- `toStlBytes` (function, @openav/fab): `toStlBytes(mesh)` — Writes a triangle mesh as a binary STL file: 84 + 50 bytes per face, with a normal worked out for every face.
- `weldMesh` (function, @openav/fab): `weldMesh(mesh, tolerance)` — Merges vertices that sit closer together than a tolerance and drops the faces that collapse; returns a new mesh with shared vertices.

## mcp

- `list_controllers` (tool, @openav/mcp): `list_controllers` — Lists every MIDI controller profile that ships with the framework: id, name, maker, kind, control mix, how many controls are unverified, and its page URL.
- `list_examples` (tool, @openav/mcp): `list_examples` — Lists the example works of this checkout: for each one its folder, its page title and the first comment line of its `main.js`. (before it has a value: The server running: `node packages/mcp/server.js`, which Claude Code starts from the `.mcp.json` of the repository (server name `openav`). Other clients need the same `command` and `args` in their MCP settings. An MCP client sends `initialize` once before the first call. Over stdio every message is one line of JSON: the request bodies on this page are spread over several lines to be read, and a client writes them on one line for you.)
- `read_doc` (tool, @openav/mcp): `read_doc` — Returns the text of one framework document: the agent briefing, a handbook chapter or the README, chosen by name.
- `read_profile` (tool, @openav/mcp): `read_profile` — Reads one controller profile in full, plus a readable MIDI map: for each control its type, the exact message, the signal name and whether the number is verified.
- `run_checks` (tool, @openav/mcp): `run_checks` — Runs the framework's whole test suite (`node --test` on every file in `tests/`), the same gate CI uses, and says whether it passed.
- `scaffold_profile` (tool, @openav/mcp): `scaffold_profile` — Generates a valid skeleton profile for a new controller from maker, model and control counts. Every number is an unverified placeholder; nothing is written.
- `scaffold_world` (tool, @openav/mcp): `scaffold_world` — Creates a new numbered example by copying a donor example's files; then the agent edits the World in `main.js`. This tool writes to disk.
- `validate_profile` (tool, @openav/mcp): `validate_profile` — Checks a controller profile with `validateProfile()` and against the shipped ones: same id, same short name, or port patterns that claim the same device.
